The weekly checks out the newest green commit before releasing, and every
later step then ran the release checks from that commit. CI-only PRs never
become "green" (the v3 test workflow does not run on them), so the snapshot
can predate fixes to the checks: the weekly dry run after #6373 still ran
the old evidence script and failed on a deleted PR branch.

Copy master's check-changelog-runs.py and its tests before the snapshot
checkout and run that copy. The release gate and green-commit selection
already run before the checkout; the release script still runs on the
snapshot, which its tag-only mode needs.

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6373 — fix(release): map changelog runs to squash-merge commits in the evidence check

fix(release): map changelog runs to squash-merge commits in the evidence check (#6373)

Auto Changelog runs on pull_request_target, so each run's head_sha is the
PR branch head. PRs are squash-merged and their branches auto-deleted, so
that commit is neither in master's history nor fetchable, and
check-changelog-runs.py failed closed ("Cannot determine whether changelog
run commit ... is in this release"). Any release containing a merged PR
with a deleted branch was blocked, including the scheduled nightly.

- Only unsuccessful runs are looked up; a successful run never blocks.
- A run's commit counts as included when it, or the merge commit of the
  merged PR headed at it, is an ancestor of the release snapshot.
- An unknown commit with no merged PR still fails closed.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
ci(release): look past auto-changelog commits in the green-commit check (#6372)

Every merge to master is followed by an "chore(changelog): auto-add entry"
commit, which runs no CI. The nightly checked only master HEAD, so it
warned "no green required checks; this nightly is unverified" on almost
every run, even when the merged PR passed.

--check now walks back over release-bookkeeping commits (auto-changelog,
version bumps, runtime publishes, [skip ci]) and judges the newest real
change. The weekly scan uses the same list and now skips auto-changelog
commits explicitly.

commit.message:
fix(v3/updater): keep the staged payload owned by the swap helper during restart (#6350)

fix(v3/updater): hand the staging directory to the swap helper

Restart spawns a detached helper that waits for this process to exit
before renaming the staged payload over the installed application, then
returns without retaining any claim on the staging directory. A
DownloadAndInstall arriving during that wait begins with discardStaging,
which removes the very directory the helper is about to install from.

os.RemoveAll is depth-first, and a staged .app bundle is a directory, so
the helper is left holding a path whose contents have been unlinked —
and os.Rename succeeds on a directory whether or not it still holds
anything. The swap reports success and discards the backup, leaving an
empty application with nothing to roll back to.

Restart also accepts a second call while the first helper is pending.
The built-in window starts a Restart per click, so a double click starts
a second helper against the same target.

Restart now reads the staged path, takes the staging directory and marks
a restart as pending in one critical section, and returns
ErrRestartPending if one already is. discardStaging makes the same check
under the same lock, so DownloadAndInstall returns ErrRestartPending
rather than deleting a payload a helper owns; either Restart finds
nothing staged or the download finds the helper's claim. A helper that
fails to start, or never signals readiness, hands ownership back, so a
failed spawn does not strand the payload and block every later attempt.

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): keep uxtheme.dll loaded after resolving ordinals (#6358)

fix(v3/windows): keep uxtheme.dll loaded for dark-mode windows (#6356)

pkg/w32's init resolved uxtheme ordinal functions into package-level
variables and then freed the module. applyDarkMode calls those pointers
later, so the call can jump into unmapped memory and crash the first
window on some Windows builds. Keep the module loaded for the process
lifetime while those pointers are in use.

fix(v3/windows): menu bar painting never panics on an unusable device context (#6342)

* fix(v3/windows): menu bar painting never panics on an unusable device context (#6311)

WM_UAHDRAWMENUITEM drew on UAHMENU.hdc unchecked, and the SetTextColor
wrapper panics on failure, so a DC some Windows builds hand over took the
whole app down while painting the menu bar. The handler now uses a valid DC
(UAHMENU.hdc, else the DRAWITEMSTRUCT's), leaves the item to Windows'
default drawing when neither is usable, and every menu painting path uses a
non-panicking TrySetTextColor. UAHMENUITEM.Position is a C int: as a Go int
it read four bytes of the metrics into the item position on 64-bit.

* fix(v3/windows): contain menubar painting failures and tolerate a CLR_INVALID text colour (#6311)

TrySetTextColor now compares only the low 32 bits of the result and, when the
call returns CLR_INVALID, reads the colour back: a DC whose previous text
colour is CLR_INVALID makes a successful call look like a failure.

MenuBarWndProc now recovers from any panic in the drawing code and leaves a
message with a nil lParam to Windows' default handling, so a painting failure
can never take the app down.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/windows): never call SetBkMode on a DC that rejected the text style, and keep the tests 32-bit safe (#6311)

Adds TrySetBkMode and uses it with TrySetTextColor in every menubar painting
path, skipping the item when either fails. The tests use an all-ones handle
instead of a 64-bit constant so the package still builds for windows/386, and
create their memory DC with the raw call so an unavailable DC skips the test.

fix(v3/dev): avoid Vite readiness probe timeouts (#6305)

fix(v3/dev): use TCP probe for frontend readiness gate (#6209)

The HTTP readiness probe in atterpac/refresh sends no Accept header and
requires exactly 200; Vite answers GET / without Accept with 404, so the
gate always timed out after 60s. The probe lives in the third-party
module, so wails3 dev now injects a TCP readiness check derived from
FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL (host:port, defaulting to 80/443).

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6301 — fix(v3): keep systray menus working when updated while open (#4719)
chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6302 — fix(v3/windows): survive transient WebView2 COM errors in the remaining runtime paths

fix(v3): keep systray menus working when updated while open (#4719) (#6301)

* fix(v3): keep systray menus working when updated while open (#4719)

Updating a systray menu while it was open broke its click handlers.

All platforms: Menu.Clear dropped the cleared items from the global item
map straight away, so a click on a row of the still-open menu logged
"MenuItem #N not found" (the macOS report). A rendered menu now keeps the
cleared IDs until the next Clear or Destroy.

Windows: the tray popup is a separate Win32Menu that Menu.Update never
rebuilt, so tray menus did not change at all after Menu.Update. Update
now rebuilds every tray popup built from that menu. While the popup is
showing, the rebuild waits until it closes, then runs after the clicked
row's WM_COMMAND, so the item the user clicked runs. SetMenu now
rebuilds the popup in place rather than destroying the HMENU that
TrackPopupMenuEx is tracking.

SystemTray.SetMenu after Run now also updates SystemTray.menu, and
OpenMenu reads it on the main thread.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(v3/windows): cover deferred tray popup rebuild; skip refresh without a native app

* fix(v3/darwin): keep IDs of on-screen tray rows through repeated updates

Clear kept only one generation of retired IDs, so a macOS tray menu
updated twice while open released the IDs of the rows still on screen.
The tray now reports menuWillOpen/menuDidClose to Go, and Clear keeps
every retired ID while the menu is displayed.

fix(v3/darwin): make SetRelativePosition relative to the screen work area (#6299)

SetRelativePosition/RelativePosition are documented as relative to the
screen WorkArea, and Windows implements them that way. On macOS both used
the full NSScreen frame, so SetRelativePosition(0, 0) placed the window
under the menu bar (and under a left-side dock), and the same coordinates
landed in different places on macOS and Windows.

Use NSScreen visibleFrame in both windowSetRelativePosition and
windowGetRelativePosition so they keep round-tripping (#5408) and match
Screen.WorkArea on macOS.

Refs #4300

commit.message:
fix(v3/generator): keep bindings stable when encoding/json aliases json/v2

Go 1.27 enables GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 by default, which turns
encoding/json.Marshaler, Unmarshaler and RawMessage into aliases of
encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext types. The generator
followed those aliases, emitting models for encoding/json/v2 and
rendering json.Marshaler as json$0.Marshaler instead of any.

Treat aliases declared in encoding/json whose target lives in an
encoding/json subpackage like the named types they replace, both when
collecting models and when recording imports (including when they are
reached through user alias chains), so output matches Go 1.26.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: run required PR checks for pull requests into releases/**

The branch ruleset that requires "Run Go Tests" and "v3 Build Results"
also covers releases/**, but PR Checks (master) and Build + Test v3
only ran for pull requests into master. On a PR into a release branch
the test jobs were skipped and the always-run gate passed on "skipped",
so untested changes could merge.

Both workflows now trigger for pull requests into releases/** and their
base-branch conditions accept master or any releases/ branch, so the
test jobs and the gate jobs run for those PRs too. The gate job names
are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: test on Go 1.26 and 1.27 and stop silent toolchain downloads

Go 1.25 is out of support. The v2 and v3 test workflows now test every
platform on Go 1.27 and also test Go 1.26 on one Linux runner, so the
oldest supported release is still covered without adding macOS jobs.
In the v3 workflow the GTK3 legacy and server-mode steps run only on
the Go 1.27 Linux job, and the macOS API variants job uses Go 1.27
instead of reading the minimum from v3/go.mod.

The test jobs set GOTOOLCHAIN=local, so a version mismatch fails the
job instead of downloading another toolchain. Template tests use Go
1.27 everywhere, and the remaining workflows pinned to 1.25 move to
1.27.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(v3): build with Go 1.26 and refresh golang.org/x modules

Raise the module's go directive to 1.26.0 with a go1.26.9 toolchain

commit.message:
fix: security hardening for v2 and v3 (#6288)

* Harden the dev IPC server against cross-origin and DNS-rebinding attacks

Gate the wails dev IPC WebSocket behind a per-launch capability cookie and a strict same-origin check, and validate every request's Host against an allowlist (localhost, IP literals, the configured bind address, and WAILS_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS) so a malicious page in the developer's browser cannot reach the bound-method dispatcher.

* Silence the unhandled-key system beep in WailsWindow

* fix(security): update v2 runtime lockfiles for shell-quote, devalue, source-map-js, brace-expansion, vitest

- shell-quote 1.10.0 -> 1.12.0
- devalue 5.8.1 -> 5.9.4
- source-map-js 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2
- brace-expansion 1.1.18 -> 1.1.21
- vitest / @vitest/* 4.1.6 -> 4.1.12 (pulls vite 8.3.4, rolldown 1.2.14)

Lockfile-only; rebuilt runtime bundles are byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v2/cli): warn that remote templates can run build commands

`wails build` and `wails dev` run the frontend:* commands from a
project's wails.json. When a project is created from a remote template,
extend the existing third-party template notice to say that templates
are code, list the frontend commands found in the generated wails.json,
and ask the user to review them before building. The notice is now also
shown with -q.

Document the trust boundary in the v2 CLI reference and community
templates pages, and add a matching note for v3 remote templates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): update v3 runtime lockfile for source-map-js, brace-expansion, markdown-it, js-yaml, vitest

- source-map-js 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2
- brace-expansion 2.1.4 -> 2.1.7 and 5.0.9 -> 5.0.12
- markdown-it 14.2.0 -> 14.3.3
- js-yaml 4.3.1 -> 4.3.2
- vitest / @vitest/* 4.1.0 -> 4.1.12

Lockfile-only; package.json ranges unchanged. Typecheck, tests and
typedoc output are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/updater): use a recognised zip-slip guard when joining archive entries

safeJoin already rejected traversal, but via checks on the filepath.Rel
result that CodeQL's go/zipslip query does not treat as sanitising the
joined path. Guard entry names with filepath.IsLocal and keep a prefix
containment check on the joined target as defence in depth. Add tests
for nested, backslash and absolute traversal in zip and tar.gz, zip
symlink escapes, and symlink write-through.

Resolves code-scanning alerts 224 and 225.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/application): bound runtime window ID header to uint32

The window ID header was parsed with strconv.Atoi and then converted to
uint32, so negative or oversized values wrapped onto another window's
ID. Parse with strconv.ParseUint(..., 32) so out-of-range values are
rejected as an invalid runtime call.

Resolves code-scanning alert 164.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/notifications): do not fall back to PowerShell for Windows toasts

Push Windows toast notifications through the WinRT API only and return
its error instead of engaging go-toast's PowerShell fallback, which
renders the toast XML into a generated script and cannot deliver
activation callbacks.

v2's Windows frontend used toast.Notification.Push, which always enables
the fallback; it now renders the XML with go-toast's template and calls
wintoast.Push without the fallback option.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3): only accept framework control messages from the main frame

On macOS and iOS, WebKit reports whether a script message was posted by
the main frame. Use it to ignore reserved `wails:` messages posted from
child frames. Non-reserved messages are still delivered to
RawMessageHandler with their origin info. Platforms that do not report
frame identity keep their existing behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): update example frontend lockfiles for source-map-js, devalue, nanoid

- source-map-js 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2 (v3 notifications, mobile, ios,
  file-association, dock, dev, custom-protocol-example, android;
  v2 dragdrop-test)
- devalue 5.8.1 -> 5.9.4 (v3 dev)
- nanoid 5.0.8 -> 5.1.16 (v3 file-association) and 3.3.16 -> 3.3.20

Lockfile-only; committed dist bundles are left untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3): validate origin on server-mode runtime requests

In server mode /wails/runtime is reachable from any page open in the
user's browser. Accept only POST requests, and only from the request
host or an origin matching ServerOptions.WebSocketOriginPatterns (or
any origin with WebSocketAllowAllOrigins), mirroring the policy already
applied to the server's WebSocket endpoints. Requests without Origin
whose Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site or same-site are rejected; requests
with neither header (non-browser clients) are still accepted.

The check runs before chunk handling and before the query-string
fallback, and is compiled only into server builds, so webview transports
are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/cli): validate remote template URLs before cloning

Remote template values from `wails3 init -t` were passed to `git clone`
as positional arguments without validation. Validate the URL before any
temporary directory is created, accept only https, http, ssh, git and
scp-like URLs, pass url/dir after `--`, reject option-like tags, and run
the clone with git's protocol allowlist limited to those transports.
Also pass `git remote add` arguments after `--`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/cli): keep URL userinfo when parsing remote template tags

Split the optional tag from a remote template value on the last '@' and
only treat the suffix as a tag when it contains no ':' or '/'. This keeps
scp-like (git@host:path) and ssh://user@host URLs intact while still
supporting url@tag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/cli): allow '/' in remote template tags

Decide whether the text after the last '@' is a tag from the URL part
before it rather than the tag itself, so branch tags such as
release/1.0 keep working while URL userinfo is still preserved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(v2): replace wailsapp/mimetype fork with upstream gabriel-vasile/mimetype

Switch v2's asset MIME detection from the github.com/wailsapp/mimetype
fork (v1.4.1, a 2022 snapshot of upstream) to upstream
github.com/gabriel-vasile/mimetype v1.4.16. The fork's only functional
change, recognising UTF-8 BOM-prefixed HTML, is covered upstream.

Upstream's SVG detector no longer skips a UTF-8 BOM, so strip it before
content detection to keep BOM-prefixed SVG detected as image/svg+xml.
Add extensionless test cases that exercise the content-detection path.

Update the example modules that replace wails/v2 with the local tree and
the stale template go.mod/go.sum snapshots.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(v3): drop stale wailsapp/mimetype entries from project templates

v3 no longer depends on the fork, but generated projects still listed it
as an indirect requirement, which dependency scanners flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: declare least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN permissions

Add explicit top-level contents: read to build-and-test, semgrep,
upload-source-documents and sync-translated-documents. The translation
sync job keeps contents: write and pull-requests: write for
peter-evans/create-pull-request. Semgrep reports to Semgrep Cloud via
SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN, not GitHub SARIF, so it needs no extra scope.

Resolves code-scanning alerts 207, 208, 111, 129, 118 and 115.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: stop running PR code from workflow_dispatch runs

workflow_dispatch runs in the default branch's context, so its cache
scope is the default branch's. changelog-v3 (dispatch checked out
refs/pull/N/head and ran go test/go run on it) and cross-compile-test-v3
(dispatch ran gh pr checkout N, then built and ran the PR's code) both
let PR-controlled code execute with access to that cache scope, where
it could plant entries later restored by trusted workflows.

- changelog-v3: drop the workflow_dispatch trigger and the report job
  that only ran for it; validation still runs on every pull_request,
  which is unprivileged. Re-run the PR check to validate again.
- cross-compile-test-v3: drop the pr_number input and the PR checkout
  step; a manual dispatch now tests the dispatched ref only. PRs are
  still tested on approval via pull_request_review.
- cross-compile-test-v3: add top-level permissions: contents: read.

Resolves code-scanning alerts 236, 234, 180, 186 and 185.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/examples): render XMLHttpRequest event log entries as text

logEvent interpolated messages (request URLs, response data) into
innerHTML, so a response containing markup was rendered as HTML.
Build the entry spans with textContent instead.

Resolves code-scanning alert 195.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v2/runtime): pass dev log message as a console argument

The dev runtime concatenated the message into console.log's format
string, so % sequences in backend-supplied text were interpreted as
format directives. Pass it via %s instead and rebuild ipc_websocket.js
(rebuilding unchanged sources reproduces the committed bundle byte for
byte, so the bundle diff is only this change).

Resolves code-scanning alert 102.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): update website lockfiles for transitive security advisories

Update both website/package-lock.json and website/pnpm-lock.yaml to the
same patched versions, within existing semver ranges:

- shell-quote 1.12.0, proxy-addr 2.0.8, source-map-js 1.2.2
- joi 17.13.8, compression 1.8.2, body-parser 1.20.8, express 4.22.3
- qs 6.16.1, fast-uri 3.1.8, http-cache-semantics 4.3.0
- postcss-selector-parser 7.1.6 (7.x copies only)
- brace-expansion 1.1.21, image-size 2.0.4, js-yaml 3.15.2 / 4.3.2
- svgo 3.3.5, baseline-browser-mapping 2.11.29, browserslist 4.29.3
- colord 2.10.0, postcss 8.5.30, http-proxy-middleware 2.0.10
- axios 1.20.0 (pnpm: @crowdin/crowdin-api-client 1.56.0 -> 1.59.1,
  which pins axios exactly)

Not fixed (patched release is a major bump outside the parent's range,
or no patched release exists): postcss-selector-parser 6.1.4 (cssnano 6
plugins pin ^6; GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf needs 7.1.6), tinypool 1.1.1,
serialize-javascript 6.0.2, uuid 8.3.2, sprintf-js 1.0.3, braces 3.0.3.

package.json is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): update v3 runtime lockfile for nanoid

- nanoid 3.3.16 -> 3.3.20 (GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8), matching #5985

Lockfile-only; npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): update v2 labstack/echo to v4.15.3

Resolves the encoded-slash route bypass advisory for the dev server's
echo dependency in v2 and its example and test modules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: tidy merged v2 changelog sections

* fix(security): override website transitive deps pinned to vulnerable majors

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/application): format runtime window ID without an int conversion

The window ID header is parsed as a 32-bit unsigned value; converting it
to int for logging overflows on 32-bit platforms. Format it as unsigned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/cli): keep URL credentials out of remote validation errors

ValidateRemoteURL, cloneArgs and RemoteAdd echoed the supplied value,
whose userinfo can carry a token. Report only the reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v2/templates): raise template go directives to match wails/v2

The template scaffolds declared go 1.18 and go 1.23.0, below the go 1.25.0
that wails/v2 requires and the go 1.24 that gabriel-vasile/mimetype needs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v2/devserver): scope IPC capability cookie to port and refresh it on reconnect

Browsers do not scope cookies by port, so two `wails dev` instances on
different ports overwrote each other's capability cookie. The cookie name
now carries the bind port taken from the configured dev server address.

After `wails dev` restarts the app a new capability is minted, but the dev
runtime reconnects without reloading the page, so every reconnect was
refused until a manual reload. Add a no-op GET /wails/ipcauth route that
passes through the host guard and cookie middleware, and have the dev
runtime fetch it before each IPC connect attempt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/application): reject rebound Host headers on loopback server binds

When server mode binds a loopback address, a page whose hostname has been
rebound to 127.0.0.1 sends a matching Origin and Host, which passes the
same-origin checks on /wails/runtime and the WebSocket endpoints. Wrap the
server mux in a Host check for loopback binds that accepts only localhost,
IP literals, the bind host, and hosts matching WebSocketOriginPatterns.
Non-loopback binds are unchanged.

Document that WebSocketOriginPatterns targets reverse-proxy deployments and
that cross-origin frontends calling /wails/runtime are not supported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: 0x <0xfbfe7617@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

ci(v3): cut macOS runner demand so PR checks stop queueing for hours (#6290)

PR runs spent most of their wall time waiting for macOS runners (225-400
min queues observed) while actual job time was ~20 min. Each run requested

commit.message:
fix(v3/appimage): start the bundled WebKit helpers on every distro (#6213)

* fix(v3/appimage): start the bundled WebKit helpers on every distro

The bundled WebKit library looks for WebKitWebProcess and
WebKitNetworkProcess in the build machine's absolute directory, so
AppImages built on Debian/Ubuntu only start where that path exists
and crash elsewhere with "Unable to spawn a new child process". The
copied helpers also lost their executable bit in s.COPY.

Patch the helper directory in the deployed library to an AppDir
relative path of the same length, between a deploy-only and a
pack-only linuxdeploy run, and keep file modes in s.COPY. With GTK4
the AppRun wrapper turns off WebKitGTK 6.0's bubblewrap sandbox,
which cannot bind the relative path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/appimage): bundle the GPU process and apply modes to existing files

Bundle WebKitGPUProcess when the host's WebKit ships it: once the
library is relocated, WebKit looks for every helper in the AppDir, so a
GPU process left on the host could no longer start.

s.COPY applies the source's permission bits with Chmod after opening,
so they hold for an existing target as well. The relocation test sets
the fixture's mode explicitly instead of relying on the umask.

The Linux guide no longer suggests DEB or RPM bring the WebKit sandbox
back for GTK3 apps: WebKit2GTK 4.1 leaves it off in every format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/appimage): keep WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox on

Helpers move to usr/lib/<name>, the library names them as ././<name>/, and AppRun starts the app in usr/lib, so the path resolves inside the sandbox too.

* fix(v3/appimage): load the bundled WebKit injected bundle

The injected-bundle path in the WebKit library is still the build
machine's absolute path. On Fedora it does not exist, so every web
process logged "Error loading the injected bundle". On Debian and
Ubuntu it points at the system's bundle, which can come from a
different WebKit build than the one in the AppImage.

AppRun now sets WEBKIT_INJECTED_BUNDLE_PATH, which release builds of
WebKitGTK read, to the bundle shipped in the AppImage. WebKit adds
that directory to the sandbox itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(v3/appimage): skip the file mode check on Windows

Windows has no Unix permission bits, so the library written with 0755
reads back as 0666 there and TestRelocateWebKitHelpers failed on the
windows-latest runner. The rest of the test still runs everywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(v3): report stat error before checking AppImage library mode

Avoid dereferencing a nil FileInfo when os.Stat fails; report the stat
error and the permission mismatch separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(v3/linux): open the asset response pipe with O_CLOEXEC (#6241)

The Linux response writers stream the body to WebKit through a pipe created
with Pipe2(p, 0). Without O_CLOEXEC, any child process forked while a
response is in flight (os/exec, a helper the app spawns) inherits the write
end. The handler returns and closes its copy, but WebKit only sees EOF once
every copy is closed, so the body (and the fetch() behind a binding call)
stalls until that child exits, even though headers arrived on time.

Create the pipe with O_CLOEXEC on both ends. The read end is only consumed
in-process by the GUnixInputStream, so nothing relies on inheriting it.
Applies to both the GTK4 and GTK3 writers.

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(v3/darwin): zoom the page with WKWebView.pageZoom instead of magnification (#6227)

ZoomIn/ZoomOut/ZoomReset/SetZoom/GetZoom on macOS drove
-[WKWebView setMagnification:], a view-level scale: the layout viewport
stays the same, the page is drawn larger and clipped at the window
edges, nothing reflows. Windows (put_ZoomFactor) and Linux
(webkit_web_view_set_zoom_level) implement the same API as a browser
zoom, and so does Safari.

WKWebView.pageZoom (macOS 11+) is that browser zoom; below macOS 11 the
magnification path stays as the fallback. ZoomReset also keeps resetting
the magnification so a pinch zoom (AllowsMagnification) still returns to
actual size.

Fixes #6226

commit.message:
fix(v3/android): apply the "color" field in SetStatusBar (#6193)

application.Mobile.SetStatusBar(json) has always accepted only "style"
(icon light/dark) and "hidden" in its JSON payload on Android — the
"color" key that callers might reasonably expect a status-bar API to
support (matching how the equivalent theme attribute
android:statusBarColor already colors it statically) was never read by
WailsBridge.setStatusBar(), so the status-bar background could only ever
reflect whatever was baked into the app's static theme at Activity
creation, never anything set at runtime.

This is easy to hit for any app that switches between light/dark themes
at runtime from JS rather than following the OS-level day/night setting:
the icon style updates correctly (that part was already wired), but the
background color stays stuck at whatever the static theme resolved to
when the Activity was created, silently mismatching the new icon color —
e.g. light icons on a still-light background, unreadable status-bar text.

Add color handling: parse an optional "color" key ("#RRGGBB" /
"#AARRGGBB") and apply it via Window.setStatusBarColor(), alongside the
existing style/hidden handling. No API surface changes — "color" is a
new optional key in an existing JSON payload, so this is fully backward
compatible with callers that don't send it.

Not applicable to iOS: UIStatusBarStyle has no background-color concept
there (the iOS status bar is always a transparent overlay tinted by
whatever view sits behind it), so this is an Android-only addition and
mobile_features_ios.go is untouched.

Touches:
- v3/internal/commands/build_assets/android/app/src/main/java/com/wails/app/WailsBridge.java
- v3/pkg/application/mobile_features_android.go (doc comment)
- v3/examples/mobile/build/android/app/src/main/java/com/wails/app/WailsBridge.java

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): show the systray label as the tooltip (#6075)

* fix(v3/windows): show the systray label as the tooltip

The docs say SetLabel behaves like SetTooltip on Windows, but the Windows
setLabel was an empty stub and show() only applied the tooltip when the
icon was added, so a label set before Run never reached the icon either.

Route the Windows setLabel through setTooltip, fall back to the label in
show() when no tooltip is set, and store the label and tooltip on the
SystemTray before dispatching to the platform impl so Label() reports
the current value once the tray is running.

Fixes #6045

* fix(v3/windows): keep an explicit systray tooltip over the label

SetTooltip("x") followed by SetLabel("y") showed "y" until Explorer
restarted, when show() put "x" back. Both paths now go through
SystemTray.tooltipOrLabel, so an explicit tooltip always wins and the
label is only the fallback.

SetLabel and SetTooltip also wrote label and tooltip on the caller
goroutine while Label() and the Windows show() read them. Guard the two
fields with a small RWMutex.

* fix(v3/windows): fall back to the label when the systray tooltip is cleared

SetTooltip("") handed the empty string straight to the Windows setTooltip,
which wrote an empty SzTip, so SetLabel("label"); SetTooltip("") left the
hover text blank instead of showing the label.

setTooltip and setLabel now both apply SystemTray.tooltipOrLabel through
one updateTooltip. The value is read when the dispatched call runs rather
than captured at the call site, so the icon always ends up with the latest
stored text whatever order the calls land in.

---------

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

fix(v3/windows): show the systray label as the tooltip (#6075)

* fix(v3/windows): show the systray label as the tooltip

The docs say SetLabel behaves like SetTooltip on Windows, but the Windows
setLabel was an empty stub and show() only applied the tooltip when the
icon was added, so a label set before Run never reached the icon either.

Route the Windows setLabel through setTooltip, fall back to the label in
show() when no tooltip is set, and store the label and tooltip on the
SystemTray before dispatching to the platform impl so Label() reports
the current value once the tray is running.

Fixes #6045

* fix(v3/windows): keep an explicit systray tooltip over the label

SetTooltip("x") followed by SetLabel("y") showed "y" until Explorer
restarted, when show() put "x" back. Both paths now go through
SystemTray.tooltipOrLabel, so an explicit tooltip always wins and the
label is only the fallback.

SetLabel and SetTooltip also wrote label and tooltip on the caller
goroutine while Label() and the Windows show() read them. Guard the two
fields with a small RWMutex.

* fix(v3/windows): fall back to the label when the systray tooltip is cleared

SetTooltip("") handed the empty string straight to the Windows setTooltip,
which wrote an empty SzTip, so SetLabel("label"); SetTooltip("") left the
hover text blank instead of showing the label.

setTooltip and setLabel now both apply SystemTray.tooltipOrLabel through
one updateTooltip. The value is read when the dispatched call runs rather
than captured at the call site, so the icon always ends up with the latest
stored text whatever order the calls land in.

commit.message:
fix(android): wrap runtime-call HTTP fallback errors in JSON envelope (#5858)

The Android HTTP fallback path in serveAssetForAndroid returned raw
plain-text error bodies (from the errs package) for non-200 runtime
calls. The JS runtime JSON.parse()s every runtime response, so an error
surfaced as 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token ... is not valid JSON'
instead of the actual message.

Wrap non-200 runtime-call bodies in the same {"ok":false,"error":...}
envelope used by handleRuntimeCallForAndroid so the frontend can parse
and surface the error.

commit.message:
fix(ios): document required privacy usage-description keys in Info.plist (#5809)

The iOS Info.plist template shipped no NS*UsageDescription keys, yet the
Wails runtime exposes camera, microphone, photo-library, location, motion
and biometric APIs. On iOS, calling any of these without the matching key
is an instant hard crash (and an App Store rejection), with nothing in the
template hinting at the requirement.

Add a commented block listing the six keys that map to the runtime's
permission-gated APIs, so developers uncomment the ones their app uses and
supply a real justification string. Keys are commented (not active) to
avoid shipping usage descriptions for unused features, which draws App
Store review scrutiny.

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>

fix(android): support HTML file inputs via WebChromeClient (#5807)

generated MainActivity set only a WebViewClient and never a

commit.message:
fix(android): default to singleTask launchMode to prevent duplicate A… (#5727)

fix(android): default to singleTask launchMode to prevent duplicate Activity instances

The Android manifest template ships with no explicit launchMode, defaulting
to "standard". This means any incoming intent (deep link, notification tap,
foreground service return) spawns a second MainActivity — a second WebView
and a second attempt to initialise the Go bridge against process-global
state (g_bridge, g_jvm, globalApp).

Set launchMode="singleTask" so there is always exactly one Activity
instance. New intents are delivered via onNewIntent() instead of creating
duplicates. This is the standard approach for single-activity WebView
shells (Capacitor, Cordova, etc.).

Affects the scaffold template and both Android examples.

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(v3): compile server mode for Android and iOS; fix updater regression test (#6278)

* fix(v3): compile server mode for Android and iOS

`go build -tags server` failed for GOOS=android and GOOS=ios. The mobile
platform files carried no !server constraint, so they collided with the
server implementations and called into the GUI bridge that server builds
exclude. Fixes #6271.

Follow the desktop convention: mobile GUI files, their Objective-C
sources and the iOS runtime API now carry !server, and server builds use
the existing message-processor, iOS runtime and desktop logger stubs.
The mobile signal handler files stay selected, as
TestSignalHandlerBuildVariants requires. Mobile server builds are now
pure Go. Desktop and non-server mobile builds select exactly the same
files as before.

Two tests assumed non-server builds without saying so, which hid behind
the compile failure: the Linux window test now matches its source's
constraint and the system-mode test is tagged !server.

CI now cross-compiles server mode for every target on Ubuntu and runs the
application package tests in server mode. The server-build guide lists
supported platforms and what is unavailable on mobile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(updater): isolate #6185 regression test by executable path

#6262 moved download staging from os.TempDir to the directory beside the
target executable so the helper's swap is a same-filesystem rename. The
regression test added in #6259 still isolated itself by pointing TMPDIR at
a temp root, so the staging directory it watches for never appeared there
and the test failed deterministically on every platform and every PR.

Point the test's executable resolver into its isolated root instead, the
same way the other DownloadAndInstall tests do. The test still fails when
the #6259 production fix is reverted.

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): allow multiple folder selection in OpenFile dialogs (#6264)

On Windows, OpenFile() ignored PromptForMultipleSelection() whenever

FOS_ALLOWMULTISELECT together. Add cfd.NewSelectMultipleFoldersDialog and
choose the dialog through openDialogKindFor, which keeps the existing
precedence (directories over files) and adds the multi-folder case.

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows/arm64): pass by-value doubles to WebView2 COM methods (#6165)

* fix(windows/arm64): pass by-value doubles to WebView2 COM methods

#5741 stopped passing a pointer where WebView2 expects a double, and on
windows/arm64 replaced the call with ErrDoubleArgUnsupported, because
syscall.SyscallN cannot load d0 (golang.org/issue/62583). So put_ZoomFactor,
put_RasterizationScale, put_Expires and the print-settings setters were
silently no-ops there: SetZoom does nothing, and a monitor DPI change never
reaches the webview.

The new internal/webview2/pkg/doublecall package owns the call on every
architecture. amd64 and 386 keep the bit-pattern words; arm64 goes through
runtime.cgocall — the system-stack switch SyscallN itself uses, and a
linkname Go keeps for purego — into an assembly trampoline that loads the
integer words into r0-r3 and the double into d0. Both binding packages
(pkg/edge, pkg/webview2) use it; appendDoubleArg, ErrDoubleArgUnsupported
and the ok result of appendRectArg go away.

Refs golang/go#62583

* fix(windows/arm64): keep controller alive across SetBoundsAndZoomFactor and expand changelog

fix(v3/windows/arm64): pass by-value doubles to WebView2 COM methods (#6165)

* fix(windows/arm64): pass by-value doubles to WebView2 COM methods

#5741 stopped passing a pointer where WebView2 expects a double, and on
windows/arm64 replaced the call with ErrDoubleArgUnsupported, because
syscall.SyscallN cannot load d0 (golang.org/issue/62583). So put_ZoomFactor,
put_RasterizationScale, put_Expires and the print-settings setters were
silently no-ops there: SetZoom does nothing, and a monitor DPI change never
reaches the webview.

The new internal/webview2/pkg/doublecall package owns the call on every
architecture. amd64 and 386 keep the bit-pattern words; arm64 goes through
runtime.cgocall — the system-stack switch SyscallN itself uses, and a
linkname Go keeps for purego — into an assembly trampoline that loads the
integer words into r0-r3 and the double into d0. Both binding packages
(pkg/edge, pkg/webview2) use it; appendDoubleArg, ErrDoubleArgUnsupported
and the ok result of appendRectArg go away.

Refs golang/go#62583

commit.message:
fix(darwin): stop posting WindowDidUpdate and WindowWillUpdate (#6171)

NSWindowDidUpdateNotification fires on every run-loop pass (~120/s while
idle) and every window event is forwarded to the page through
evaluateJavaScript:. The WebKit in macOS 27.0 (316338@main) runs each
evaluateJavaScript as a forced user gesture and consumes the page's
transient activation when that gesture ends, so a click's activation is
gone within ~10 ms of mousedown and any activation-gated API called from
the click handler (navigator.clipboard.writeText, WebAuthn, window.open)
rejects with NotAllowedError. WebKit fixed the over-consumption in
321448@main, which has not shipped. Nothing in wails consumes either
event and neither carries data.

Fixes #6170

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6135 — fix(updater/linux): fallback for cross-device EXDEV rename failures

fix(updater/linux): fallback for cross-device EXDEV rename failures (#6135)

* fix(updater/linux): fallback for cross-device EXDEV rename failures

Ports the rename-or-copy fallback from #5560 to Unix: on EXDEV the
helper now copies (files and .app dirs via copyAny) instead of failing
all 20 swap attempts. replaceTarget no longer deletes the target before
a successful move, so a failed swap cannot orphan the install.

Fixes #6134.

* test(updater/linux): cover failed directory swap recovery + docstrings

Addresses CodeRabbit review on #6135: adds an end-to-end test for the
bothDirs path where a non-EXDEV rename failure after RemoveAll must
restore the original bundle via restoreFromBackup and relaunch it
without helper env. Also documents the three remaining new test
functions to clear the 80% docstring coverage threshold.

* fix(updater/linux): stage EXDEV file copies before swapping target

Addresses CodeRabbit Major on #6135: cross-device file copies now land
via a synced temp sibling beside the target and are atomically renamed
into place, so a crash mid-copy leaves the complete old or new file —
never a partial binary. Directories still copy onto the cleared slot
(atomic dir replace is impossible on Unix); surviving-process failures
there stay covered by the outer backup/restore, matching #5560.

* test(updater/linux): deterministic staged-copy failure via injectable seam

Addresses CodeRabbit Minor on #6135: permission-based copy failure
injection (chmod 000) is bypassed by root-capable test runners, so the
staging-failure test could false-pass there. Adds copyFileFunc alongside
renameFunc and injects the failure through it instead.

fix(v3/windows): SetMenu always redraws the menu bar (#6106)

fix(v3/windows): always redraw the menu bar after SetMenu

windowsWebviewWindow.setMenu only called w32.DrawMenuBar inside the
menubar-theme branch, so an application that sets or replaces a menu
at runtime without a theme configured got a menu bar Windows was
never told to redraw.

Move the DrawMenuBar call out of the theme conditional so it runs
after every SetMenu, unconditionally, leaving SetMenuBackground and
InvalidateRect (theme-only concerns) where they were.

Fixes #6103

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): SetMenu(nil) is a no-op, matching macOS (#6105)

fix(v3/windows): treat SetMenu(nil) as a no-op, matching macOS

windowsWebviewWindow.setMenu dereferenced the *Menu argument via
menu.Update() with no nil check. WebviewWindow.SetMenu is a no-op on
macOS when passed nil, so a running application calling SetMenu(nil)
on Windows panicked instead of behaving the same way cross-platform.

Add a guard at the top of setMenu that returns immediately when menu
is nil, and add a regression test that reproduces the pre-fix panic.

Fixes #6104

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): handle WM_CONTEXTMENU so the systray menu opens on right-click (#6162)

* fix(v3/windows): handle WM_CONTEXTMENU so the systray menu opens on right-click

The tray icon is registered with NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4, which delivers a
right-click as WM_CONTEXTMENU rather than WM_RBUTTONUP (NOTIFYICONDATAW
docs: LOWORD(lParam) holds notification events "such as NIN_BALLOONSHOW,
NIN_POPUPOPEN, or WM_CONTEXTMENU"). The callback switch only handled
WM_RBUTTONUP, so rightClickHandler never fired and SetMenu menus were
silently dead on Windows (Linux/macOS use different paths and are fine).

Also fall back to GetCursorPos() in openMenu() when Shell_NotifyIconGetRect
fails or returns nil - that happens while the icon lives in the Windows 11
overflow flyout, and the menu was dropped silently.

* fix(windows): use cursor monitor for systray fallback menu placement

Pick the monitor containing the menu position, not the owner window's,
for the right-edge check in Win32Menu.ShowAt. Also fix
w32.MonitorFromPoint to pass the POINT by value as one argument.

commit.message:
fix(v3): release InvokeSync* callers when the callback panics (#6108)

All five InvokeSync* variants called wg.Done() as the last statement of
the dispatched closure, below `defer handlePanic()`. handlePanic calls
recover() and returns normally, so a panicking callback unwound the
closure cleanly, skipped wg.Done() and left wg.Wait() blocked for the
life of the process — with no crash to point at, because the panic had
been handled.

Deferring the release fixes all five. wg.Done() is deferred first so
that, deferred calls being LIFO, handlePanic still runs to completion
before the caller is let go: a panic handler that draws UI on the main
thread depends on not racing the released caller.

For the variants that assign a result, a callback that panics before its
assignment completes now hands the caller the zero value rather than
never returning at all.

Fixes #6107

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(linux): do not treat opening the tray menu as a click (#6018)

* fix(linux): do not treat opening the tray menu as a click

Right-clicking a tray icon ran the click handler as well as opening the menu,
so an app that shows its window on click had the window toggle on every
right-click — and with an attached window, toggle again on the next one.

The dbusmenu "opened" event says the host is about to show the context menu,
which is the secondary button. ItemIsMenu is published as false, so a primary
click arrives as Activate and is already handled there; the menu-open path only
needs to run the onMenuOpen callback.

* docs: changelog entry

* docs: reference the PR in the changelog entry

* test(linux): cover tray menu-open vs click dispatch

Pins the fix: Event("opened") must run onMenuOpen and not the click
handler, Event("closed") must run onMenuClose and not the click handler,
and Activate — the path a primary click actually arrives on — must still
run it.

* test(linux): assert tray events run only their own callback

Each assertion now pins the whole set of click / onMenuOpen / onMenuClose
counts rather than the one callback it is about, and Activate is checked
against a tray that has the menu callbacks attached, so an event reaching a
callback it should not fails the test.

---------

Co-authored-by: stefan <stefan@znipp.ch>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6184 — fix(v3/windows): keep WebView2 callback handlers alive until native release

fix(v3/windows): keep WebView2 callback handlers alive until native release (#6184)

Go-allocated WebView2 handlers were passed to native code as raw addresses
while their AddRef/Release returned 1 without holding any Go reference. Once a
window dropped an abandoned or replaced Chromium, the GC could free handlers
that WebView2 still referenced, e.g. a controller completion delivered after
the embed timeout.

Handler AddRef/Release now count native references in a registry keyed by the
handler pointer, which keeps the handler and its Chromium reachable until the
final Release. ShuttingDown drops host callbacks so a retained instance does
not also retain its window.

Fixes #6168

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6002 — fix(v3/windows): recover from WebView2 process failures instead of leaving a blank window

fix(v3/windows): recover from WebView2 process failures instead of leaving a blank window (#6002)

* [windows] Recover from WebView2 process failures instead of leaving a blank window

Register CoreWebView2's ProcessFailed event (previously unhandled).
Renderer exited/unresponsive -> re-navigate to the last host-set URL.
Browser process exited -> rebuild the controller on a fresh
edge.Chromium instance and restore the last URL; the old instance
cannot be re-embedded because Embed's init-wait loop keys on a
per-instance flag a used instance has already set.

Without this, any browser-process death (crash, GPU-kill exhaustion,
external kill of msedgewebview2) leaves every controller COM call
failing with ERROR_INVALID_STATE (0x8007139F) and the window
permanently blank until the host app is restarted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/windows): bound WebView2 process-failure recovery and stop it drifting from startup

Adapts the process-failure recovery from #5733 to current master and closes
the gaps that showed up rebasing it off v3.0.0-alpha2.112.

Share one Chromium construction path. The original rebuild carried its own
copy of run()'s construction, which was accurate at alpha2.112 when that was
just NewChromium plus SetErrorCallback. run() has since grown three more
pre-Embed settings, so a rebuilt window silently lost non-client region
support, dropped from composition hosting to windowed while
options.WebView2CompositionHosting stayed true, and lost cursor handling.
newChromium is now the only place that construction lives, so the two paths
cannot drift again.

Restore the last navigation from setupChromium rather than after it.
setupChromium already navigates on its way out, so navigating again from the
rebuild loaded the start URL and immediately threw it away for the real one.
Folding the restore into that existing branch also fixes an options.HTML
window recovering into a window that is never shown: the NavigateToString
branch left webviewNavigationCompleted set from the dead controller's last
navigation, and navigationCompleted uses that flag to skip the Hide/Show
visibility hack — so recovery completed onto exactly the blank window it
exists to prevent.

Bound the attempts. A rebuilt controller that dies again re-enters the same
handler, so an unrecoverable runtime turned recovery into a hot loop spawning
WebView2 processes. Recovery now gets maxWebviewRecoveryAttempts consecutive
tries, reset by any completed navigation, so a working recovery costs nothing
and a broken one degrades to the pre-existing blank window instead of looping.
RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE re-fires for as long as the renderer stays hung,
so the bound covers re-navigation too.

Guard the rebuild against teardown, since shutting the app down kills the
WebView2 processes and a failure racing destroy would otherwise embed into a
window that is going away.

The failure-kind policy and the attempt budget are split into
webviewRecoveryActionFor and beginWebviewRecovery, which touch no COM and are
covered by unit tests. The rest of the path needs a live WebView2 runtime; the
manual matrix is in the pull request.

Refs #5733, #5705

Co-authored-by: rmurphy <rmurphy@fortressinfosec.com>
Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Signed-off-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>

* test(v3/windows): match the build tag of the file under test

webview_window_windows.go is `windows && !server`, so tagging its test plain
`windows` broke `go test -tags server` for the package: the test file compiled
without any of the declarations it references.

Note that dialogs_windows_internal_test.go has the same mismatch and already
breaks that build on master; left alone here as unrelated.

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Signed-off-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>

* fix(v3/windows): only reset the recovery budget on a successful navigation

A dead render process leaves WebView2 on an error page, and that error page
fires NavigationCompleted like any other load. Resetting the attempt budget
there handed a crash-looping renderer a fresh budget every cycle, so the bound
never tripped — reintroducing exactly the runaway it was added to stop.

Gate the reset on ICoreWebView2NavigationCompletedEventArgs::IsSuccess, whose
vtbl slot was already declared but had no accessor; add one following the
existing BOOL out-param pattern. An unreadable IsSuccess counts as
unsuccessful, since assuming success is the failure mode that loops.

Also guard the renderer re-navigation against teardown. rebuildWebView already
bails when the window is being destroyed; the deferred Navigate had the same
race and no guard.

Both found by CodeRabbit on the pull request.

Co-authored-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>
Signed-off-by: taliesin-ai <bot@taliesin.ai>

* fix(v3/windows): run the process-failure restore after the ProcessFailed handler returns

InvokeAsync runs its function inline when the caller is already on the
main thread, and the ProcessFailed callback always is: WebView2 delivers
it through the message loop. The recovery restore therefore ran inside
the event handler, where WebView2 never delivers a new controller's
creation callback — a browser-process kill made Embed pump for 30
seconds inside the handler and then exit the process via errorCallback.
The WebView2 ProcessFailed documentation requires scheduling the work
"to take place after completion of the event handler".

Hopping off the main thread first forces dispatchOnMainThread to post,
so the handler returns before the restore runs.

Validated on Windows 11 26200 / WebView2 151.0.4129.93: repeated
browser-process kills recovered 0/8 inline and 8/8 posted (with the
message-wait fix in the next commit), ~0.5s per recovery.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/windows): wake the embed wait for input already in the queue

pumpUntilInited waited with MsgWaitForMultipleObjects, which only wakes
for input that arrives after the wait is entered. A message posted
between the drain loop and the next wait was therefore invisible until
some later message happened to arrive, and the controller-creation
completion could sleep out the whole 30s deadline. Two live symptoms:

- A WebView2CompositionHosting window fails at plain startup,
  deterministically, since the wait/deadline rework: bisects to
  8e08788b3 (#5952); the parent commit and v3.0.0-beta.4 both start
  fine on the same machine.
- WebView2 process-failure recovery (#6002): even with the restore
  correctly posted out of the ProcessFailed handler, rebuilds wedged in
  1 of 6 browser-kill trials on the busy post-crash queue.

MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx with MWMO_INPUTAVAILABLE also returns when
matching input is already available. With it, composition-hosted
startup works again and posted rebuilds recover 8/8.

Validated on Windows 11 26200 / WebView2 151.0.4129.93.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/windows): release the abandoned instance's DComp target before a controller rebuild

An HWND can carry only one DirectComposition target. After a
browser-process exit the abandoned Chromium's DComp target is still
bound to the window, so the replacement's composition setup fails with
DCOMPOSITION_ERROR_WINDOW_ALREADY_COMPOSED and falls back to windowed
hosting: a WebView2CompositionHosting window recovered with the wrong
hosting mode, visible only as one log line and a changed child-window
tree (Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND and Intermediate D3D Window appear).

Releasing the old composition controller and host before creating the
replacement keeps the recovered window composition-hosted; the
post-recovery child-window set matches the pre-failure one.

Validated on Windows 11 26200 / WebView2 151.0.4129.93.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v3/windows): contain failures during WebView2 recovery

Return controller initialization errors during recovery, clean up partial controllers, ignore late callbacks, and preserve quit messages. Recover HTML renderer failures and prevent overlapping recovery attempts. Keep initial startup failures fatal.

Co-authored-by: rmurphy <rmurphy@fortressinfosec.com>

* fix(v3/windows): address WebView2 recovery review findings

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

fix(security): address multiple security vulnerabilities (#4895)

* fix(security): address multiple security vulnerabilities

This commit bundles fixes for several security issues identified by
GitHub Advanced Security and Semgrep code scanning.

## Workflow Permissions (CodeQL)
- Add explicit permissions blocks to GitHub Actions workflows
- Restrict GITHUB_TOKEN to minimum required permissions
- Affected files: automated-releases.yml, build-and-test-v3.yml,
  publish-npm.yml, test-simple.yml

## Path Traversal (CodeQL)
- Fix directory traversal vulnerability in screen example
- Add path validation using filepath.Clean and containment checks
- Affected file: v3/examples/screen/main.go

## Rollup XSS Vulnerability (Semgrep)
- Update rollup from 3.28.0 to 3.29.5
- Fixes CVE-2024-47068 (Cross-site Scripting)
- Affected file: v3/examples/dev/frontend/package-lock.json

Note: The setup wizard command injection alert was reviewed and determined
to be a false positive - commands originate from backend package manager
detection, not user input. Added clarifying documentation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): add command whitelist to prevent command injection bypass

This commit addresses a critical security issue identified by CodeRabbit
where the sudo flag-skipping logic could be bypassed to execute arbitrary
commands (e.g., "sudo -u apt bash -c malicious_command").

Changes:
- Add allowedCommands whitelist for package managers
- Add allowedSudoCommands whitelist for commands after sudo/pkexec/doas
- Implement isCommandAllowed() with secure validation that rejects
  any sudo invocation with flags before the command
- Add comprehensive test cases including bypass attack scenarios

The fix follows CodeRabbit's recommendation to not attempt parsing
sudo flags, instead requiring the package manager to immediately
follow the privilege escalation command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): add nosec comments for validated path usage

Add #nosec G304 directives to suppress false positive warnings from
gosec/CodeQL on the path traversal fix. The path is validated to be
within assetsDir before use via strings.HasPrefix check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): improve command injection protection for CodeQL

- Refactor whitelist validation to use getSafeCommand() which returns
  safe command names from a static lookup table instead of user input
- This allows CodeQL to trace that executed commands come from a
  known-safe whitelist rather than tainted user input
- Add comprehensive tests for the new getSafeCommand function
- Add lgtm[go/path-injection] comments for CodeQL suppression on the
  example file where paths are properly validated

ubuntu-latest runner image no longer includes libwayland-server.so.0,

stale apt cache.

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5973 — fix(v3/linux): claim the single instance name under the app's own id

fix(v3/linux): claim the single instance name under the app's own id

linuxLock.acquire mangled UniqueID into an org.wails_app_*.SingleInstance name
unrelated to the application id. A flatpak may only own names prefixed with its
app id, so a sandboxed app could not claim it without being granted unfiltered
--socket=session-bus, which is access to the entire session bus in order to
obtain one well-known name.

The mangling existed because one string served as bus name, interface name and
object path, and D-Bus spells those differently: bus names may contain hyphens,
interface names may not, and object paths separate elements with / and allow
neither. Derive the three separately so the bus name can keep UniqueID verbatim,
as its documented convention (com.myapp.myapplication) already suggests.

Also report a refused name instead of swallowing it. RequestName errors were
returned bare and unexpected replies were treated as success, so a sandbox
refusal could reach the caller as alreadyRunningError -- notifying a first
instance that does not exist and exiting silently at startup.

chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6112 — fix(v3/windows): free the replaced menu, redraw the bar, and ignore a nil menu

fix(v3/windows): free the replaced menu, redraw the bar, and ignore a nil menu (#6112)

* fix(v3/windows): free the replaced menu, redraw the bar, and ignore a nil menu

Three defects in windowsWebviewWindow.setMenu, each with a test that fails
without its fix.

**#6102** - the menu being replaced was dropped without freeing anything it
owned: its HMENU, the HBITMAPs allocated while building it, and the submenu
handles detached for hidden rows. Win32Menu.Update does free those, but only
for the same object, and setMenu builds a new one - so nothing ever freed the
old. Two ordering constraints matter and neither is obvious. The runtime
bitmaps have to be taken off the item impls before the replacement is built,
because building reassigns item.impl and puts them beyond the mapping walk
that would free them; and the outgoing menu has to be destroyed after
SetMenu, not before, because destroying one still assigned to a window
leaves the window pointing at a freed handle.

**#6103** - DrawMenuBar was only called inside the `if w.menubarTheme != nil`
branch, so an application setting a menu at runtime without a menubar theme
never told Windows the bar had changed. It now runs after every SetMenu.

**#6104** - setMenu dereferenced its argument with no nil check, so
SetMenu(nil) panicked on Windows while doing nothing on macOS. Same public
call, same argument, different outcome. It now returns, matching macOS.

w32.IsMenu is added because without it a freed handle cannot be
distinguished from a dropped one, which is what made the leak assertable and
is plausibly why it survived this long.

Found while sharing the Windows menu implementation with a second frontend:
writing the same logic a second time, with different questions in mind,
surfaced what reviewing it had not.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WP7MWnMpQDT2WB7CPLWbqr

* fix(v3/windows): preserve menu state when SetMenu fails

commit.message:
fix(v3/webview2): remove the native WebView2 loader and its embeds (#6031)

native_module_{386,amd64,arm64}.go embedded x86/, x64/ and arm64/
WebView2Loader.dll, but the root .gitignore *.dll rule kept those binaries
out of every commit and therefore out of every published module zip. Because
go mod vendor resolves embed patterns for all build configurations, ignoring
GOOS, GOARCH and build tags, vendoring failed for every consumer on every OS,
not just Windows builds.

The native loader is the old path that loaded Microsoft's bootstrap DLL from
memory via go-winloader. The pure Go loader has superseded it, so rather than
ship the missing binaries, remove the native path entirely: delete
native_module*.go and edge/create_env_native.go, drop the
native_webview2loader build tag from the files that were gated against it,
and drop the now-unused github.com/jchv/go-winloader dependency.

Nothing referenced the embeds outside the tag, so default builds are
unaffected. Passing -tags native_webview2loader still builds; the tag is now
simply inert.

Fixes #5782
Fixes #5376

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6029 — fix(v3): prompt for the notarization password in a new terminal window

fix(v3): prompt for the notarization password in a new terminal window (#6029)

* fix(v3): prompt for the notarization password in a new terminal window

`wails3 setup` ran `xcrun notarytool store-credentials` with
`--password-stdin`, which notarytool does not accept, so the signing page
always failed with "Unknown option '--password-stdin'".

The only alternative flag, `--password`, would put the app-specific
password in the process arguments where `ps` can read it. notarytool
prompts securely when the password is omitted, so the wizard now spawns a
Terminal window of its own and lets notarytool prompt there. The window
opens in front of the browser, prints the exact command it is about to
run, and writes notarytool's exit code out when it is done; the wizard
watches for that and the browser page updates itself, so nobody has to go
looking for the terminal `wails3 setup` was started from.

The password no longer touches the browser, the wizard's HTTP API or any
command line.

Based on #6022 by @acheong08.

Co-authored-by: acheong08 <36258159+acheong08@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0184PYtYte172MGWuNWvh3XQ

* test(v3): skip the notarization script tests where there is no POSIX sh

The generated script is /bin/sh and only ever runs on macOS, but the Go
test matrix includes windows-latest, where it would be at the mercy of

fix(v3): name Control-letter key presses correctly on macOS (#6032)

* fix(v3): name Control-letter key presses correctly on macOS

Pressing Control-A ran the binding registered for Control-Home, and no
Control-A binding could ever fire. Seven other combinations behaved the
same way:

    ctrl+a -> ctrl+home        ctrl+l -> ctrl+clear
    ctrl+d -> ctrl+end         ctrl+m -> ctrl+enter
    ctrl+h -> ctrl+backspace   ctrl+n -> ctrl+page up
    ctrl+k -> ctrl+page down   ctrl+[ -> ctrl+escape

AppKit reports a press three ways: a virtual key code, the modifiers held,
and the characters produced. Only the key code identifies the physical key.
The characters depend on what else is held, and with Control held macOS
collapses letters to their control codes, so Control-A produces U+0001 -
which keyStringFromEvent read as Home, because it consulted the characters
before the key code.

Five of those character comparisons could never have matched the key they
named. The real Home key produces NSHomeFunctionKey, not U+0001, and the
Delete key produces U+007F, not U+0008, so the tests for U+0001, U+0004,
U+000B, U+000C, U+000E and U+0008 only ever matched a Control-letter press.
Home, End, Page Up, Page Down and Return had no key code of their own here,
which is why the characters were being consulted at all; they have one now.

The naming has moved from Objective-C into Go so that it can be tested
without standing up AppKit - the accompanying table test fails on every one
of the eight combinations above when the old order is restored. The
Objective-C side now reads the key code, the modifiers and the first
character off the NSEvent and asks Go for the name, so all four existing
callers are unchanged. The first character is passed rather than the string
because Control-Space produces a NUL, which as a C string is
indistinguishable from no character at all.

Two smaller things came out of the test that every name emitted must be one
parseAccelerator accepts. "forward delete" was emitted but not accepted, so
every press of that key was reported as an error and it could not be bound;
it is now a known name. "clear" was accepted nowhere and only reachable
through Control-L, so it is gone.

Confirmed against a test application registering ctrl+a, ctrl+b and
ctrl+home: before, pressing Control-A fired the ctrl+home binding; after, it
fires ctrl+a, and Control-B is unaffected either way.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WP7MWnMpQDT2WB7CPLWbqr

* fix(v3): name only presses that can actually be bound, on macOS

Addresses both review comments on #6032, each confirmed with a test that
fails against the previous code first.

A press with no name was still named after its modifiers alone, producing
strings like "cmd" that no binding can match and that parseAccelerator
rejects outright - so each one was reported as an error rather than
ignored. The name is now empty in that case, and -keyDown: does not send an
empty name on, which would only have moved the error rather than removed
it. -performKeyEquivalent: already declined to.

F21 to F35 and the keypad's Clear key had no name at all. namedKeys accepts
f21 through f35 and numlock, so bindings can be written for them, but
nothing on macOS ever produced those names: the keys exist only on extended
keyboards, where AppKit reports them through characters rather than through
a key code this build knows. They are named from their characters now -
NSF21FunctionKey and consecutive, and NSClearLineFunctionKey for numlock.

Neither was introduced by this pull request; both were carried over from
the Objective-C the branch replaced.

Also verified against a running application: bindings still fire, and no
accelerator now fails to parse.

chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #6026 — fix(v3): keep serving main thread work on macOS while a modal loop runs

fix(v3): keep serving main thread work on macOS while a modal loop runs (#6026)

* fix(v3): keep serving main thread work on macOS while a modal loop runs

dispatchOnMainThread posted its callback to the main dispatch queue. AppKit
drains that queue and does not re-enter, so when a callback went on to show a
modal dialog or open a menu - AppKit calls which do not return until they are
dismissed, turning a nested run loop instead - every callback queued behind it
waited that long too. InvokeSync and InvokeAsync are how all window, menu and
runtime work reaches the main thread, so an open menu or a parentless dialog
stalled the lot of it.

The run loop keeps turning throughout, so schedule the callback on the run loop
instead and it is delivered in the nested loop as well, leaving the queue free.

The test fails against the current dispatch and passes with this change. Two
things are needed to make it reproduce, both found by measuring: it has to drive
the main run loop, so TestMain runs the suite on its own goroutine and turns the
loop on the main thread; and AppKit has to be loaded, because until it is, the
main queue is drained by CFRunLoop, which re-enters and delivers the callback
whether or not the bug is present. If AppKit cannot start, the test skips rather
than reporting a false green.

Windows already avoids this class of bug deliberately - see the comment in
mainthread_windows.go about modal inner loops and wails/issues/969 - and Linux
dispatches through g_idle_add, which nested GTK loops keep draining. macOS was
the one platform left.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WP7MWnMpQDT2WB7CPLWbqr

* test(v3): address review of the macOS dispatch test

Each point was reproduced as a failing test before being fixed.

The harness set its running state inside Run, so a Stop which landed first was
overwritten and the loop never ended - TestMain would block forever if the suite
finished before the main thread reached the loop. Reproduced by calling Stop
then Run: the loop was still turning three seconds later. A loop is now created
in the running state and the flag is read and written with C11 atomics, so a
Stop can never be lost. TestLoopHonoursStopBeforeRun keeps it that way.

The delivery timeout disagreed with the assertion it guarded: a callback
arriving 1.7s into a 2s nested loop ran while the loop was going, which is what
the test is meant to accept, yet the 1.5s timeout rejected it. Reproduced with a
deliberately late delivery. There is now a single budget, used both as the
timeout and as the assertion, so the two cannot disagree - and it is what we
actually want to assert, since a working dispatch delivers in under a
millisecond and a starved one takes the whole nested loop.

The cgo helpers were in a normal source file, so they were compiled into the
shipped package. They now live in an internal package which only the tests
import, keeping cgo out of _test.go where the go tool forbids it and out of the
application package where it does not belong.
TestNoTestOnlyHelpersInShippedFiles keeps it out.

The regression test still fails without the dispatch fix and passes with it.

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5923 — fix(mobile): make secure storage fallible and fail-closed

fix(mobile): make secure storage fallible and fail-closed (#5923)

* fix(mobile): make secure storage fallible and fail-closed

BREAKING CHANGE: SecureSet, SecureGet, and SecureDelete now return errors.

SecureSet(key, value string) error
SecureGet(key string) (value string, found bool, err error)
SecureDelete(key string) error

iOS:
- Use SecItemUpdate before falling back to SecItemAdd (non-destructive)
- Check and propagate all OSStatus values
- Distinguish missing key (found=false) from empty value (found=true)

Android:
- Remove plaintext fallback (wails_secure_plain eliminated)
- Require API 23+ for EncryptedSharedPreferences; return error below
- Use commit() instead of apply() for durable writes
- Use contains() to distinguish missing from empty
- Return structured JSON envelope across JNI bridge

Desktop stub returns ErrSecureStorageUnsupported for all three methods.

Empty key is rejected at the Go layer before crossing any bridge.
Delete of a non-existent key succeeds on both platforms.

Closes #5913 (partially — secure storage portion of the mobile hardening audit)

* fix(android): cache securePrefs and use JSONObject for error envelopes

Address CodeRabbit review feedback:
- Cache EncryptedSharedPreferences instance after first initialization
- Add secureError() helper using JSONObject to safely handle null
  getMessage() and avoid JSON injection from special characters
- Replace manual string concatenation in all catch blocks

commit.message:
chore(v3): remove precompiled example binaries (#6025)

Two macOS arm64 build artifacts are tracked under v3/examples:

  17 MB  v3/examples/menu/menu_demo
  15 MB  v3/examples/server/server

Nothing references either file. Both examples build from source, so the
binaries only cost people bandwidth: menu_demo sits inside the main
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 module and is downloaded by every `go get`
of v3, and server/ is a nested module, so its binary is carried by every
clone of the repository instead.

.gitignore already lists the per-example binaries for six other
examples. It missed these two because the names don't match the pattern
the others follow: a bare `go build .` in examples/server produces
`server`, which had no entry at all, and the menu binary was built as
`menu_demo` rather than the `menu` that is ignored. Add both names so
they don't come back.

Fixes #5927.

commit.message:
fix(application): let registered accelerators win over the webview on… (#5902)

fix(application): let registered accelerators win over the webview on macOS

On macOS the WKWebView is first responder and swallows most key events
before they reach NSWindow's keyDown:. Common combos like Ctrl+Tab never get
there, so an app-registered KeyBinding for them silently never fires.

Override performKeyEquivalent: on WebviewWindow, which runs before the
responder chain and before NSMenu's own key-equivalent dispatch. It calls
into Go with the same accelerator string keyDown: builds, looks it up via
the existing processKeyBinding path, and returns YES only on a real match.
On a miss it falls through to super, so main-menu key equivalents and every
other Cocoa default keep working — only accelerators the app explicitly
registered are claimed.

The Go side is a synchronous sibling of processWindowKeyDownEvent rather
than a channel send, because performKeyEquivalent: needs the answer
immediately to decide whether to consume the event. It's a single map read
under RLock plus the same goroutine dispatch processKeyBinding already does,

fix(application): let registered accelerators win over the webview on… (#5902)

fix(application): let registered accelerators win over the webview on macOS

On macOS the WKWebView is first responder and swallows most key events
before they reach NSWindow's keyDown:. Common combos like Ctrl+Tab never get
there, so an app-registered KeyBinding for them silently never fires.

Override performKeyEquivalent: on WebviewWindow, which runs before the
responder chain and before NSMenu's own key-equivalent dispatch. It calls
into Go with the same accelerator string keyDown: builds, looks it up via
the existing processKeyBinding path, and returns YES only on a real match.
On a miss it falls through to super, so main-menu key equivalents and every
other Cocoa default keep working — only accelerators the app explicitly
registered are claimed.

The Go side is a synchronous sibling of processWindowKeyDownEvent rather
than a channel send, because performKeyEquivalent: needs the answer
immediately to decide whether to consume the event. It's a single map read
under RLock plus the same goroutine dispatch processKeyBinding already does,
so the threading matches the keyDown: path. The modifier-string assembly is
pulled out of keyDown: into acceleratorStringFromEvent: so both callers
produce identical strings.

fix(v3/linux): don't make GTK4 applications unique (#5971)

* fix(v3/linux): don't make GTK4 applications unique

appNew built the GtkApplication with G_APPLICATION_DEFAULT_FLAGS, so the
application was unique. GTK derives the bus name from the application id, and a
second launch that finds it owned registers as a remote instance: activate is
forwarded to the primary and never emitted locally. waitForActivation blocks on
that signal before any window is created, so the process comes fully up and then
hangs with nothing on screen and nothing logged.

instance behaviour to SingleInstanceOptions.
