commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5333 — feat(v3:notifications): add sounds, attachments, and more

feat(v3:notifications): add sounds, attachments, and more (#5333)

* refactor(v3/notifications/windows): build toast XML directly via wintoast

Drop the dependency on the high-level go-toast/v2 builder package
(git.sr.ht/~jackmordaunt/go-toast/v2) in favour of constructing the
toast XML ourselves with encoding/xml and pushing it through the
already-used wintoast subpackage.

The wintoast subpackage exposes SetAppData, SetActivationCallback, and
Push as public API, so no further linkname shims were needed beyond the
existing registerFactoryInternal / wintoast.ClassFactory wiring at
service Startup (kept so cold-start clicks on toasts pinned in Action
Center from a previous run still dispatch to OnNotificationResponse).

Behaviour-preserving change. The encoded base64 payload that round-trips
NotificationOptions through every <action arguments="..."> attribute
and the toast's launch="..." attribute is unchanged, as is the
<input id="userText"> channel for reply text. Actions, categories, and
ActivationType=foreground all match the previous template output.

Net effect: encoding/xml now handles attribute escaping (a small
robustness win for titles/bodies containing < > & or quotes), and the
Windows backend is positioned to wire the new sound, image, threading,
scenario, schedule, and tag-based update fields directly into XML in a
follow-up commit without relying on the upstream go-toast struct
exposing those fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(v3/notifications/darwin): pass NotificationOptions as JSON across the cgo boundary

The send-notification C entry points used to take five separate
const-char* parameters (identifier, title, subtitle, body, data_json).
Replace them with a single options_json blob produced by json.Marshal of
the whole NotificationOptions struct, parsed in Objective-C with
NSJSONSerialization.

Behaviour-preserving change: title/subtitle/body/userInfo are still
populated identically, the default sound is still applied, and the
identifier/categoryId still flow through to UNNotificationRequest. New
helper functions parseOptions and stringOrEmpty in the .m provide safe
typed access; createNotificationContentFromOptions replaces the previous
per-arg createNotificationContent.

Net effect: future fields (sound, attachments, threadId,
interruptionLevel, schedule) can be wired in by reading additional keys
from the same dict in createNotificationContentFromOptions and the
follow-up trigger path, without growing C signatures or adding more
C.CString churn on the Go side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(v3/notifications): add Sound, Attachments, ThreadID, InterruptionLevel, Schedule, and UpdateNotification

Extend NotificationOptions with five additive fields plus a new
UpdateNotification method on NotificationService. Each new field
gracefully degrades on platforms with limited backend support; see the
package godoc for the per-platform support matrix.

Sound: nil = platform default, {silent: true} = no sound,

  validation paths: non-accessible file, relative path, relative
  file:// URL, and oracle-free error messages.

* chore: drop UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md edit (auto-generated on merge)

The v3 changelog is generated automatically from PR titles by the nightly
release workflow, so hand-edited entries here only cause merge conflicts.
Removing this PR's entry to keep it cleanly mergeable.

* docs(notifications): explain how to attach a bundled asset

Answers the review question about how a caller obtains the absolute path
for an attachment shipped with the app: for a go:embed'd asset there is no
fixed on-disk path, so materialise it to a writable dir at startup and pass
that path. Notes that a user/downloaded file can be passed directly, and
that an in-memory bytes API may come later.

commit.message:
ci(docs): pin docs build to Node 22.12.0 for Astro 6.4+ (#5696)

Astro 6.4 dropped Node 20 support (engines.node '>=22.12.0'), so the
Cloudflare Pages 'wails-v3-site' docs build fails once astro resolves to
6.4.x. Pin the docs build root to Node 22.12.0 so it (and future astro
bumps, e.g. #5641) build cleanly.

commit.message:
ci: add release-v3.yml workflow for signed v3 binary releases (#5318)

* ci: add release-v3.yml workflow for signed v3 binary releases

Builds wails3 CLI for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64,
darwin/arm64, and a darwin universal binary on tag push matching
v3.*. macOS binaries are signed with Developer ID and notarized
via xcrun notarytool. All binaries are attached to the GitHub
Release created for the tag.

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5249 — fix(windows): prevent Center() from stealing focus when StartHidden:true

fix(windows): prevent Center() from stealing focus when StartHidden:true (#5249)

* fix(windows): prevent Center() from stealing focus when StartHidden is true

When StartHidden:true is set, the Center() method's SetWindowPos call
would activate the window and steal focus from the foreground application.
Adding SWP_NOACTIVATE to the flags prevents this behavior.

Fixes #4882

* test(4882): make Center() focus test a real regression guard

The previous test only OR'd together locally-redefined SWP_* constants and
never referenced Center(), so it passed even if form.go reverted to
SWP_NOSIZE only (per PR review). Replace it with an AST-based assertion that
parses form.go and verifies Center()'s SetWindowPos call still includes
SWP_NOACTIVATE. Runs on any OS (winc is Windows-only), and fails if the flag
is dropped.

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5380 — v3(windows): add WindowsOptions.UseVisualHosting to fix WebView2 hangs over RDP

v3(windows): add WindowsOptions.UseVisualHosting to fix WebView2 hangs over RDP (#5380)

* v3(windows): add WindowsOptions.UseVisualHosting to fix WebView2 hangs over RDP

When a Wails3 app is used over Microsoft Remote Desktop's iOS client (or
any RDP client that provisions a virtual monitor with a different DPI
context mid-session), WebView2's default windowed hosting forces a
synchronous DComp re-marshal on every controller call. Each PutIsVisible,
MoveFocus, first-paint, and surface release blocks the UI thread for
~2 s, and the bad state persists across reconnects until the host is
rebooted. The aggregated cost on a typical popup-heavy app is 4-8 s for
open and 2-3 s of parent-window stalls on close.

A native Win32 + WebView2 sample on the same machine is unaffected,
which is consistent with this being a hosting-mode interaction rather
than a generic WebView2 or DWM bug.

The Microsoft-documented fix is to set the
COREWEBVIEW2_FORCED_HOSTING_MODE env var to
COREWEBVIEW2_HOSTING_MODE_WINDOW_TO_VISUAL before WebView2 initialises.
With visual hosting the controller's compositor surface is owned through
a DComp visual the host owns, so DPI-context changes don't trigger the
synchronous re-marshal.

This change adds a WindowsOptions.UseVisualHosting opt-in (default false
to preserve existing behavior) that sets the env var inside
newPlatformApp, before any WebView2 environment is constructed.

Refs:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/windowed-vs-visual-hosting
- https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/5248
- https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/4485
- https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1212

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat(v3): first-class production server build (parity with desktop Taskfiles) (#5695)

* feat(v3): first-class production server build, consistent with desktop tasks

Server mode previously only built a dev-tagged binary: `build:server` passed
just `-tags server`, so deployed headless servers shipped with dev-only code
paths and no build hardening, with no parity to the desktop build/package matrix.

`server` and `production` are orthogonal, composable tags, so this wires the
existing capability into the build tooling:

- build:server now builds a production binary by default
  (-tags server,production -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-w -s"),
  mirroring the desktop `build` task; DEV=true builds a development server,
  OBFUSCATED=true builds via garble, and EXTRA_TAGS adds build tags.
- run:server runs a development server (DEV=true).
- Dockerfile.server / build:docker build the production server statically
  (CGO_ENABLED=0, -tags server,production) and build the production frontend
  first so the embedded assets are current.

Verified end-to-end via a generated project: production build is
-tags=server,production -trimpath, stripped (~28% smaller than the dev server).

Closes #5693

* fix(v3): make CGO configurable in Dockerfile.server instead of hardcoding off

Hardcoding CGO_ENABLED=0 blocked projects that need CGO. Expose CGO_ENABLED,
GO_IMAGE and RUNTIME_IMAGE as Docker build args (defaults unchanged: pure-Go
static binary on distroless/static), pass them through `task build:docker`, and
install a C toolchain in the builder only when CGO is enabled (apk or apt).

CGO apps: task build:docker CGO_ENABLED=1 GO_IMAGE=golang:bookworm RUNTIME_IMAGE=gcr.io/distroless/base-debian12

The native `build:server` task is unchanged and remains CGO-neutral (inherits
the environment), so CGO projects already build correctly outside Docker.

* review: quote server binary path; tag docker frontend bindings

Address CodeRabbit review on #5695:
- Quote the server binary path in build:server (-o "...") and run:server, so an
  APP_NAME containing spaces is not shell-split (matches the desktop tasks).
- build:docker now passes BUILD_FLAGS="-tags server,production" to build:frontend
  so generate:bindings analyses the same build the image compiles, rather than
  the default-tag build.

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5668 — fix(v3/linux): confine remaining WebKit request ops to the GTK main thread (#5631)

fix(v3/linux): confine remaining WebKit request ops to the GTK main thread (#5631) (#5668)

* fix(v3/linux): confine remaining WebKit request ops to the GTK main thread (#5631)

#5640 marshalled the response completion (webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish_*)
onto the GTK main thread via invokeOnMainSync, but deliberately left the
request metadata reads and the request-body input stream on the asset-server
worker goroutine. alpha2.105 (which includes #5640) still aborts in
g_object_unref during g_main_context_iteration, and the reporter confirmed via
a ~22h soak that confining the remaining operations stops the crashes.

WebKit2GTK is not thread-safe: every call that touches a WebKit/libsoup object
owned by the GTK main loop must run on the thread driving g_application_run.
This extends the confinement to all such calls that still ran on the worker:

- request URL / HTTP method / HTTP headers reads
- request body stream lookup, reads and close/unref
- the response GUnixInputStream: it is now created and unref'd inside the same
  invokeOnMainSync hop as webkit_uri_scheme_response_new/finish_with_response,
  instead of being built and unref'd on the worker while WebKit took its ref on
  the main thread (a cross-thread refcount split on the stream).

Applied to both the GTK3 (webkit2gtk-4.1) and default GTK4 (webkitgtk-6.0) cgo
builds. The purego build was removed in #5661, so no longer applies.

Credit to @jalfdev for the diagnosis and the validated patch outline in #5631.

Refs #5631, #5640

* fix(v3/linux): run main-thread dispatch inline once the GTK loop has stopped

invokeOnMainSync schedules a source onto the GTK main loop and blocks the
asset-server worker on a GCond until it runs. If the loop stops (app shutdown)
while a worker is mid-request, the source is never serviced and the worker
blocks forever — the shutdown weakness jalfdev flagged in #5631 (review
question 5).

Add an atomic gate (webview_main_dispatch_enabled): appRun clears it via
webview.DisableMainThreadDispatch() the moment g_application_run returns, and
invokeOnMainSync then runs the callback inline on the calling goroutine instead
of scheduling it. Running inline is safe at that point precisely because the
loop is no longer iterating, so the cross-thread race that confinement guards
against is gone — and in-flight asset requests drain during shutdown instead of
wedging.

Refs #5631

* fix(v3/linux): close shutdown race and guard zero-length body reads (#5631)

Address CodeRabbit review on #5668:

- Serialize the dispatch-enabled check with main-loop scheduling under a
  dedicated GMutex. Previously a worker could read the flag as enabled, have
  the GTK loop stop before it scheduled its source, and then block forever on
  a source that would never run. The check and g_main_context_invoke now hold
  webview_dispatch_mu together, so a worker either schedules onto a live loop
  or runs the callback inline because the loop has already stopped.

- Return early from webkitRequestBody.Read on a zero-length buffer instead of
  taking &p[0], which panics on an empty slice. Matches the io.Reader contract.

* test(v3/linux): cover main-thread dispatch and shutdown disable (#5631)

Drive invokeOnMainSync and DisableMainThreadDispatch against a real GLib main
loop to lock in the invariants behind the #5668 shutdown-race fix:

- callbacks run on the loop thread while dispatch is enabled;
- racing DisableMainThreadDispatch against in-flight workers never deadlocks;
- after disable, callbacks run inline on the caller instead of being scheduled
  onto the (now dead) loop.

Go forbids cgo in _test.go files, so the GLib loop scaffolding lives in a
companion non-test file. Passes under -race on both gtk3 and gtk4 build tags.

* test(v3/linux): add zero-length Read guard test and document subtest order (#5631)

* test(v3/linux): synchronize test main-loop globals across threads (#5631)

CodeRabbit flagged the test-support loop globals (webview_test_loop,
webview_test_loop_thread) as written on the loop thread and read from worker
goroutines with no C-level synchronization, so testWaitLoopRunning could spin on
a stale value and testOnLoopThread could read stale state.

Guard all shared loop state with a GMutex, and publish loop readiness from an
idle source via a GCond instead of spin-polling an unsynchronized flag. Still
passes under -race on gtk3 and gtk4.

---------

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): re-assert WebView2 bounds on WM_DPICHANGED for mixed-DPI drag (#5677) (#5689)

* fix(v3/windows): re-assert WebView2 bounds on WM_DPICHANGED (#5677)

When dragging a window across a mixed-DPI monitor boundary, the
WM_DPICHANGED handler re-put the WebView2 rasterization scale but never
re-asserted the controller bounds. A scale re-put alone does not make
WebView2 re-lay out content whose bounds are unchanged, so the page kept
reporting sizes computed with the stale scale: content rendered shrunk,
then disappeared entirely, until the app was restarted.

Mirror the un-minimise path (resyncWebviewDPIAfterMinimise, #5544) and
call chromium.Resize() after a successful scale resync. Gating on the
resync return value keeps the call off an unavailable/suspended
controller (#5605): a true return is proof PutRasterizationScale just
succeeded, so the controller is live.

Fixes #5677

* docs(v3): changelog entry for #5677 mixed-DPI WebView2 fix

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha2.108 and update changelog [skip ci]

feat(v3): global (system-wide) keyboard shortcuts (#5686)

feat(v3): add global (system-wide) keyboard shortcuts

Add app.GlobalShortcut for registering system-wide hotkeys that fire even
when the application is not focused. The manager exposes Register,
Unregister, UnregisterAll, IsRegistered and GetAll, reuses the existing
accelerator syntax, and supports registration before app.Run (bindings are
flushed at startup).

Implemented natively per platform with no third party dependencies:
- macOS: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey (no Accessibility permission required)
- Windows: Win32 RegisterHotKey + WM_HOTKEY
- Linux X11: XGrabKey (single-threaded Xlib loop with self-pipe wakeup)
- Linux Wayland: XDG Desktop Portal org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts

Same-shortcut behavior: an intra-app duplicate returns an error and
preserves the original binding on every platform; an inter-app conflict is
resolved by the OS (Windows/X11 reject, macOS allows, Wayland compositor
arbitrates).

Includes unit tests, an X11 integration test, an interactive manual-test
example, and documentation.

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
ci: fix runtime publish (tag/Node), commit regenerated runtime back, auto-commit sponsor image (#5647)

* ci(npm): publish prerelease as latest + bump CI Node to 22

The OIDC migration (#5646) authenticates correctly but `npm publish` fails
on npm >= 11 with 'You must specify a tag using --tag when publishing a
prerelease version' — the old JS-DevTools action defaulted to `latest`
implicitly. v3 intentionally ships alpha.N as the default dist-tag (the
templates pin "@wailsio/runtime": "latest"), so publish with --tag latest.

Also bump the CI Node from the deprecated 20 to 22 (LTS).

* ci(npm): verify generated artifacts + commit regenerated runtime to master

Harden the publish flow per the existing regenerate-before-publish design:
- add a Verify step that fails the job if (re)generation didn't produce the
  expected outputs (bundled runtime + npm dist/), catching silent build
  failures before anything is published or committed.
- make the commit-back explicit: 'git add -A' sweeps every regenerated tracked
  file (bundled runtime in internal/assetserver/bundledassets, generated
  pkg/events/events.go, TypeDoc output) back to master alongside the version
  bump; log 'git status' so the committed set is visible. dist/ is gitignored
  and is rebuilt fresh by prepack at publish time.

* ci(sponsors): auto-commit sponsor image instead of opening a PR

Push the regenerated website/static/img/sponsors.svg straight to master
(no-op when unchanged) using the bypass-capable WAILS_REPO_TOKEN, matching
publish-npm.yml, rather than opening a daily 'update sponsors' PR. Also
modernise the actions (checkout v3->v4, setup-node v2->v4, Node 20->22).

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
feat(v3): built-in MCP server (experimental) (#5682)

* feat(v3): add MCP service for LLM-driven app testing and control

Adds v3/pkg/services/mcp: a Model Context Protocol server (streamable
HTTP) that lets MCP clients such as Claude Code inspect, test and drive
a running Wails application.

- 16 tools: window inventory/control, JS eval, DOM inspection and
  query, bound method calls, application events, and simulated input.
- Mouse input is rendered in-page with a fully animated cursor overlay
  (eased movement, hover transitions, click ripples, press animation,
  drag with HTML5 DnD support, smooth scrolling) while dispatching
  complete pointer/mouse event sequences. Keyboard input dispatches
  per-character key/input events using native value setters so
  controlled inputs (React et al.) observe changes.
- Gated behind the 'mcp' build tag; without it the service is a no-op
  stub so registration can remain in place for all builds.
- The CLI maps the WAILS_MCP env var to the build tag for both
  'wails3 build' and 'wails3 dev' (via EXTRA_TAGS).
- JS results return over a same-origin asset-server route when the
  service is mounted with ServiceOptions.Route, with a CORS-enabled
  localhost fallback. Server binds 127.0.0.1 and validates origins.
- Includes protocol/CLI tests, a playground example (v3/examples/mcp),
  docs guide and changelog entry.

* refactor(v3): move MCP server into application package as a build-tag feature

MCP is no longer a user-registered service. The server now auto-starts
inside App.Run() when built with -tags mcp — no user code changes required.

Key changes:
- Delete v3/pkg/services/mcp (the old service package)
- Add mcp_enabled.go / mcp_disabled.go in v3/pkg/application with a
  startMCPServer(a *App) function called from App.Run()
- All configuration via env vars with sensible defaults:
    WAILS_MCP_HOST        (default 127.0.0.1)
    WAILS_MCP_PORT        (default 9099; 0 = free port)
    WAILS_MCP_TIMEOUT     (default 30000 ms)
    WAILS_MCP_HIDE_CURSOR (default off)
- Example app (v3/examples/mcp) drops the mcp.New() service registration
- Tutorial doc rewritten with step-by-step guide, multi-window and
  element-selector details, and full env-var reference table

* fix(v3/mcp): guard against mobile targets and mark as experimental

- Add !ios && !android to all mcp build constraints so the server
  compiles out silently on mobile (TCP server not viable on real
  devices; simulator edge case not worth supporting)
- mcp_disabled.go now covers !mcp || ios || android
- Mark the MCP guide as Experimental (sidebar badge + Aside callout)
- Fix redundant WAILS_MCP=1 in go run example (env var only consumed
  by the Wails CLI, not by go directly)

* docs: add MCP to Experimental section; remove Experimental badge from Mobile and Server Build

- Add LLM Control (MCP) to the Experimental sidebar group
- Add MCP LinkCard to experimental/index.mdx Current experiments
- Remove Experimental badge/pill from the Mobile sidebar group
- Remove Experimental badge, Aside, and Overview heading from server-build.mdx
- Remove Experimental badge from mobile/index.mdx frontmatter

* fix(mcp): address PR #5682 review comments

- docs: correct startup description to App.Run() (not application.New())
- docs: remove stale v3/pkg/services/mcp and mcp.Config.Port references from README
- mcp_enabled: reject negative port values; only 0 means OS-assigned free port
- mcp_enabled: add ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout/IdleTimeout to http.Server
- mcp_eval: normalise wildcard bind hosts (0.0.0.0, ::) to localhost in callbackURL
- mcp_inject: wrap drag body in try/finally so state.buttons is reset on failure
- mcp_inject: add 2000-node budget cap to DOM snapshot traversal to prevent webview stalls
- mcp_protocol: return invalid-request error for empty batch [] instead of 202
- mcp_protocol: check isNotification before method switch so all methods honour it uniformly
- mcp_tools: require explicit bool for set_always_on_top; error on missing/non-bool argument
- mcp_tools: reject zero or negative width/height in set_size
- mcp_test: assert exactly 16 tools (count check + duplicate detection)

---------

  stub so registration can remain in place for all builds.

  'wails3 build' and 'wails3 dev' (via EXTRA_TAGS).

- Remove Experimental badge, Aside, and Overview heading from server-build.mdx

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha2.107 and update changelog [skip ci]
chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5613 — fix(v3/wake): propagate included Taskfile vars so preconditions expand correctly

fix(v3/wake): propagate included Taskfile vars so preconditions expand correctly (#5613)

* fix(v3/wake): propagate included Taskfile vars so preconditions expand correctly

When wake resolves `includes:`, it cloned tasks into the parent Taskfile but
dropped the included file's top-level `vars:` block entirely.  This caused any
template reference inside a cloned task's preconditions or commands — such as
`{{.CROSS_IMAGE}}` in the `linux:build:docker` precondition — to be rendered
literally rather than expanded.  The unexpanded shell command also made the
precondition fail on a literal string, so cross-compilation via Docker was
completely broken even after running `wails3 task setup:docker`.

Three coordinated changes:

* parse/parse.go: inject the included file's top-level vars into each cloned
  task's Vars map (included-file vars are defaults; task-own vars win).
* exec/runner.go: call parse.ExpandTemplates on both pc.Sh and pc.Msg before
  executing the precondition shell check or formatting the error message.
* exec/exec.go: move mergeVars before checkPreconditions so the fully-merged
  variable map is available for template expansion in preconditions.

Adds a regression test in parse_test.go that verifies top-level vars from an
included file propagate into all cloned tasks and that task-level vars still
take precedence.

* fix(v3/wake): deep-copy injected include vars; skip mergeVars for cached preconditionless tasks

Address PR review feedback:
- Deep-copy the included Taskfile's top-level vars when injecting them into
  cloned tasks (consistent with Task.Clone). Sharing *ast.Var by pointer let
  the in-place mutation in ResolveVars/ResolveAllVarShells leak across all
  tasks that include the same file. Regression test asserts distinct pointers
  and isolation under mutation.
- Compute mergedVars lazily: tasks without preconditions that are up-to-date
  no longer pay for the fixed-point template expansion.

* docs(v3): add Experimental section with Wake page

Introduce a top-level Experimental docs section that explains what
'experimental' means in Wails (opt-in, may not survive, actively seeking
feedback), plus a dedicated page per experiment. First page documents Wake —
the experimental Wails-aware build runner from #5613 — covering why it exists,
how to enable it (WAILS_USE_WAKE=true), local overrides, automatic fallback to
Task, and the full env-var reference.

* docs(v3/experimental): scope section to Wake; single GitHub feedback channel

- Drop the redundant 'Experimental' badge from the sidebar group (the
  section is already named Experimental).
- Remove the Server Build card from the overview (it is not an experiment).
- Drop the note framing Mobile as experimental.
- Consolidate feedback to a single channel: GitHub Discussions (best fit for
  open-ended experiment feedback), replacing the Discussions/Issues/Discord set
  on both the overview and the Wake page.

* docs(v3/experimental): point feedback links at the GitHub Discussions threads

- Wake page links to the dedicated Wake feedback discussion (#5679).
- Overview links to the Experiments discussions category, which scales as
  more experiments get their own threads.

* docs(v3/wake): reframe 'why it exists' around domain understanding

Lead with the core idea that Wake understands the Wails build domain, and
recast the benefits accordingly: it rebuilds only what a build actually needs
(precise input/output tracking rather than relying on hand-declared
sources/generates), parallelises what it knows to be independent, and — being
part of wails3 rather than a third-party tool — can grow new capabilities
in-house, including running cross-platform tooling natively where a Taskfile
shells out to the wails3 binary today. Drops the confusing 'Wails templates
don't declare them' phrasing.

---------

commit.message:
ci(release): skip internal commits and link webview2 notes in release notes (#5673)

* ci(changelog): skip internal commits/PRs from release notes

Internal-only changes (CI/pipeline, chores incl. secret rotations and
dependency bumps, build/test/style plumbing) no longer reach the
user-facing release notes.

- auto-changelog.go: detect the conventional-commit type from the PR
  title and skip internal-typed PRs (ci/chore/build/test/style) before
  the LLM call. Fails open: a non-conventional title is treated as
  user-facing, never dropped. Maintainers can still force an entry by
  editing UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md in the PR (existing skip-if-touched
  step leaves it intact).
- auto-changelog-v3.yml: guard the commit step so an internal PR that
  produces no entry doesn't fail at 'git commit' (nothing to commit).
- release-webview2.yml: filter the same internal types out of the
  git-log release notes, pipefail-safe, with a maintenance-release
  fallback when nothing user-facing remains.

Skip-set kept in sync between the Go predicate and the shell filter.

* ci(release): link to webview2 release notes instead of embedding them

Each webview2 release body uses its own heading style (hand-written
'### Fixes' vs flat auto-generated bullet lists), so inlining the notes
into the v3 changelog produced inconsistent, messy entries. Replace the
embedded body with a single bullet linking to the webview2 release page
(tag slash URL-encoded as %2F). Drops the now-unused gh release view call
and its GH_TOKEN env.

---------

commit.message: chore(changelog): auto-add entry for PR #5671 — ci(webview2): fix release build (cross-compile Windows + complete go.sum)

ci(webview2): fix release build (cross-compile Windows + complete go.sum) (#5671)

ci(webview2): fix the release build (cross-compile for Windows + complete go.sum)

The release-webview2 'Build and test' step ran 'go build ./... && go test ./...'
on the ubuntu runner, but webview2 is Windows-only code, so it failed two ways:
- go.sum was incomplete for a clean resolve (missing golang.org/x/sys entries)
- even with that fixed, building/testing Windows-only packages on linux errors
  with 'build constraints exclude all Go files'

Fix the build gate to cross-compile for Windows (GOOS=windows go build + go vet,
after go mod download) and commit the completed go.sum (go mod tidy, +13 lines).
Native 'go test' can't run Windows binaries on linux; vet is the lightweight
cross-platform gate (full tests run in the Windows CI).

This unblocks the nightly webview2 release workflow.

* ci(changelog): generate entries with GitHub Models instead of OpenRouter

The per-PR changelog auto-fill (auto-changelog.go) called OpenRouter
(google/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001) via OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Switch it to
GitHub Models, which is included with the repo's GitHub plan and uses the
built-in GITHUB_TOKEN — no third-party key to manage.

- auto-changelog.go: POST to https://models.github.ai/inference/chat/completions
  with GITHUB_TOKEN; model openai/gpt-4.1-mini. The API is OpenAI-compatible,
  so the request payload and response parsing are unchanged.
- auto-changelog-v3.yml: grant 'models: read' so the built-in token can call
  inference; drop the OPENROUTER_API_KEY env.

Dry-run verified: a direct inference call returns HTTP 200, and an
end-to-end run of auto-changelog.go against a merged PR produced a correctly
classified changelog entry.

* ci(changelog): harden against prompt injection + address review

Security hardening (the PR title / CodeRabbit summary fed to the model are
attacker-influenceable):
- isolate the untrusted PR context inside <pr_data> markers and instruct the
  model to treat it as data, never instructions
- sanitise the entry in code (not just via the prompt): collapse to a single
  line, strip HTML/JSX tags and markdown link/image/code syntax, hard-cap the
  length — so a prompt-injected response can't inject markup into the changelog
  or release notes

Review feedback (CodeRabbit on #5666):
- auto-changelog-v3.yml: declare pull-requests: read and issues: read (the job
  reads PR files/info and issue comments via GITHUB_TOKEN under an explicit
  permissions block)
- auto-changelog.go: give outbound HTTP a 30s timeout via a shared client so a
  stalled GitHub/model response can't hang the job

commit.message:
ci(webview2): nightly release with change-detection, notes, and auto-fold into v3 release notes (#5665)

* ci(webview2): nightly release with change-detection, notes, and auto-fold into v3

Rework the webview2 release automation into a coherent nightly flow.

release-webview2.yml:
- run nightly (cron) + manual dispatch instead of push-on-webview2-change;
  add a 'force' input
- only cut a tag if webview2/ actually changed since the last webview2/v*
  tag (no-op on quiet days)
- generate release notes from the webview2 git log since the last tag and
  attach them to the GitHub release (gh release create --notes-file),
  replacing the static 'Release of webview2 vX' body
- drop the repository-dispatch -> bump chain. It was broken: client-payload
  was written as a YAML mapping instead of a JSON string, so the workflow
  failed to parse and could not run at all.

nightly-release-v3.yml:
- new 'Sync webview2 to latest release' step: reads the latest webview2/v*
  tag and, if v3/go.mod is behind, bumps it and folds the webview2 release
  notes into v3/UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md so they surface in the v3 release
  notes. Best-effort: a failure never blocks the v3 release.

bump-webview2-v3.yml: removed - the v3 nightly consumes webview2 directly,
so the separate dispatch/PR bump workflow is redundant.

Validated with actionlint.

* ci(webview2): address review — harden inputs, best-effort sync, accurate summary

- release-webview2: validate the workflow_dispatch 'version' input via env and
  a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH regex instead of interpolating it into the shell
  (prevents template/command injection in a contents:write step)
- release-webview2: gate the success summary on the release step's outcome so a
  failed build/tag/release no longer reports 'Released ...'
- nightly-release-v3: make the webview2-sync commit/push best-effort (reset +
  continue on failure) so it can never block the v3 release
- nightly-release-v3: if the '## Changed' changelog anchor is missing, append
  the section so the webview2 notes are never silently dropped

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

chore(v3/linux): remove the unmaintained purego build path (#5661)

The `purego` Linux build target (-tags purego, CGO_ENABLED=0) does not
compile on master — `go build -tags purego ./v3/pkg/application` fails
with `undefined: linuxApp`, `fatalHandler`, `newPlatformApp`,
`clipboardSet`, … The platform app layer was never completed for it, so
it is dead, non-building code that only adds maintenance surface (e.g. it
silently diverged from the cgo menu model — see #5464).

Remove it:
- delete the purego implementation files (application + assetserver/webview)
- drop the two purego-only source-introspection tests from
  linux_undo_regression_test.go (the cgo/gtk3 tests are kept)
- drop the now-unused github.com/ebitengine/purego dependency (go mod tidy)

The default cgo (GTK4) and gtk3 build paths are unaffected — they are
gated on the `cgo` build tag and never referenced the purego files. The
code is preserved on the `archive/purego-linux` branch if it is ever
revived and completed.

No issue number — this is cleanup surfaced while fixing #5464.

commit.message:
fix(v3/linux): make Menu.Update() rebuild the native menu (GTK4) (#5659)

The default GTK4 path (menu_linux.go + linux_cgo.go) used a one-way
`processed` guard that returned early on every processMenu() after the
first, so Menu.Update() was a silent no-op — added/removed items never
appeared (#5464).

Replace the early-return with a clear-and-rebuild on re-process, matching
the pattern the GTK3 path (menu_linux_gtk3.go) already uses — it calls
menuClear() before rebuilding. The GTK4 GMenu model was simply missing its
menuClear(): add it in linux_cgo.go using g_menu_remove_all on the native
GMenu, and reset the per-menu append counter (menuItemCounters) so rebuilt
items get fresh 0-based positions (the index is used by menu_remove_item
for hide/show). In processMenu, call menuClear(menu) instead of returning
when already processed.

Because the rebuild clears first and then re-appends, re-running Update()
is idempotent and cannot duplicate items (the original guard's concern).

Verified on Linux/GTK4 under Xvfb (lin-node1): after adding an item and
calling Menu.Update() at runtime, the native GMenu's item count tracks the
change (1 -> 2). Only the default GTK4 cgo path was affected.

Fixes #5464

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(webview2): recover from transient runtime COM errors instead of exiting (#5658)

Chromium.errorCallback logs and then calls os.Exit(1). That is correct
while the WebView2 environment/controller is being created, but several
*runtime* COM paths routed transient failures through the same callback,
so a recoverable hiccup after startup killed the whole application
(wailsapp/wails#5580, and the crash class behind #5544/#5650/#5446/#4158).

Following the precedent already set for Focus() and Eval(), convert the
runtime sites from the issue audit table to log-and-recover:

  - Resize / GetClientRect  -> log + skip frame
  - Navigate / NavigateToString -> log
  - Init (AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated) -> log
  - MessageReceived: a malformed/untrusted web message is now dropped
    (log + return) instead of taking the process down; a failed
    GetAdditionalObjects falls back to delivering the plain message;
    PostWebMessageAsString failure logs

Also convert two further user-triggered runtime ops beyond the audit
table (PutZoomFactor, OpenDevToolsWindow).

The ~20 init/controller-creation sites remain fatal as specified.

Refs #5580 #5544 #5650

and Bindings steps.

commit.message:
fix(v3/setupwizard): light-mode, layout, and cross-platform code signing (#5648)

* feat(v3/setupwizard): cross-platform code signing, light-mode fixes, global signing config

Setup wizard (frontend + server):
- Fix light-mode setup wizard: darker sidebar step labels/circles, legible captions, white dragon-eye preserved
- Harden static asset serving: pin Content-Type for .svg etc. so the logo never blanks on hosts with an incomplete MIME DB (+test)
- Code Signing page now helps sign for every platform from any host: detect signing tools with host-aware install commands, Docs links to the Wails signing guide, a Recheck button, and git-config-prefilled forms
- Generate signing material: GPG key creation that also exports the key to a file (and auto-exports id-only keys), Windows self-signed certificate via OpenSSL
- Prefill author identity from git config (SystemInfo.GitName/GitEmail)

Sign pipeline (commands):
- resolveSigningDefaults now backfills macOS/Windows/Linux options from ~/.config/wails/defaults.yaml, applied for every sign path (+test)
- Linux/Windows Taskfile templates: PGP_KEY/SIGN_CERTIFICATE are now optional overrides that fall back to global config; clearer 'no key found' errors

Docs:
- Rework the code-signing guide: wails3 setup quick start, configuration-precedence and per-project sections, self-signed cert + auto-export notes

* fix(v3/setupwizard): keep the wizard card usable and proportional when resized

The card scaled as a flat 75vw/75vh with no minimum, so shrinking the window
left large backdrop margins while the content squashed to unusable.

- Card now holds a fixed 3:2 aspect ratio (matching the 1200x800 max) and
  scales to fit whichever of width/height is the tighter constraint, down to an
  864x576 minimum (content pane never below ~36rem)
- Margins shrink first: the card fills the viewport (minus a small gutter) before
  capping at 1200x800 and centering with the backdrop margins
- Below the minimum the card holds its size and the viewport-locked scroll
  container scrolls in both axes so nothing is clipped/unreachable
- Sizing via inline style so Tailwind's purge can't drop the clamp()/min() math

* fix(v3/setupwizard): address PR review (signing security + robustness)

- Validate GPG keyID against a hex allowlist before using it in the export file
  path (fixes CodeQL path-injection + traversal risk in exportGPGSecretKey)
- Surface SaveGlobalDefaults failures in the GPG create/export and Windows cert
  handlers instead of returning success on a silent config-save failure
- Clear gpgKeyPath when the selected GPG key changes so the path can't mismatch
  the id and the export prompt can re-appear
- Quote PGP_KEY/SIGN_ROLE and SIGN_CERTIFICATE/SIGN_THUMBPRINT/TIMESTAMP_SERVER
  in the Linux/Windows sign Taskfiles so values with spaces don't split

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

commit.message:
ci(webview2): auto-release a new tag when webview2 source changes (#5638)

* ci(webview2): auto-release on webview2 source changes to master

Add a push trigger (branches: master, paths: webview2/**) to the existing
Release webview2 workflow so any change to the webview2 module cuts a new
patch tag automatically, then the existing bump-webview2-v3 opens the v3
go.mod bump PR. Prevents the gap where webview2 source gains an API (e.g.
IsReady() in #5568) that v3 cannot use because no release was cut (see #5616).

Loop-safe: the release pushes a tag (not a master commit) and the bump only
edits v3/**, so neither re-triggers this workflow. Adds a concurrency group
to serialise near-simultaneous releases.

* fix(ci): strip leading v in webview2 auto-increment to avoid vv tag

The auto-increment path derived MAJOR from "v1.0.24" as "v1" and then
prefixed another v, producing webview2/vv1.0.25. Stripping the leading v
(webview2/v prefix) yields the correct webview2/v1.0.25. This path becomes
the default once the push trigger fires, so it must be correct.

commit.message:
fix(v3/linux): WebKitGTK main-loop crashes on long-running apps (#5631) (#5640)

* fix(v3/linux/gtk3): keep window IDs integer-typed to avoid GC stack-scan crash

setupSignalHandlers, contextMenuSignals, enableDND and disableDND passed the
window ID as signal user_data, but materialised it in a Go unsafe.Pointer local
via unsafe.Pointer(uintptr(id)). The value is a small integer (e.g. window ID 1,
0x1), not a real pointer, so when the Go garbage collector scanned that
pointer-typed stack slot during a stack copy it aborted with:

    runtime: bad pointer in frame ...setupSignalHandlers at 0x...: 0x1
    fatal error: invalid pointer found on stack

The GTK4 path already passes the ID as C.uintptr_t: #4958 switched the C signal
functions to uintptr_t specifically to clear -race/checkptr errors from this same
fake-pointer pattern, but only on the (then new) GTK4 files. When #5463 flipped
GTK4 to default and renamed the legacy code to *_gtk3.go, the GTK3 path kept the
old unsafe.Pointer form. Back-port the uintptr_t change here: signal_connect,
enableDND and disableDND now take uintptr_t and cast to gpointer in C, so the ID
is never a Go pointer-typed value.

Refs #5631

* fix(v3/linux): complete WebKit asset requests on the GTK main thread

The asset server completes WebKitURISchemeRequests from a pool of worker
goroutines (assetserver_webview.go), calling webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish_*
off the GTK main thread. WebKit2GTK is not thread-safe: these calls mutate and
finalise GObjects owned by the main loop, racing g_application_run and corrupting
refcounts. The result is intermittent native crashes, typically SIGSEGV inside
g_object_unref during g_main_context_iteration (addr=0x28) on long-running apps
under frequent asset/media loads.

#5566 marshalled only the trailing g_object_unref of the request onto the main
context; the finish call itself - where most of the WebKit object manipulation
happens - was still run on the worker goroutine, so the crash persisted.

Add invokeOnMainSync (mainthread_linux.go): a synchronous main-thread dispatch
built on g_main_context_invoke + GCond, shared by the GTK3 and GTK4 cgo builds.
Run the full response completion (webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish_with_response
and finish_error, including response/header construction and unref) under it.

The wait cannot deadlock the main loop: finish_with_response returns before the
response stream is drained (WebKit reads it asynchronously), so the main thread
never blocks waiting on the worker. Body streaming over the pipe stays off the
main thread. The request-body input stream (read/close/unref) is intentionally
left on the worker: it is transfer-full and owned solely by us, so its blocking
read must not freeze the main loop and its unref finalises nothing in the
main-loop object graph.

Refs #5631, #5557

* fix(v3/linux): use a stable GError domain for asset-server finish errors

finishWithError interned the per-request error message as the GError domain via
g_quark_from_string(msg). GQuarks are never freed, so a long-running app with
varying error messages grew the global quark table unboundedly, and the message
string is the wrong value for a domain anyway. Intern a single static domain
quark once (g_quark_from_static_string) instead; the error text is still carried
in the GError message field. Applies to both the GTK3 and GTK4 builds.

This pre-existing leak sat next to the finish_error call moved onto the main
thread in the previous commit. Addresses Copilot review feedback on #5640.

Refs #5631

commit.message:
fix(v2): prevent origin bypass via suffix match in wildcardPatternToRegex (#5074)

* fix(v2): prevent origin bypass via suffix match in wildcardPatternToRegex

Wildcards in BindingsAllowedOrigins patterns are now only expanded when
they represent a full domain component (after "://", ".", or ":").
A wildcard appended to a partial label (e.g. "com*") is stripped,
preventing attacker-controlled domains like "myapp.community" from
bypassing origin checks when "https://myapp.com*" is configured.

Fixes GHSA-47hv-j4px-h3c9

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v2): require both-side component boundary for origin wildcards

Addresses review feedback on GHSA-47hv-j4px-h3c9: the previous fix checked
only the left boundary of '*', so partial-label wildcards (e.g.
"https://*myapp.com", "https://myapp.*com") still expanded and could match
across host boundaries.

A '*' is now expanded only when it forms a complete origin component — a
separator ("://", "." or ":") on the left AND a separator (".", ":", "/" or
end) on the right. It expands to [^.:/@]+ (one non-empty component that cannot
absorb a userinfo '@' delimiter), and the pattern is anchored with \A...\z. Any
other '*' is treated as a literal, so misused trailing/partial wildcards fail
closed.

Adds regression tests for nested-suffix, partial-label, port, and userinfo
(user@host) bypass attempts.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(v3/windows): drop IsReady() guard not present in released webview2

The resync added a w.chromium.IsReady() guard, but IsReady() exists only
in unreleased webview2 source (added in #5568) — it is not in the webview2
module version v3 pins (v1.0.24), so it fails to cross-compile and would
break end-user builds. The guard was defense-in-depth only; the real #5605
protection is the DPI-change gate, and the existing GetController()==nil
check still covers the unavailable-controller case. Re-add the IsReady guard
once a webview2 release including it lands and v3's go.mod is bumped.

docs(v3/windows): correct minimised-window position in DPI-resync comments

The minimise/restore DPI comments asserted a minimised window is parked at
(-32000,-32000). Empirically that is not the position on current Windows
builds: on win-node1 (build 26200, same as the #5605 reporter) a minimised
top-level window's GetWindowRect / WINDOWPLACEMENT.ptMinPosition is the
primary monitor's bottom-left corner (e.g. {0,740}), not (-32000,-32000).
The legacy -32000 value is version/shell dependent, so describe the actual
behaviour instead: while minimised the window is repositioned off the monitor
it will restore to. The fix itself never depended on the exact coordinate.

No functional change.

fix(v3/windows): skip WebView2 rasterization resync in WM_DPICHANGED while minimised

Copilot review on #5616: WM_DPICHANGED ran resyncWebviewRasterizationScale()
unconditionally. While the window is minimised it is parked at (-32000,-32000),
so GetDpiForWindow can report a different monitor's DPI — pushing a wrong scale
onto the controller (which the restore-time DPI gate then won't correct, since
DPI == lastKnownDPI) and making a COM call into a possibly-suspended controller,
reintroducing the #5605 crash mechanism. Gate both the resync and the
lastKnownDPI update behind !w.isMinimizing; a genuine DPI difference is caught on
restore by resyncWebviewDPIAfterUnminimiseIfDPIChanged.

Verified on win-node1: gofmt clean, build + pkg/application suite pass.

fix(v3/windows): don't resync WebView2 DPI on restore unless DPI changed (#5605)

The minimise/restore rasterization-scale resync added in #5544 ran a
GetRasterizationScale COM probe on every restore-from-minimise (it is the
no-op check inside resyncWebviewRasterizationScale). If the window had been
minimised long enough for WebView2 to suspend or for its render/GPU process
to be recycled (the reporter's 10-15s window on Optimus + real displays),
that COM call into the now-unusable controller is the suspected fatal
operation that crashes the app on reopen.

Gate the resync on an actual DPI change detected with the Win32
GetDpiForWindow (never via COM): track lastKnownDPI while the window is
non-minimised (creation, non-minimised WM_SIZE, WM_DPICHANGED) and only
call into the controller on un-minimise when the DPI differs. In the
common same-monitor/fixed-DPI case this makes zero COM calls on restore,
which is what removes the suspected crash. Also add an IsReady() guard to
resyncWebviewRasterizationScale (covers only the early-init window, not a
process-failed controller — the DPI gate is the real protection).

The #5544 mixed-DPI restore is preserved (verified by tracing, not by test):
on a DPI-changing restore the resync still fires, either via the DPI gate
(current != lastKnownDPI) or via the ungated WM_DPICHANGED handler.

Not reproduced or verified-fixed on available hardware: win-node1 has only a
virtual display, so WebView2 never suspends there (process count/memory flat
across a 60s minimise) and the crash cannot be triggered. What is verified on
win-node1 (same WebView2 149.0.4022.69 as reporter): build + pkg/application
suite pass, and an instrumented run confirms the restore path now logs
'DPI unchanged -> SKIP, 0 COM calls'. Needs reporter confirmation on
Optimus/multi-display hardware; the Application event-log faulting module
would confirm the mechanism.

Refs #5605
chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha2.104 and update changelog [skip ci]

fix(v3/ios): empty string from a bound method no longer crashes the app (#5626)

The iOS asset response writer guarded the body pointer with 'buf != nil'
instead of its length. A bound Go method returning "" produces a zero-length
(but non-nil) response body, so '&buf[0]' panicked with index-out-of-range and
aborted the Go runtime (SIGABRT). Guard on len(buf) instead — matching the
darwin/desktop writers — and pass a nil pointer + length 0 for an empty body
(a valid empty NSData on the C side).

Reproduced and verified fixed on the iOS simulator.

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha2.103 and update changelog [skip ci]

fix(wake): expand precondition templates before running them (#5612)

Wake ran each task's precondition `sh:` string directly as a shell command
without expanding its Go template first. The generated build Taskfiles guard
the garble check with:

    sh: '{{if eq .OBFUSCATED "true"}}command -v garble >/dev/null 2>&1{{else}}true{{end}}'

Because wake never templated this, the raw `{{if ...}}` text reached the shell,
failed to parse as a command, and surfaced the precondition's `msg:` as a
spurious "garble is required for obfuscated builds" error on every
`WAILS_USE_WAKE=true wails3 build` — even when obfuscation was not requested.

checkPreconditions now expands `pc.Sh` via parse.ExpandTemplates against the
task's merged vars (matching how cmds, deps and env are handled). The
precondition check is moved after mergeVars so those vars are available, and
still runs before the up-to-date short-circuit. Adds a regression test.

commit.message:
feat(v3/mobile): IOS/Android manager API + event rename; first-class mobile docs (#5602)

* docs: add Mobile to MorphText cycling words on landing page

* docs: add first-class mobile documentation suite

- New Mobile section in sidebar (promoted out of Building & Packaging)
- Mobile overview page: how it works, prereqs table, feature matrix, build tag rules
- 'Your First Mobile App' tutorial: iOS Simulator + Android Emulator paths,
  step-by-step from zero to running app, responsive CSS, platform detection,
  haptics, production builds, troubleshooting
- iOS and Android guides moved to guides/mobile/; old paths redirect
- Landing page card updated: 'Mobile coming soon...' → iOS + Android listed
- Both platform guides link back to the first-mobile-app tutorial for newcomers

* docs(mobile): promote kitchen sink example with run instructions; note screenshot gap

* docs(landing): make mobile a headline feature with zero-changes pitch

* docs(mobile): remove redirect stubs, no remaining links to old paths

* docs(mobile): explain platform-gating pattern for desktop/mobile shared codebase

* refactor(v3/mobile): move native features to IOS/Android managers, rename events

Convert the iOS and Android native-feature free functions into methods on
platform manager singletons:

  application.IOSShare(...)   -> application.IOS.Share(...)
  application.AndroidHaptic() -> application.Android.Haptic(...)
  application.IOSSetScrollEnabled(...) -> application.IOS.SetScrollEnabled(...)

`application.IOS` / `application.Android` are zero-size singletons that only
exist on their respective builds; all callers live in //go:build ios/android
files.

Rename the mobile bridge events away from the `native:*` prefix:
  - cross-platform events -> `common:*` (common:haptic, common:location, …)
  - iOS-only             -> `ios:*`     (ios:beginBackgroundTask, ios:backgroundTask)
  - Android-only         -> `android:*` (android:foregroundService)

The frontend keeps a single listener per event under `common:*`, matching the
shared-codebase model. Updated the Objective-C/C bridge, the Android Java
bridge (template + committed example build copy), the kitchen-sink example
(Go handlers + frontend), IOS.md/ANDROID.md, the docs-site mobile guides and
the unreleased changelog.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/mobile): emit iOS orientation as a map, not via jsonToMap

IOS.GetOrientation() returns a plain string ('portrait'/'landscape'/…),
not JSON, so jsonToMap() failed to parse it and emitted an empty map.
Wrap it under the 'orientation' key the frontend reads (matching the
Android handler). Caught in CodeRabbit review of #5602.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): prevent crash when camera lacks the requested capture media type

mfPresentCamera set picker.mediaTypes to public.movie/public.image without
checking the camera actually offers that type. On the iOS Simulator (and any
device whose camera reports available but does not support video) the virtual
camera exposes stills only, so requesting video made -[UIImagePickerController
setMediaTypes:] throw an uncaught NSException -> SIGABRT.

Check availableMediaTypesForSourceType: before configuring the picker and emit
a graceful common:capture error instead, with an @try/@catch safety net. Pre-
existing since #5562; surfaced by the Xcode 26 simulator's virtual camera.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): rework camera fix — guard setMediaTypes, don't pre-check media list

Follow-up to ec23d47f: the previous fix pre-checked
availableMediaTypesForSourceType:, but that list is unreliable on the iOS
Simulator — it returns empty even when the camera is authorized and can
present, so the pre-check would wrongly block capture. Verified on-simulator:
the list stays empty across authorization states and a 3s poll, yet photo
capture presents fine.

Instead: photos use the picker's default media type (public.image, never
throws); video opts into public.movie inside an @try/@catch so the
'No available types for source 1' NSException degrades to a graceful
common:capture error instead of SIGABRT. Real devices list public.movie and
record normally.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): quote product-name paths in generated Xcode project

The pbxproj template left the c-archive PBXFileReference path and the build
phase's 'go build -o' path unquoted, so a productName containing a space (the
default config ships 'My Product') produced an invalid project.pbxproj —
Xcode reported 'The project main is damaged ... parse error'. Quote both
paths. Also give the mobile example a real, space-free productName
(KitchenSink) and identifier.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/mobile example): add NSFaceIDUsageDescription; show feedback per control group

- Add NSFaceIDUsageDescription to the iOS Info.plist(s). Tapping Authenticate
  called LAContext biometric evaluation, which hard-crashes on a real device
  without this key (same class as the camera/mic keys). The crash left the app
  white-screening on relaunch; a clean reinstall + this key resolve it.
- Move result feedback out of one box at the bottom of each section into a
  compact inline output beside each control group (Share, Screen, Status bar,
  Security, Secure storage, Haptics, Location, Motion, Speech, Keyboard,
  Camera, Background), so results appear next to the control you tapped.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): reload WebView when iOS terminates the WebContent process

WKWebView's renderer (WebContent) process is reaped by iOS under memory
pressure or after repeated background/foreground and launch cycles. With no
webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate: handler the view stayed permanently
blank — the 'white screen on the 3rd+ launch' reported on device. Implement
the delegate method to reload and respawn the renderer. Framework-level fix;
affects all Wails v3 iOS apps.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): fix cold-launch white screen (double WebView) + launch flash

Two iOS fixes:
- ios_create_webview_with_id manually called -loadView and -viewDidLoad, so
  UIKit ALSO loaded the view automatically — two WebViews/viewDidLoad passes per
  cold launch. Content loaded into one while the blank one was displayed →
  intermittent white screen after force-quit + relaunch. Load the view once via
  -loadViewIfNeeded. Verified on-device: one viewDidLoad per launch, renders
  reliably across repeated force-quit relaunches.
- Also fix the missing withError: parameter on didFailProvisionalNavigation
  (the old selector never matched, so load failures were swallowed) and add a
  didFailNavigation:withError: handler.

Flash: any non-zero IOSOptions.BackgroundColour is now applied to the app
window automatically (no need to also set AppBackgroundColourSet), so the
window matches the web background instead of flashing white before the WebView
paints. The mobile example sets it to its web background (#1b2636).

Refs #5602

* refactor(v3/ios): remove IOSOptions.AppBackgroundColourSet

The flag only existed to distinguish a deliberate fully-transparent app window
({0,0,0,0}) from the unset zero value — but a transparent app-window background
is meaningless (the window needs an opaque backing), so the distinction had no
real use. Drop it and treat any non-zero BackgroundColour as set; the zero
value means unset (defaults to white). Simpler API, one field instead of two.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): remove white launch flash (launch screen + initial window)

The app declared UILaunchStoryboardName but the build never bundled a compiled
storyboard, so iOS showed a white default launch screen; and the window was
created white in the delegate before Go could apply a background colour. Both
caused a white flash on (cold) launch.

- Add a LaunchBackground colour asset (#1b2636) and switch Info.plist(s) to
  UILaunchScreen { UIColorName = LaunchBackground } — bundled via the asset
  catalog the build already compiles.
- Colour the initial UIWindow/root view from the same LaunchBackground asset in
  didFinishLaunching (timing-independent; falls back to white if absent).

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): show local notifications while app is in foreground

iOS suppresses a local notification's banner while the app that posted it is
in the foreground unless the app registers a UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate
and opts into presentation. Wails registered no such delegate, so notifications
fired but were delivered silently to Notification Center with no banner.

Add an MFNotificationDelegate (UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate) whose
willPresentNotification returns banner+list+sound (alert+sound pre-iOS 14) and
didReceiveNotificationResponse handles taps. Register it via
ios_notifications_init() — both at launch (see delegate change) and defensively
at the top of ios_post_notification so it is set regardless of build path.

The mobile example surfaces the new common:notification {presented}/{tapped}
signals so foreground delivery is visible in the UI.

* fix(v3/ios): finalize cold-launch fix and clean up iOS build templates

Start the Go runtime from the app delegate's didFinishLaunchingWithOptions
(after UIKit has launched) instead of concurrently with UIApplicationMain,
which intermittently corrupted the FrontBoard launch handshake on device
(blank cold launch / 0x8BADF00D). main.m is now a minimal bootstrap; because
it no longer references a Go symbol the archive must be linked with
-Wl,-force_load (set in all iOS Taskfiles) or the WailsAppDelegate class is
dead-stripped.

Also: register the notification delegate before launch finishes; remove the
dead, archive-less build.sh.tmpl (+ rendered copies); align the older
examples/ios bootstrap with the verified examples/mobile pattern; tidy the
example go.mod.

* fix(v3/ios): make ios:run/package work in a normal (non-repo) project

Three bugs prevented a plain 'wails3 init' app from building/running on iOS,
while the in-repo examples masked them:

- overlay:gen read its main_ios.go template from the wails SOURCE TREE via
  repoRoot(); outside the wails repo that path doesn't exist, so it failed with
  'file does not exist'. Read it from the embedded build_assets FS instead
  (same approach as xcode:gen).
- run/deploy-simulator/deploy-device hardcoded a com.wails.<app>[.dev] bundle
  id for simctl/devicectl, but the real id comes from build/config.yml (e.g.
  com.example.<app>). simctl install succeeded but launch failed (code 4). Read
  CFBundleIdentifier from the built bundle's Info.plist instead.
- the iOS build depended on common:generate:icons (icns/ico — not used by iOS,
  and its dir:build broke through the nested include) and a redundant
  generate:ios:bindings that raced build:frontend's own bindings -clean. Both
  removed; iOS icons come from Assets.xcassets via actool and bindings from
  build:frontend.

Verified end-to-end: 'wails3 init' + 'wails3 task ios:run' builds, installs and
launches a default app on the iOS Simulator.

* docs(ios): document the IOS manager pattern + common/ios events; add verified simulator screenshot

- ios.mdx: replace the inaccurate runtime blurb (which mixed Go and JS APIs and
  referenced a non-existent IOS.Scroll.SetEnabled JS call) with proper sections:
  * 'Native device features — the IOS manager': the Go application.IOS.* pattern
    (one-shot actions, JSON query helpers) with correct Haptic values.
  * 'Asynchronous results: common:* and ios:* events': the event model with a
    full table mapping each event to the manager call that triggers it and its
    payload (common:* = shared with Android, ios:* = iOS-only).
  * 'Runtime WebView controls': the Go SetScrollEnabled/... toggles plus the
    real frontend runtime (IOS.Haptics.Impact, IOS.Device.Info).
- first-mobile-app.mdx: add a screenshot of a default 'wails3 init' app running
  on the iOS Simulator, captured by actually running the tutorial end to end.

The tutorial's command sequence (wails3 init -> wails3 task ios:run -> ios:logs:dev
-> ios:xcode) was verified by running it against a fresh project on the Simulator.

* fix(v3/templates): make the default app templates mobile-responsive

On a phone the starter app's 'Wails + <Framework>' heading (font-size: 3.2em)
overflowed and wrapped onto two lines, and content ran to the screen edges
under the notch. Applied the same responsive treatment to every template's
style.css and index.html:

- h1 uses clamp(1.9rem, 8vw, 3.2rem) so it fits one line on phones and stays
  3.2rem on desktop.
- .container gets box-sizing, a 720px max-width and safe-area-aware padding
  (env(safe-area-inset-*)) so content clears the notch/home indicator.
- logos cap at 40vw and shrink on <=480px viewports.
- viewport meta gains viewport-fit=cover so the safe-area insets apply on iOS.

Verified on the iOS Simulator with a fresh 'wails3 init' app: the heading now
renders on a single line. The docs tutorial screenshot is updated to match.

* docs(mobile): correct Go version to 1.25+ and simplify first-run steps

- The mobile guides stated 'Go 1.24+', but the generated project's go.mod (and
  wails/v3) require go 1.25.0. Corrected to 1.25+ in ios, android,
  first-mobile-app and the index requirements table.
- first-mobile-app: replaced the six-bullet technical breakdown of 'wails3 task
  ios:run' (Xcode scaffold, c-archive, GOOS=ios, ad-hoc signing, ...) with a
  single beginner-friendly sentence plus a short 'first run is slow' tip.

Verified against the code: config.yml keys (bundleID/displayName/version/
minIOSVersion), IOSOptions fields, and the what-works table (save-file dialog
error, UIPasteboard clipboard, UIDocumentPicker) are all accurate.

* docs(ios): use dark-mode simulator screenshot in the first-app tutorial

* docs(ios): update first-app tutorial simulator screenshot

* fix(v3/android): make android:run work in a normal project (like iOS)

A plain 'wails3 init' app could not run on Android. Four bugs, the same class
as the iOS ones (masked by the in-repo example):

- ensure-emulator had a go-task template with backslash-escaped quotes
  ({{if eq .HOST_ARCH \"arm64\"}}) that fails to parse ('unexpected \ in
  operand'), aborting any android task. Replaced with a precomputed ANDROID_ABI
  var.
- gradlew lost its executable bit when extracted from the embedded build assets
  ('permission denied', exit 127). chmod +x before invoking it.
- the app launched but showed ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED: the c-shared library has
  no main registered because main_android.go (which calls
  application.RegisterAndroidMain in init) was only extracted to build/android/,
  not the main package. Added 'wails3 android overlay:gen' (mirrors iOS
  overlay:gen) to inject main_android.gen.go into the main package via
  -overlay, wired into the c-shared build.
- dropped the bogus common:generate:icons (unused on android, breaks through the
  nested include) and redundant generate:android:bindings (races
  build:frontend's own bindings) deps.

Verified end to end: a fresh 'wails3 init' app builds, installs and renders on
the Android emulator.

* fix(v3/android): robust emulator auto-boot + sync example to overlay approach

- ensure-emulator: start the emulator via 'nohup sh -c "... &"' so it is
  reparented to launchd and survives go-task reaping background jobs (a bare
  'emulator &' is killed before the install/launch steps run); also tolerate the
  logcat grep exiting non-zero.
- example: bring build/android/Taskfile.yml in line with the template (overlay
  wiring, gradlew chmod, dropped bogus deps) and remove the hand-written root
  main_android.go — the build overlay now injects main registration, so the
  example matches what a fresh project generates. Update main.go's comment to
  describe the ios/android overlay mechanism.

Verified on the Android emulator: both a fresh 'wails3 init' app and the
kitchen-sink example build, install and render (dark mode).

* chore(v3/mobile): gitignore generated mobile overlay artifacts

The iOS/Android build overlays (overlay.json + gen/) contain per-machine
absolute paths and are regenerated each build, so they must not be committed.
The example already ignored the iOS ones; add the Android equivalents, and add
both to the fresh-project template .gitignore so 'wails3 init' projects ignore
them too.

* fix(v3/android): robust emulator auto-boot + sync example android Taskfile

(Completes the previous commit, whose git add aborted on an already-removed
path and silently dropped these files.)

- ensure-emulator: daemonize the emulator via 'nohup sh -c "... &"' so it
  survives go-task reaping background jobs; tolerate the logcat grep exiting
  non-zero.
- example: sync build/android/Taskfile.yml with the template (overlay wiring,
  gradlew chmod, dropped bogus deps) and update main.go's comment to describe
  the ios/android overlay mechanism (root main_android.go was already removed).
