platform manager singletons:

  application.IOSShare(...)   -> application.IOS.Share(...)
  application.AndroidHaptic() -> application.Android.Haptic(...)
  application.IOSSetScrollEnabled(...) -> application.IOS.SetScrollEnabled(...)

`application.IOS` / `application.Android` are zero-size singletons that only
exist on their respective builds; all callers live in //go:build ios/android
files.

Rename the mobile bridge events away from the `native:*` prefix:
  - cross-platform events -> `common:*` (common:haptic, common:location, …)
  - iOS-only             -> `ios:*`     (ios:beginBackgroundTask, ios:backgroundTask)
  - Android-only         -> `android:*` (android:foregroundService)

The frontend keeps a single listener per event under `common:*`, matching the
shared-codebase model. Updated the Objective-C/C bridge, the Android Java
bridge (template + committed example build copy), the kitchen-sink example
(Go handlers + frontend), IOS.md/ANDROID.md, the docs-site mobile guides and
the unreleased changelog.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/mobile): emit iOS orientation as a map, not via jsonToMap

IOS.GetOrientation() returns a plain string ('portrait'/'landscape'/…),
not JSON, so jsonToMap() failed to parse it and emitted an empty map.
Wrap it under the 'orientation' key the frontend reads (matching the
Android handler). Caught in CodeRabbit review of #5602.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): prevent crash when camera lacks the requested capture media type

mfPresentCamera set picker.mediaTypes to public.movie/public.image without
checking the camera actually offers that type. On the iOS Simulator (and any
device whose camera reports available but does not support video) the virtual
camera exposes stills only, so requesting video made -[UIImagePickerController
setMediaTypes:] throw an uncaught NSException -> SIGABRT.

Check availableMediaTypesForSourceType: before configuring the picker and emit
a graceful common:capture error instead, with an @try/@catch safety net. Pre-
existing since #5562; surfaced by the Xcode 26 simulator's virtual camera.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): rework camera fix — guard setMediaTypes, don't pre-check media list

Follow-up to ec23d47f: the previous fix pre-checked
availableMediaTypesForSourceType:, but that list is unreliable on the iOS
Simulator — it returns empty even when the camera is authorized and can
present, so the pre-check would wrongly block capture. Verified on-simulator:
the list stays empty across authorization states and a 3s poll, yet photo
capture presents fine.

Instead: photos use the picker's default media type (public.image, never
throws); video opts into public.movie inside an @try/@catch so the
'No available types for source 1' NSException degrades to a graceful
common:capture error instead of SIGABRT. Real devices list public.movie and
record normally.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): quote product-name paths in generated Xcode project

The pbxproj template left the c-archive PBXFileReference path and the build
phase's 'go build -o' path unquoted, so a productName containing a space (the
default config ships 'My Product') produced an invalid project.pbxproj —
Xcode reported 'The project main is damaged ... parse error'. Quote both
paths. Also give the mobile example a real, space-free productName
(KitchenSink) and identifier.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/mobile example): add NSFaceIDUsageDescription; show feedback per control group

- Add NSFaceIDUsageDescription to the iOS Info.plist(s). Tapping Authenticate
  called LAContext biometric evaluation, which hard-crashes on a real device
  without this key (same class as the camera/mic keys). The crash left the app
  white-screening on relaunch; a clean reinstall + this key resolve it.
- Move result feedback out of one box at the bottom of each section into a
  compact inline output beside each control group (Share, Screen, Status bar,
  Security, Secure storage, Haptics, Location, Motion, Speech, Keyboard,
  Camera, Background), so results appear next to the control you tapped.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): reload WebView when iOS terminates the WebContent process

WKWebView's renderer (WebContent) process is reaped by iOS under memory
pressure or after repeated background/foreground and launch cycles. With no
webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate: handler the view stayed permanently
blank — the 'white screen on the 3rd+ launch' reported on device. Implement
the delegate method to reload and respawn the renderer. Framework-level fix;
affects all Wails v3 iOS apps.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): fix cold-launch white screen (double WebView) + launch flash

Two iOS fixes:
- ios_create_webview_with_id manually called -loadView and -viewDidLoad, so
  UIKit ALSO loaded the view automatically — two WebViews/viewDidLoad passes per
  cold launch. Content loaded into one while the blank one was displayed →
  intermittent white screen after force-quit + relaunch. Load the view once via
  -loadViewIfNeeded. Verified on-device: one viewDidLoad per launch, renders
  reliably across repeated force-quit relaunches.
- Also fix the missing withError: parameter on didFailProvisionalNavigation
  (the old selector never matched, so load failures were swallowed) and add a
  didFailNavigation:withError: handler.

Flash: any non-zero IOSOptions.BackgroundColour is now applied to the app
window automatically (no need to also set AppBackgroundColourSet), so the
window matches the web background instead of flashing white before the WebView
paints. The mobile example sets it to its web background (#1b2636).

Refs #5602

* refactor(v3/ios): remove IOSOptions.AppBackgroundColourSet

The flag only existed to distinguish a deliberate fully-transparent app window
({0,0,0,0}) from the unset zero value — but a transparent app-window background
is meaningless (the window needs an opaque backing), so the distinction had no
real use. Drop it and treat any non-zero BackgroundColour as set; the zero
value means unset (defaults to white). Simpler API, one field instead of two.

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): remove white launch flash (launch screen + initial window)

The app declared UILaunchStoryboardName but the build never bundled a compiled
storyboard, so iOS showed a white default launch screen; and the window was
created white in the delegate before Go could apply a background colour. Both
caused a white flash on (cold) launch.

- Add a LaunchBackground colour asset (#1b2636) and switch Info.plist(s) to
  UILaunchScreen { UIColorName = LaunchBackground } — bundled via the asset
  catalog the build already compiles.
- Colour the initial UIWindow/root view from the same LaunchBackground asset in
  didFinishLaunching (timing-independent; falls back to white if absent).

Refs #5602

* fix(v3/ios): show local notifications while app is in foreground

iOS suppresses a local notification's banner while the app that posted it is
in the foreground unless the app registers a UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate
and opts into presentation. Wails registered no such delegate, so notifications
fired but were delivered silently to Notification Center with no banner.

Add an MFNotificationDelegate (UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate) whose
willPresentNotification returns banner+list+sound (alert+sound pre-iOS 14) and
didReceiveNotificationResponse handles taps. Register it via
ios_notifications_init() — both at launch (see delegate change) and defensively
at the top of ios_post_notification so it is set regardless of build path.

The mobile example surfaces the new common:notification {presented}/{tapped}
signals so foreground delivery is visible in the UI.

* fix(v3/ios): finalize cold-launch fix and clean up iOS build templates

Start the Go runtime from the app delegate's didFinishLaunchingWithOptions
(after UIKit has launched) instead of concurrently with UIApplicationMain,
which intermittently corrupted the FrontBoard launch handshake on device
(blank cold launch / 0x8BADF00D). main.m is now a minimal bootstrap; because
it no longer references a Go symbol the archive must be linked with
-Wl,-force_load (set in all iOS Taskfiles) or the WailsAppDelegate class is
dead-stripped.

Also: register the notification delegate before launch finishes; remove the
dead, archive-less build.sh.tmpl (+ rendered copies); align the older
examples/ios bootstrap with the verified examples/mobile pattern; tidy the
example go.mod.

* fix(v3/ios): make ios:run/package work in a normal (non-repo) project

Three bugs prevented a plain 'wails3 init' app from building/running on iOS,
while the in-repo examples masked them:

- overlay:gen read its main_ios.go template from the wails SOURCE TREE via
  repoRoot(); outside the wails repo that path doesn't exist, so it failed with
  'file does not exist'. Read it from the embedded build_assets FS instead
  (same approach as xcode:gen).
- run/deploy-simulator/deploy-device hardcoded a com.wails.<app>[.dev] bundle
  id for simctl/devicectl, but the real id comes from build/config.yml (e.g.
  com.example.<app>). simctl install succeeded but launch failed (code 4). Read
  CFBundleIdentifier from the built bundle's Info.plist instead.
- the iOS build depended on common:generate:icons (icns/ico — not used by iOS,
  and its dir:build broke through the nested include) and a redundant
  generate:ios:bindings that raced build:frontend's own bindings -clean. Both
  removed; iOS icons come from Assets.xcassets via actool and bindings from
  build:frontend.

Verified end-to-end: 'wails3 init' + 'wails3 task ios:run' builds, installs and
launches a default app on the iOS Simulator.

* docs(ios): document the IOS manager pattern + common/ios events; add verified simulator screenshot

- ios.mdx: replace the inaccurate runtime blurb (which mixed Go and JS APIs and
  referenced a non-existent IOS.Scroll.SetEnabled JS call) with proper sections:
  * 'Native device features — the IOS manager': the Go application.IOS.* pattern
    (one-shot actions, JSON query helpers) with correct Haptic values.
  * 'Asynchronous results: common:* and ios:* events': the event model with a
    full table mapping each event to the manager call that triggers it and its
    payload (common:* = shared with Android, ios:* = iOS-only).
  * 'Runtime WebView controls': the Go SetScrollEnabled/... toggles plus the
    real frontend runtime (IOS.Haptics.Impact, IOS.Device.Info).
- first-mobile-app.mdx: add a screenshot of a default 'wails3 init' app running
  on the iOS Simulator, captured by actually running the tutorial end to end.

The tutorial's command sequence (wails3 init -> wails3 task ios:run -> ios:logs:dev
-> ios:xcode) was verified by running it against a fresh project on the Simulator.

* fix(v3/templates): make the default app templates mobile-responsive

On a phone the starter app's 'Wails + <Framework>' heading (font-size: 3.2em)
overflowed and wrapped onto two lines, and content ran to the screen edges
under the notch. Applied the same responsive treatment to every template's
style.css and index.html:

- h1 uses clamp(1.9rem, 8vw, 3.2rem) so it fits one line on phones and stays
  3.2rem on desktop.
- .container gets box-sizing, a 720px max-width and safe-area-aware padding
  (env(safe-area-inset-*)) so content clears the notch/home indicator.
- logos cap at 40vw and shrink on <=480px viewports.
- viewport meta gains viewport-fit=cover so the safe-area insets apply on iOS.

Verified on the iOS Simulator with a fresh 'wails3 init' app: the heading now
renders on a single line. The docs tutorial screenshot is updated to match.

* docs(mobile): correct Go version to 1.25+ and simplify first-run steps

- The mobile guides stated 'Go 1.24+', but the generated project's go.mod (and
  wails/v3) require go 1.25.0. Corrected to 1.25+ in ios, android,
  first-mobile-app and the index requirements table.
- first-mobile-app: replaced the six-bullet technical breakdown of 'wails3 task
  ios:run' (Xcode scaffold, c-archive, GOOS=ios, ad-hoc signing, ...) with a
  single beginner-friendly sentence plus a short 'first run is slow' tip.

Verified against the code: config.yml keys (bundleID/displayName/version/
minIOSVersion), IOSOptions fields, and the what-works table (save-file dialog
error, UIPasteboard clipboard, UIDocumentPicker) are all accurate.

* docs(ios): use dark-mode simulator screenshot in the first-app tutorial

* docs(ios): update first-app tutorial simulator screenshot

* fix(v3/android): make android:run work in a normal project (like iOS)

A plain 'wails3 init' app could not run on Android. Four bugs, the same class
as the iOS ones (masked by the in-repo example):

- ensure-emulator had a go-task template with backslash-escaped quotes
  ({{if eq .HOST_ARCH \"arm64\"}}) that fails to parse ('unexpected \ in
  operand'), aborting any android task. Replaced with a precomputed ANDROID_ABI
  var.
- gradlew lost its executable bit when extracted from the embedded build assets
  ('permission denied', exit 127). chmod +x before invoking it.
- the app launched but showed ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED: the c-shared library has
  no main registered because main_android.go (which calls
  application.RegisterAndroidMain in init) was only extracted to build/android/,
  not the main package. Added 'wails3 android overlay:gen' (mirrors iOS
  overlay:gen) to inject main_android.gen.go into the main package via
  -overlay, wired into the c-shared build.
- dropped the bogus common:generate:icons (unused on android, breaks through the
  nested include) and redundant generate:android:bindings (races
  build:frontend's own bindings) deps.

Verified end to end: a fresh 'wails3 init' app builds, installs and renders on
the Android emulator.

* fix(v3/android): robust emulator auto-boot + sync example to overlay approach

- ensure-emulator: start the emulator via 'nohup sh -c "... &"' so it is
  reparented to launchd and survives go-task reaping background jobs (a bare
  'emulator &' is killed before the install/launch steps run); also tolerate the
  logcat grep exiting non-zero.
- example: bring build/android/Taskfile.yml in line with the template (overlay
  wiring, gradlew chmod, dropped bogus deps) and remove the hand-written root
  main_android.go — the build overlay now injects main registration, so the
  example matches what a fresh project generates. Update main.go's comment to
  describe the ios/android overlay mechanism.

Verified on the Android emulator: both a fresh 'wails3 init' app and the
kitchen-sink example build, install and render (dark mode).

* chore(v3/mobile): gitignore generated mobile overlay artifacts

The iOS/Android build overlays (overlay.json + gen/) contain per-machine
absolute paths and are regenerated each build, so they must not be committed.
The example already ignored the iOS ones; add the Android equivalents, and add
both to the fresh-project template .gitignore so 'wails3 init' projects ignore
them too.

* fix(v3/android): robust emulator auto-boot + sync example android Taskfile

(Completes the previous commit, whose git add aborted on an already-removed
path and silently dropped these files.)

- ensure-emulator: daemonize the emulator via 'nohup sh -c "... &"' so it
  survives go-task reaping background jobs; tolerate the logcat grep exiting
  non-zero.
- example: sync build/android/Taskfile.yml with the template (overlay wiring,
  gradlew chmod, dropped bogus deps) and update main.go's comment to describe
  the ios/android overlay mechanism (root main_android.go was already removed).

commit.message:
fix(v3): move release tags to alpha2.N to fix go-install @latest (#5609)

* fix(v3): switch release tags to alpha2.N series to outrank stray alpha.98-tui tag

A manually-pushed `v3.0.0-alpha.98-tui` tag is stuck as `go install ...@latest`.
In semver, prerelease identifiers split on dots, so `alpha.98-tui` becomes
`alpha` + `98-tui`; because `98-tui` is alphanumeric it always outranks the
numeric `100`/`101`/`102`, so every newer alpha is skipped. The tag cannot be
unpublished (proxy.golang.org cached it permanently), so we must out-rank it.

Bumping the number can never win (any `alpha.N` loses to the alphanumeric
`98-tui`), so move to an `alpha2.N` series: the label `alpha2` > `alpha`
lexically, which wins the first identifier comparison, while the dotted numeric
suffix keeps proper numeric ordering (alpha2.999 < alpha2.1000) and leaves every
split-on-dot parser (release.go, semver, CLI `tool version`) untouched. The
number continues from the legacy series (alpha.102 -> alpha2.102 -> alpha2.103).

- version.txt: v3.0.0-alpha.102 -> v3.0.0-alpha2.102 (next tag: alpha2.103)
- nightly-release-v3.yml: change-detection glob now targets the alpha2.* series
- release_test.go: lock in alpha2 increment + numeric ordering at the digit boundary

Verified with golang.org/x/mod/semver: alpha2.103 > alpha.98-tui and > alpha.102.

* test(v3): assert alpha2.103 outranks stray alpha.98-tui via go's semver

Adds TestAlpha2OutranksStrayTuiTag, which uses golang.org/x/mod/semver (the
exact comparator the go command uses for @latest) to prove the new alpha2.103
tag outranks both the stray alpha.98-tui tag and the legacy alpha.102, and that
the alpha2 series keeps numeric ordering across the 999->1000 boundary.

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): restore size constraints after drag-restoring frameless window (#5559)

* fix(windows): restore size constraints after drag-restoring frameless window

* fix(v3/windows): move constraint options writes inside InvokeSync to eliminate data race

SetMinSize/SetMaxSize were writing w.options.{Min,Max}{Width,Height} directly
on the calling goroutine before any synchronisation, while the new
restoreSavedSizeConstraintOptions() reads/writes the same fields from WndProc
on the Windows message thread — a real data race.

Consolidate all w.options.* writes into a single InvokeSync per setter.
dispatchOnMainThread short-circuits when already on the main thread, so this
is deadlock-free even when called from within EnableSizeConstraints' InvokeSync.

* fix(v3/ci): fix Build Examples CI failure for examples with local replace directives

Go 1.25's stricter module nesting check rejects `go build` when a module uses
`replace github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 => ../..` and the module's directory is
physically inside the replaced module's tree.

Fix: remove standalone go.mod/go.sum from dev, file-association, and
notifications — these examples only depend on wails itself and build correctly
as part of the v3 module.  Remove gin-example, gin-routing, gin-service from
the test:examples task since they require external deps (gin) that cannot be
folded into the v3 module; they remain in test:examples:all for full builds.

---------

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>

fix(webview2): never treat a failed SetSize/PutBounds as fatal (#5597)

PutBounds can fail transiently while the WebView2 browser process is
reconfiguring — the same RESOURCE_NOT_IN_CORRECT_STATE that Eval and
Focus already handle non-fatally. A dropped resize during a DPI
transition or restore-from-minimise is recoverable (the next WM_SIZE
re-asserts bounds); killing the process is not.

Refs #5544

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): remove ResizeDebounceMS and fix resize background painting (#5596)

ResizeDebounceMS delayed WebView2 resizing to improve performance, but
inherently left newly-exposed window areas undrawn for the debounce
period. No mitigation can fully hide the content gap, so the option is
removed — modern WebView2 handles live resize well enough without it.

Also fix WM_ERASEBKGND to fill the client area with the configured
background colour before returning, so any area momentarily not covered
by WebView2 during a resize shows the correct colour instead of white.

Fixes #5594

commit.message:
fix(v3/ci): quote pipe in 'wails3 tool has gcc|clang' Taskfile command (#5600)

* fix(v3/ci): quote pipe in 'wails3 tool has gcc|clang' Taskfile command

The shell in Task's `sh:` var interprets the bare `|` as a pipe, running
`wails3 tool has gcc` and piping its output to `clang`. clang exits 1
with "no input files", failing all Linux template builds.

Fix: wrap the argument in shell double-quotes so the pipe is passed
literally to the Go program, which splits on `|` to check each tool.

Regressed in #5533 (0464978ce).

* fix(v3/generator): disable workspace mode when loading packages for binding generation

Go 1.25 changed behaviour for modules nested inside a Go workspace but not
listed as workspace members: packages.Load returns the package with errors,
leaving TypesInfo.Instances empty. The binding generator then finds zero
services, produces no output, and the frontend vite build fails with
'Cannot find module ../bindings/<pkg>'.

Fix: set GOWORK=off in the packages.Config.Env for both ResolvePatterns
and LoadPackages. The binding generator analyses source code in isolation
and never needs workspace-level module routing; the module's own go.mod
replace directives are still honoured when GOWORK=off.

Fixes all Test Templates CI failures on ubuntu/macos/windows.

* fix(v3/ci): register generated template project in workspace before build

Go 1.25 rejects packages in a module that is nested under the workspace
root but not listed in go.work — packages.Load returns errors that leave
TypesInfo.Instances empty, causing the bindings generator to find zero
services and produce no frontend/bindings/ output.

The template test step creates a new project inside the repo tree (which
is a Go workspace), so the project module is nested but unlisted. Fix by
running 'go work use .' in the generated project directory before
'wails3 build'. This registers the project as a proper workspace member
so Go 1.25 loads its packages correctly and bindings are generated.

Revert the earlier GOWORK=off approach in load.go — disabling workspace
mode in the generator would break local development workflows where
go.work ties v3 and webview2 changes together.

* ci: re-trigger CI run (artifact unavailable after re-run)

commit.message:
fix(v3,linux): enable frameless resize edge detection on Linux (#4680) (#5366)

* fix(v3,linux): enable frameless window resize edge detection on Linux

The resize border detection in drag.ts was gated behind !IsWindows(),
which silently disabled JavaScript edge detection on Linux (and macOS).
On Linux, frameless windows have no WM-managed resize handles, so the
JavaScript path — detect edge → invoke("wails:resize:<edge>") → GTK's
gtk_window_begin_resize_drag() — is the only mechanism available.

When a DOM scrollbar sits at the window's right or bottom edge, the
mouse never leaves the WebView viewport, so clientX/clientY coordinates
are still correct. The capture-phase mousemove listener fires first,
detects the resize zone, and sets resizeEdge. Without this fix, though,
the !IsWindows() guard drops the event and resizeEdge stays empty,
making resize unresponsive regardless of the scrollbar.

Change the guard to !IsWindows() && !IsLinux() so Linux follows the same
JavaScript edge-detection path as Windows, while macOS keeps its current
(native-WM) behaviour unchanged.

Also rebuild runtime.js and runtime.debug.js from the updated source.

Fixes #4680.

CC @leaanthony

Co-authored-by: multica-agent <github@multica.ai>

* fix(linux): propagate setResizable to JS runtime on Linux

The Linux setResizable implementation only called gtk_window_set_resizable
but never notified the JS side via window._wails.setResizable(). This left
the drag.ts `resizable` flag permanently false on Linux, causing the
!resizable guard in onMouseMove to always short-circuit before edge
detection could run — making the frameless resize fix in this PR a no-op.

Apply the same execJS call that the Windows backend already uses. The call
is dispatched asynchronously after wails:runtime:ready fires the
SetResizable init, so window._wails.setResizable is guaranteed to exist
when the JS runs.

Both GTK3 (linux_cgo.go) and GTK4 (linux_cgo_gtk4.go) paths fixed.

Co-authored-by: multica-agent <github@multica.ai>

fix(v3/darwin): resize the drag-and-drop overlay with the window (#5577)

The WebviewDrag overlay view is created at the window's initial size,
and the autoresizing mask intended for it was set on the content view
instead (a no-op — the content view already tracks the window). The
overlay therefore stayed frozen at creation size: files dragged over
any area gained by resizing the window had no drop target under the
cursor and were rejected, exactly as reported.

Set the mask on the drag view itself.

Verified by frame introspection on macOS: before, after SetSize(600,500)
the content view is 600x468 while the drag view remains 299x299; after,
both track. pkg/application suite passes.

Fixes #3743

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): show dialogs with icons in dev builds and keep their buttons (#5576)

* fix(v3/windows): show dialogs with icons in dev builds and keep their buttons

Dialogs with UseAppIcon or a custom Icon called MessageBoxIndirect with
icon resource ID 3 and hardcoded MB_OK|MB_USERICON flags. Two bugs:

1. Dev binaries (go run, wails3 dev) have no embedded icon resource, so
   MessageBoxIndirect failed outright — the dialog never appeared and
   the error was routed to handleFatalError, aborting the app. This is
   the 'dialog does not show' from #4233 (reproduced via the dialogs
   example). The icon path now falls back to a standard MessageBox when
   MessageBoxIndirect fails.

2. The hardcoded MB_OK discarded the computed dialog flags, so question
   dialogs shown with an icon silently lost their Yes/No buttons. The
   flags are now preserved, with only the MB_ICON* bits stripped (the
   user icon replaces the standard icon).

Custom Icon bytes still map to the application icon: MessageBoxIndirect
cannot render arbitrary image bytes; true custom icons need a
TaskDialog implementation, tracked separately.

Verified on Windows: build, new flag test and full pkg/application
suite pass. Visual dialog confirmation needs an interactive session —
requested via the issue.

Fixes #4233

* fix(v3/windows): derive mbIconMask from w32 MB_ICON* constants

commit.message:
fix(v3/runtime): honour subscription changes made during event dispatch (#5574)

* fix(v3/runtime): honour subscription changes made during event dispatch

dispatchWailsEvent filtered its pre-dispatch listener snapshot for
expired (maxCallbacks) listeners and wrote that snapshot back into the
listener map after running the callbacks. Any subscription change made
inside a handler was therefore undone: a listener that unsubscribed
itself (the reported case) was resurrected and fired again on the next
event, and a listener registered during dispatch was silently dropped.

Dispatch still iterates a snapshot, but expired listeners are now
removed individually via listenerOff, which re-reads the live map state
instead of clobbering it.

The new tests fail on the previous implementation (self-removing
listener fires twice; listener added during dispatch never fires) and
pass with the fix. Full suite: 1168 tests green, tsc clean.

This fixes the v3 runtime half of #4393; the original v2 report
(notifyListeners in events.js) has the same write-back pattern and
needs an equivalent fix in the v2 runtime.

Refs #4393

* perf(v3/runtime): batch-remove expired listeners in O(n) instead of O(n²)

* chore: remove UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md to avoid merge conflicts

commit.message:
fix(v3/build): dedupe shared tasks racing in parallel universal builds (#5573)

* fix(v3/build): dedupe shared tasks racing in parallel universal builds

darwin:build:universal runs its amd64 and arm64 builds as task deps,
which go-task executes in parallel. Each arch build's dependency chain
runs common:build:frontend, so a single universal build executed the
whole frontend pipeline twice concurrently: one invocation regenerates
frontend/bindings (with -clean=true deleting the directory first) while
the other's bundler is reading it, failing intermittently with
'Could not resolve "./bindings/<pkg>"' — most often on slow CI
runners. Two go:mod:tidy processes also raced on go.mod.

Mark the shared, arch-independent tasks (go:mod:tidy,
install:frontend:deps, build:frontend, generate:bindings,
generate:icons) as run:once so concurrent invocations with identical
vars deduplicate. Side benefit: universal builds now run the frontend
pipeline once instead of twice.

Verified with scaffolded apps on macOS: a universal build from the old
template executes 'wails3 generate bindings' and the frontend bundle
twice (the race window); from the patched template exactly once, and
lipo reports a correct x86_64+arm64 binary.

Existing projects pick this up via 'wails3 update build-assets'.

Fixes #4637

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): resync WebView2 rasterization scale after minimise/restore (#5572)

* fix(v3/windows): resync WebView2 rasterization scale after minimise/restore

Wails runs WebView2 in raw-pixels bounds mode with
ShouldDetectMonitorScaleChanges disabled, which makes the rasterization
scale the application's responsibility — but nothing ever set it after
controller creation. While a window is minimised it is parked at
(-32000,-32000), which on mixed-DPI systems can re-associate it with a
different monitor's DPI; on restore nothing corrected the scale, so
window.devicePixelRatio kept the wrong monitor's value (e.g. 1.25 on a
200% display) and content rendered at the wrong size until a manual
resize forced a resync. Reproduced consistently by the reporter on a
200%/125% dual-monitor setup, including with
DisableFramelessWindowDecorations enabled.

Add resyncWebviewRasterizationScale(), invoked on restore-from-minimise
and in the WM_DPICHANGED handler (the natural owner of scale updates
now that auto-detection is off). It is a no-op when the controller is
unavailable or the scale already matches, so single-DPI setups are
unaffected.

Verified: build and pkg/application suite pass on Windows; vet output
identical to master. Mixed-DPI behaviour needs a physical multi-monitor
setup — reporter verification requested on the issue.

Fixes #5544

* fix(v3/windows): don't apply DPI suggested rect while minimised

Verification on a 200%/125% mixed-DPI setup showed the rasterization
scale now recovers on restore, but the window bounds did not: a
WM_DPICHANGED delivered while the window is parked at (-32000,-32000)
carries a suggested rect scaled for the wrong monitor, and applying it
rewrites the window's restore bookkeeping (a maximised 1920x1080 window
came back as 3072x1728). Skip the suggested-rect resize while
minimised; the scale resync still runs, and a fresh WM_DPICHANGED with
a correct rect arrives if the DPI genuinely differs on restore.

* fix(v3/windows): resync DPI on un-minimise to maximised + force bounds re-put

Reporter verification round 2 (200%/125% hardware) showed two gaps:

1. Their window is maximised, so leaving the minimised state delivers
   WM_SIZE with SIZE_MAXIMIZED, not SIZE_RESTORED — the resync hook
   never ran on that path. Both transitions now share
   resyncWebviewDPIAfterMinimise.

2. Re-putting the rasterization scale alone does not make WebView2
   re-lay out content whose bounds are unchanged: dpr recovered but the
   page kept sizes computed with the stale scale (3072x1728 instead of
   1920x1080) until a manual resize re-asserted bounds. When the resync
   actually corrects a drifted scale, the current bounds are now
   re-put via chromium.Resize() to force the re-layout.

Refs #5544

* fix(v3/windows): compare rasterization scale with a tolerance

Review follow-up (#5544): GetRasterizationScale returns a float that may
not be bit-identical to dpi/96 for non-25% DPI steps, so an exact ==
could re-Put the scale on every resync. Use a small tolerance.

commit.message:
fix(v3/runtime): make @wailsio/runtime importable without a DOM (#5571)

* fix(v3/runtime): make @wailsio/runtime importable without a DOM

Importing @wailsio/runtime during server-side rendering (e.g. Next.js
'output: export' prerendering via next build) threw
'ReferenceError: window is not defined': several modules touched
window/document at module scope — runtime.ts computed the runtime URL
from window.location at import, drag.ts constructed a MouseEvent,
installed listeners and started a setInterval poll, and
calls/events/dialogs/contextmenu/utils/index performed window._wails
setup and listener registration as import side effects.

Add an environment.ts hasDOM guard and put every import-time DOM access
behind it; the runtime URL is now resolved lazily on first call. With a
DOM present, behaviour is unchanged (all webview init still runs at
import). Without one, the package imports cleanly and Wails APIs simply
remain non-functional, which is the correct semantic for prerendering.

New ssr_import.test.js runs vitest in a bare Node environment and
imports the full module graph: it fails with the ReferenceError on the
old code and passes with the guards. Full suite: 1166 tests pass.

Fixes #4679

* fix(v3/runtime): guard System.invoke and androidBridge init behind hasDOM

* chore: remove UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md to avoid merge conflicts

commit.message:
fix(v3): reject the call instead of crashing when a bound method panics (#5570)

* fix(v3): reject the call instead of crashing when a bound method panics

A panic inside a user's bound service method was recovered by
handlePanic, whose default path is globalApplication.fatal — printing
the catastrophic-failure banner and exiting the process. A bug in one
bound method (e.g. a nil dereference triggered by an HMR-driven call)
therefore took down the entire application, and with a custom
PanicHandler registered the call returned (nil, nil), leaving the
frontend promise to resolve with null.

BoundMethod.Call now converts a recovered panic into a *CallError with
Kind RuntimeError, so the frontend call rejects with a message naming
the method. A registered PanicHandler still observes the panic
(logging/telemetry); without one the panic and stack are logged through
the application logger instead of the fatal path.

The new tests die with the catastrophic-failure banner under the old
behaviour and pass with the fix.

Fixes #5037

* fix(v3): address review feedback on bound-method panic handling

- Compute the panic stack trace only when globalApplication is non-nil:
  it is only consumed by the logger / PanicHandler, while the returned
  CallError carries just the message. Avoids unnecessary work when
  application.New() has not been called.
- Add an internal regression test covering the custom-PanicHandler path:
  asserts the handler is invoked AND Call still returns a
  *CallError{Kind: RuntimeError}. This is the half of #5037 where the
  pre-fix code returned (nil, nil), and the external test could not
  reach it (the handler must be installed on the global singleton).

Refs #5037

commit.message:
fix(v3/darwin): make RelativePosition mirror SetRelativePosition on both axes (#5569)

* fix(v3/darwin): make RelativePosition mirror SetRelativePosition on both axes

windowGetRelativePosition returned the window's absolute X
(frame.origin.x, missing the screenFrame.origin.x subtraction) and
computed Y without the screen's origin.y term, while
windowSetRelativePosition treats both coordinates as screen-relative.
As a result SetRelativePosition(RelativePosition()) moved the window on
any screen whose NSScreen origin is not (0,0) — i.e. every non-primary
screen. The Y drift was previously masked on side-by-side arrangements
(origin.y == 0) but is just as real on stacked ones.

Get now mirrors Set exactly on both axes.

Verified on a two-display Mac (Retina primary + external above): before
the fix a round-trip on the secondary screen teleported the window by
(489, -120); after, the position is stable and Position() is unchanged.

Both functions keep using the screen frame (not visibleFrame); whether
"relative" should mean WorkArea-relative is tracked separately in the
issue.

Fixes #5408

* fix(v3/darwin): clarify windowGetRelativePosition comment

computed Y without the screen's origin.y term, while
windowSetRelativePosition treats both coordinates as screen-relative.
As a result SetRelativePosition(RelativePosition()) moved the window on
any screen whose NSScreen origin is not (0,0) — i.e. every non-primary
screen. The Y drift was previously masked on side-by-side arrangements
(origin.y == 0) but is just as real on stacked ones.

Get now mirrors Set exactly on both axes.

Verified on a two-display Mac (Retina primary + external above): before
the fix a round-trip on the secondary screen teleported the window by
(489, -120); after, the position is stable and Position() is unchanged.

Both functions keep using the screen frame (not visibleFrame); whether
"relative" should mean WorkArea-relative is tracked separately in the
issue.

Fixes #5408

commit.message:
fix(v3/linux): repair purego assetserver backend compile errors (#5564)

* fix(v3/linux): repair purego assetserver backend compile errors

The purego (CGO-free) Linux assetserver backend had rotted against the
cgo backends and no longer compiled:

- webkit2_purego.go registered six different libwebkit/libsoup functions
  into the wrong Go function variables (copy-paste of &unRef / &getUri),
  so even where it compiled it would have called the wrong symbols.
- webkit_uri_scheme_response_new was registered as returning string
  instead of a GObject pointer.
- soup_* symbols were resolved through the libgtk-3 handle, which does
  not link libsoup; they now resolve through the libwebkit2gtk handle.
- SoupMessageHeadersIter was modelled as a 12-byte buffer; it is
  declared as gpointer dummy[3] in libsoup. Out-params now use
  *[3]uintptr / *uintptr with a manual C-string conversion, since
  purego's automatic string marshalling only applies to by-value args.
- The bottom half of the file was raw cgo code (undefined C, io,
  unsafe identifiers) for a request-body reader that the purego request
  implementation never calls (it returns http.NoBody); removed.
- responseWriter.Finish() did not match the ResponseWriter interface
  (missing error return) and leaked the GInputStream it created; a
  compile-time interface assertion now guards against future drift.
- finishWithError registered g_error_new_literal with a wrong arity and
  passed a hardcoded quark; it now mirrors the cgo implementation.

GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 go build/vet -tags purego now passes for
internal/assetserver/webview on amd64 and arm64.

Note: pkg/application still does not compile under purego because the
linuxApp platform layer has no purego port; see #5550 for the scope
assessment.

Refs #5550

* fix(v3/linux): unexport internal soupMessageHeadersResponse constant

* chore: remove UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md to avoid merge conflicts

commit.message:
v3: convert tool has-cc to generic tool has <target> (#5533)

* v3: convert tool has-cc to generic tool has <target>

Replaces `wails3 tool has-cc` with `wails3 tool has cc` — a generic
subcommand that accepts the capability name as a positional argument.
Easier to extend for future capability checks without adding new subcommands.

- Rename HasCCOptions → HasOptions with pos:"1" Tool field
- Rename ToolHasCC → ToolHas, dispatch on opts.Tool with error on unknown
- Update main.go registration from "has-cc" to "has"
- Update linux Taskfile template to use `wails3 tool has cc`
- Update test to cover both the cc case and unknown-tool error path

* v3: tool has -- fall back to PATH lookup for unknown names

Instead of erroring on unrecognised tool names, do a plain exec.LookPath
so `wails3 tool has git`, `wails3 tool has node`, etc. all work without
needing explicit cases.  "cc" keeps its special logic (gcc OR clang).

* v3: keep has-cc as deprecated alias forwarding to has cc

Restores `wails3 tool has-cc` as a thin wrapper around `ToolHas` so
existing scripts and Taskfiles outside the generated templates continue
to work. The implementation simply calls ToolHas(&HasOptions{Tool: "cc"}).

* v3: tool has -- use pipe separator instead of cc special case

Replace the hardcoded "cc" alias with a generic pipe-separated syntax:
`wails3 tool has gcc|clang` checks for gcc OR clang in PATH.

- Remove the "cc" switch case; split on "|" and LookPath each alternative
- Update has-cc alias to forward to gcc|clang instead of cc
- Update Taskfile template to use `wails3 tool has gcc|clang`
- Update descriptions and tests accordingly

* v3: build warning reporter + has-cc deprecation notice

Introduces internal/buildwarnings: a lightweight file-based channel that
lets subprocess tool commands (e.g. wails3 tool has-cc) append warnings
that are then printed together at the end of the build.

How it works:
- wrapTask() creates a temp file and sets WAILS_WARNINGS_FILE in the
  process environment before running any task. Child processes inherit it.
- buildwarnings.Add(source, message) appends a tab-separated record to
  the file. No-ops when WAILS_WARNINGS_FILE is unset.
- buildwarnings.FlushAndPrint() reads, pretty-prints, and removes the file.
  Called in wrapTask's defer (success path) and in fatal() before os.Exit
  (failure path), so warnings surface regardless of build outcome.

ToolHasCC now calls buildwarnings.Add("tool has-cc", "...") before
forwarding to ToolHas, so any project still using wails3 tool has-cc
will see a deprecation notice at the end of their next build.

Docs: add tool has, tool has-cc (deprecated), tool lipo, tool capabilities,
and tool docker-mounts to the CLI reference.

* v3: tool has -- validate empty arg; deterministic tests with stub executable

Address Copilot review comments:
- Return an error when the tool argument is empty or whitespace-only,
  so `wails3 tool has` (missing arg) fails clearly rather than
  silently printing "false" and exiting 0.
- Rewrite TestToolHas to create a stub executable in a temp dir and
  prepend it to PATH, so every assertion checks the exact output
  ("true"/"false") against a controlled environment rather than
  relying on whatever tools happen to be installed on the host.

* v3: wrapTask -- restore WAILS_WARNINGS_FILE after each invocation

os.Setenv is process-wide; without a restore the env var leaks across
back-to-back wrapTask calls (visible in tests). Capture the prior value
with os.LookupEnv before setting and restore (Setenv/Unsetenv) in the
same deferred closure that calls FlushAndPrint.

* v3: ToolHas -- guard against nil opts

The empty-Tool check was already added; extend the same condition to
cover a nil opts pointer so ToolHas never reaches opts.Tool on a nil
receiver.

* v3: make ToolHasCC alias check fully deterministic in tests

The alias check previously only asserted out1 == out2 without asserting
the actual value — still the same pattern flagged by the review comment.
Add a gcc stub to the same temp dir so both ToolHasCC and
ToolHas("gcc|clang") are guaranteed to output exactly "true", regardless
of what the host has installed.

Introduces v3/internal/git, a thin stdlib-only wrapper around the
system git executable, covering HeadHash, Clone, Init, RemoteAdd and

Three tests in desktop/events.test.js read mock invocations via
window.WailsInvoke.calls, which is the pre-1.0 vitest/jest spy shape;
modern vitest exposes them at .mock.calls, so the property was
undefined and the tests failed on every run ('should emit an event'
and both EventsOff/EventsOffAll cases). The suite has been red on
master independent of any product change.

Use .mock.calls. All 11 tests now pass; no product code touched.

commit.message:
fix(v2/runtime): honour EventsOff made during event dispatch (#5578)

* fix(v2/runtime): honour EventsOff made during event dispatch

notifyListeners iterated a snapshot of the listener list, spliced
expired (max-callback) listeners out of the snapshot, and then wrote
the snapshot back into eventListeners. Any subscription change made
inside a callback was therefore undone: EventsOff (or the cancel
function returned by EventsOn) called from within a handler was
reverted — the listener fired again on the next event — and listeners
registered during dispatch were dropped. This is the v2 half of #4393;
the v3 dispatcher had inherited the same pattern and was fixed in
PR #5574.

Expired listeners are now removed from the live list instead of
clobbering it with the snapshot. Bundled runtime assets rebuilt.

Note: desktop/events.test.js has 3 pre-existing failures on master
(unrelated WailsInvoke mock drift); the two new regression tests fail
on the old implementation and pass with this fix, with no change to
the pre-existing failures.

Fixes #4393

* fix(v2/runtime): use listenerOff helper in dispatch; add test for listeners registered during dispatch

commit.message:
fix(v3/windows): keep DWM animations when SetFrameless(true) is called (#5582)

* fix(v3/windows): keep DWM animations when SetFrameless(true) is called

Windows created with Frameless: true keep the full WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW
style and have the frame trimmed in WM_NCCALCSIZE, which preserves DWM
minimise/restore/maximise animations, Aero snap and resize borders. The
runtime SetFrameless(true) path instead switched the window to a bare
WS_VISIBLE|WS_POPUP style, silently dropping the styles those behaviours
are keyed on — reporter confirmed all window animations disappear after
calling SetFrameless(true), including in the repo's frameless example.

Keep WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW in both states (the WM_NCCALCSIZE handler is
keyed on options.Frameless, which the caller updates before invoking the
impl), and re-apply the DisableResize-derived WS_THICKFRAME state since
WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW includes it unconditionally.

Verified: build + pkg/application suite on Windows. Behavioural
verification (animations) requested from the reporter, who has a
same-day verification loop going.

Fixes #5541

* fix(v3/windows): preserve window state and button styles in setFrameless

Preserve the live GWL_STYLE state/button bits instead of overwriting them
with a blanket WS_VISIBLE|WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW. The blanket write cleared the
WS_MAXIMIZE/WS_MINIMIZE state bits and re-enabled the minimise/maximise/close
buttons even when disabled via options or the runtime setters.

commit.message:
fix(v3): handle getUserMedia via a cross-platform Permissions map (Linux + Windows) (#5567)

* fix(v3/linux): allow getUserMedia by handling WebKitGTK permission requests

On Linux, navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia() always rejected with
NotAllowedError because WebKitGTK denies any permission request that no
permission-request signal handler claims, and Wails never connected one.
Applications had no way to intercept the request themselves, so camera
and microphone access was impossible — even with full OS-level access to
the devices.

Connect permission-request in both the GTK3 (webkit2gtk-4.1) and GTK4
(webkitgtk-6.0) backends and allow WebKitUserMediaPermissionRequest.
This matches the other platforms: Windows grants all WebView2
permissions by default (WindowOptions.Windows.Permissions can override),
and macOS defers to the OS-level prompt. All other permission kinds
return FALSE, keeping WebKit's default handling (deny).

Verified end-to-end on Linux (Ubuntu, WebKitGTK 4.1) under xvfb with
WebKit mock capture devices: getUserMedia({audio:true}) fails with
NotAllowedError on master and returns a live stream with this change.
gtk3 + gtk4 builds and the pkg/application test suite pass.

Fixes #5552

* fix(v3): handle getUserMedia via a cross-platform Permissions map (Linux + Windows)

Replaces the unconditional camera/microphone grant on Linux with a
declarative, cross-platform policy. A new
WebviewWindowOptions.Permissions map[PermissionType]Permission lets apps
allow/deny capabilities per kind:

  Permissions: map[application.PermissionType]application.Permission{
      application.PermissionMicrophone: application.PermissionDeny,
  }

PermissionType (uint8): Microphone, Camera, Geolocation, Notifications,
ClipboardRead. Permission (uint8): Default=0, Allow=1, Deny=2 — values
kept in step with the WebView2 permission-state ABI so the Windows
backend needs no value translation.

Linux (WebKitGTK, gtk3 + gtk4): the permission-request handler now reads
the map and allows/denies per the requested device types (audio→
Microphone, video→Camera). WebKitGTK has no native prompt, so
PermissionDefault allows media capture — preserving the getUserMedia fix
from #5552 — while PermissionDeny turns it off.

Windows (WebView2): the cross-platform map is applied via SetPermission
(translating kinds); the existing Windows.Permissions map still works and
overrides individual kinds.

Verified on Linux (Ubuntu, WebKitGTK 4.1, gtk3, mock capture devices):
default → getUserMedia GRANTED, PermissionDeny → NotAllowedError. Builds:
darwin, windows (CGO_ENABLED=0), and linux gtk3+gtk4; gtk3 pkg/application
suite passes under xvfb.

Fixes #5552

* fix(v3/windows): don't let the global permission override the Permissions map

WebView2's PermissionRequested handler checks the global permission
before the per-kind map, and setupChromium unconditionally called
SetGlobalPermission(Allow). That made both the new cross-platform
Permissions map and the pre-existing Windows.Permissions map dead on
Windows: a configured PermissionDeny was silently ignored because every
request resolved to the global Allow first.

Only set the blanket allow-all when no per-kind policy is configured, so
unconfigured apps keep their previous auto-allow behaviour while apps
that set Permissions actually have them honoured (unset kinds fall
through to PermissionDefault → the platform's native prompt).

Surfaced by review on #5567.

commit.message:
feat: add go workspace for cross-module development

Adds go.work covering v3 and webview2, enabling contributors to modify
both modules in the same PR without first publishing a new webview2 release.

The problem: any PR touching webview2/ and v3/ simultaneously (like #5462)
failed CI because v3/go.mod pinned a published webview2 version that didn't
include the PR's changes. The only workaround was to release webview2 first,
then bump v3 — a painful two-step dance.

Changes:
- Add go.work + go.work.sum (removed from .gitignore so CI picks them up)
- Remove GOWORK=off from build-and-test-v3.yml test_go and test_templates
  so PR CI resolves webview2 from the local workspace tree
- Add webview2/**, go.work, go.work.sum to PR trigger paths so webview2
  changes correctly trigger the v3 test suite
- Update cache-dependency-path to include all module sums for better cache hits
- Release workflows (nightly-release-v3, release-webview2, bump-webview2-v3)
  retain GOWORK=off so releases pin exact published versions
- cross-compile-test-v3 retains GOWORK=off pending Docker mount integration

fix(fossa): exclude v3/examples npm targets from license scan (#5497)

Example-app frontends are demo/development tooling and are not
distributed as part of the Wails Go module or @wailsio/runtime.
Adding them to the FOSSA exclude list keeps the compliance posture
focused on distributed artifacts and prevents spurious failures when
example frontends pull in new platform-specific package binaries
that FOSSA has not yet reviewed for this project.

Co-authored-by: Lea Anthony <lea.anthony@gmail.com>
