feat(mobile): iOS and Android support for Wails v3 (experimental) (#5562)

* chore(mobile): scaffold iOS/Android command templates

Baseline iOS/Android command-template directories that the mobile support
commits build upon (wails3 project scaffolding for mobile targets).

* fix(ios): GOOS=ios compile regressions + example bindings import

- export events.IOS (was unexported iOS; events_common_ios.go references it)
- define androidMethodNames stub on ios (messageprocessor.go references it
  unconditionally; mobile_stub is !ios && !android)
- examples/ios: bindings generate to ./bindings/ios-example (module name),
  not the template default ./bindings/changeme

* feat(ios): runtime correctness + native dialogs/clipboard/screens

Core fixes:
- single initial navigation: drop hardcoded loadRequest in viewDidLoad and
  manual loadView/viewDidLoad calls (page loaded twice, losing the
  wails:runtime:ready handshake); Go's window run() now loads the start URL
- runtime-ready hardening: first /wails/runtime request marks the window
  ready, so Go->JS events/ExecJS work even if the postMessage handshake is
  dropped during load
- replace the 2s startup sleep with a launch signal from the app delegate;
  ApplicationDidFinishLaunching is emitted Go-side after listeners are wired
- real hasListeners backed by a Go registry fed from app/window .on();
  delete pkg/events events_ios.go (duplicate C symbol + OOB array)
- free the C string in execJS (leaked on every Go->JS call)

Features:
- dialogs: UIAlertController message dialogs with button callbacks;
  UIDocumentPickerViewController open file/files/directory (files imported
  as sandbox copies); save dialogs return an explicit unsupported error
- clipboard: UIPasteboard-backed setText/text
- screens: real UIScreen metrics (points, pixels, scale, safe-area work area)

Hygiene:
- framework diagnostics gated behind debug builds (Go const + native
  WailsVLog); production builds are quiet
- GOOS=ios now compiles all of ./pkg/...: notifications/dock/updater/mac/
  doctor-ng darwin files no longer leak into iOS builds (ios implies the
  darwin build tag); added iOS fallbacks where needed

* feat(ios): device builds, signing, entitlements, IPA packaging, devicectl deploy

- Taskfile platform parameterisation: IOS_PLATFORM=simulator|device picks
  SDK (iphonesimulator|iphoneos), target triple and version-min flags;
  MIN_IOS_VERSION configurable (also via ios.minIOSVersion in config.yml,
  templated into Info.plist); armv7 dropped from UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities
- CODESIGN_IDENTITY (default ad-hoc), optional PROVISIONING_PROFILE embedded
  into device bundles, entitlements applied to device builds only (simulator
  bundles with entitlements are refused by SpringBoard - found the example's
  stale macOS-keyed entitlements.plist doing exactly that; replaced template
  and example with iOS-appropriate content)
- package now links the executable (the old flow shipped whatever stale
  binary happened to be in bin/), package:ipa produces a Payload zip,
  deploy-device installs+launches via xcrun devicectl
- fix webview_window_darwin_production.go build tag: production iOS builds
  never compiled (tag matched ios via implied darwin)
- ensure-simulator no longer hardcodes 'iPhone 15 Pro' when creating a device

Verified: simulator production package installs+launches with working
events/dialogs/bridge; device package produces LC_BUILD_VERSION platform 2
(PLATFORM_IOS) minos 15.0 binary; ipa contains signed Payload bundle.

* docs(ios)+chore: honest iOS guide, doctor checks, remove stale scratch scripts

- IOS.md: accurate status matrix, simulator/device quickstart, signing and
  IPA flow, config keys, porting notes; replaces the drifted
  IOS_ARCHITECTURE/IOS_RUNTIME/IOS_FEATURES_TODO docs
- examples/ios README: iOS quickstart section
- wails3 doctor now reports Xcode and iOS simulator/device SDKs on macOS
- delete repo-root scratch artifacts: build_ios.sh, test-new-ios-build.sh,
  verify-ios-setup.sh, fix-darwin-ios-constraints.sh, test-ios-compilation.go,
  test-assets/

* chore(ios): regenerate example Info.plist (templated min version, armv7 dropped)

* docs(ios): add iOS guide to the docs site + changelog entries

- new Building & Packaging guide at /guides/build/ios (experimental badge):
  simulator/device workflow, signing, IPA, configuration, status matrix,
  porting notes; registered in the sidebar
- iOS entries in UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md (Added + Fixed)

Verified: astro build succeeds (1387 pages) and emits /guides/build/ios/.

* feat(android): runtime correctness + native dialogs/clipboard/screens/haptics

- events: generate iOS+Android event mappings from events.txt (generate:events
  now emits var IOS/var Android blocks, android: entries in eventToJS and
  event_types.ts; .m post-processing preserves blank lines; template carried
  the old 'var iOS' name that broke GOOS=ios builds on regen)
- fix build-tag leaks into GOOS=android: linux_cgo.c/.h, events_linux.go/.h,
  environment_linux.go now carry !android (android implies the linux tag);
  delete dead pkg/events/events_android.go (out-of-bounds MAX_EVENTS array)
- application_android.go rewrite: generic JNI call layer (attach/detach safe,
  exception-checked, leak-free), logcat-routed logging gated by
  androidVerboseLogging (debug/production consts), typed lifecycle events
  (ActivityCreated/Started/Resumed/Paused/Stopped/LowMemory, WebViewPage*),
  setupCommonEvents wired in the cgo path, launch event emitted after
  listener registration
- runtime handshake fixed: JS invoke messages route into windowMessageBuffer
  (plain 'wails:runtime:ready' passthrough mirrors iOS HandleJSMessage) +
  synthetic ready on first /wails/runtime request; the old broken
  runtime.Core() injection at onPageFinished is gone (the bundled runtime
  self-detects the Android JavascriptInterface at document start)
- real dialogs (AlertDialog with button-role mapping + >3-button list,
  SAF document picker with copy-to-cache for real paths; save dialogs error
  with guidance), clipboard (ClipboardManager), screens (WindowMetrics +
  system-bar insets, dp/px split), main-thread dispatch (main looper),
  haptics/toast/device-info runtime methods
- Java bridge: lifecycle forwarding (onStart/Stop/LowMemory), file picker
  via ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT, debug-gated logging, VIBRATE permission;
  synced across internal/commands, build_assets and examples
- nocgo variant kept API-identical for tooling builds (bindings generation)

* feat(android): JavascriptInterface runtime transport + screen manager wiring

The Android WebView does not deliver fetch() POST bodies to
shouldInterceptRequest, so the default HTTP runtime transport never reached
Go (a bindings call SIGSEGV'd reading a nil request body). Add an Android
transport that routes runtime calls through window.wails.invokeAsync to a new
nativeHandleRuntimeCall JNI export, with responses delivered via
window._wailsAndroidCallback. The runtime auto-installs it when the
JavascriptInterface bridge is detected (internal/runtime .../runtime.ts).

- nativeHandleRuntimeCall → handleRuntimeCallForAndroid: parses the call
  envelope and drives a per-app MessageProcessor, returning
  {ok,data|text|error}
- serveAssetForAndroid now sets req.Body = http.NoBody (handlers reached via
  ServeHTTP assume the server's non-nil-Body guarantee)
- WailsJSBridge.invokeAsync rewired to handleRuntimeCall; callback target is
  window._wailsAndroidCallback
- populate ScreenManager at startup + lazily (LayoutScreens), matching the
  desktop platforms — Screens.GetAll returned nil before; screen_android.go
  now supplies PhysicalWorkArea so WorkArea scales correctly

Verified on the API 34 arm64 emulator: assets load, JS→Go bindings render
'Hello Android!', Go→JS time events tick, native AlertDialog shows, clipboard
round-trips, Device.Info + Screens.GetAll return real data (412x915 dp,
WorkArea 412x839).

* docs(android): ANDROID.md + docs-site guide, doctor checks, changelog

- ANDROID.md: status matrix, quickstart, signing/release, porting notes,
  architecture; replaces the pre-implementation ANDROID_ARCHITECTURE.md
  scratch doc
- docs site: guides/build/android page (Experimental badge) + sidebar entry
- wails3 doctor: report Android SDK, platform-tools, NDK and JDK (cross-platform)
- examples/android: README pointing at ANDROID.md
- changelog: Added/Fixed Android entries

* chore(android example): untrack Task/Gradle build caches, add to .gitignore

The Task runner cache (.task/) and the Gradle problems report
(build/android/build/) were accidentally tracked; ignore them and remove
them from version control (the files remain on disk).

* fix(ios): add MinIOSVersion to build-asset config structs

The iOS Info.plist templates reference {{.MinIOSVersion}}, but the generic
build-asset generator renders all templates against BuildConfig/UpdateConfig,
which lacked the field — failing TestGenerateBuildAssets/TestUpdateBuildAssets
(internal/commands) on all platforms. Add MinIOSVersion (default 15.0) to
BuildAssetsOptions and UpdateBuildAssetsOptions so the templates resolve.

* fix(mobile): address PR review (Copilot + CodeRabbit)

Artifacts:
- examples/ios: untrack generated build/ios/xcode/overlay.json + gen/ (they
  held an absolute developer path) and gitignore them
- replace the text-placeholder icon.png files with a real 1024x1024 PNG
- regenerate the android example package-lock to match package.json ("latest");
  it had pinned a local file: path, breaking npm ci

Security / correctness:
- android: drop usesCleartextTraffic from the manifest (assets are served
  in-process over https://wails.localhost)
- ios: nil-guard the document-picker path callback (iosOpenFileCallback)
- ios: only take security-scoped access for directory (in-place) picks, not
  for asCopy file imports (avoids leaking scoped-resource handles)
- android: getScreen() returns an explicit error instead of (nil, nil)
- android: synchronize the file-picker check-and-set (MainActivity)
- android: guard native callbacks (dialog/file-picker/main-thread) so they
  no-op after shutdown() tears down the Go side
- android: treat an empty ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE as "unsigned" in build.gradle
- runtime(android transport): delete the pending entry if invokeAsync throws
  synchronously, so the callback map can't leak

Cross-platform / cleanup:
- doctor: detect the Android SDK on Windows (LOCALAPPDATA) and look for
  adb.exe; android Taskfile SDK fallback now covers Linux (~/Android/Sdk)
- ios Xcode project: SDKROOT=iphoneos (was iphonesimulator, which blocked
  device builds from Xcode) and always rebuild the Go c-archive (the old
  existence check served stale binaries when .go sources changed)
- android: remove the dead getMimeType() helper in WailsPathHandler

Android Java/manifest/gradle/Taskfile changes are synced across the example,
internal/commands, and build_assets copies.

* feat(examples): cross-platform mobile kitchen-sink demo

A single Wails v3 app that runs on iOS, Android and desktop from one main.go
and one adaptive frontend, exercising the full runtime surface:

- Bindings: JS->Go service calls (values, structs, error propagation)
- Events: Go->JS (time clock) and JS->Go->JS (ping/pong)
- Dialogs: native Info/Warning/Error/Question with callbacks
- System: clipboard round-trip, screen metrics, device info
- Native: iOS haptics + WKWebView toggles, Android vibrate + toast

The UI feature-detects the platform and shows only the controls each one
supports; navigation uses an in-page tab bar so the UX is identical
everywhere (no native iOS tab bar to avoid a second, divergent nav).

Also adds the Android runtime JS module (Runtime.Android.Haptics.Vibrate,
Device.Info, Toast.Show) mirroring Runtime.IOS, plus objectNames.Android, so
the frontend can call Android-native methods the same way as iOS.

Verified: built + launched on the API 34 Android emulator (every feature
exercised via CDP, including Go-error propagation and the native AlertDialog
callback) and on the iOS 26.5 simulator (renders, platform detection, runtime
bindings).

* fix(ios): apply SDKROOT/prebuild fix to the shipped pbxproj template

The earlier review fix edited the static internal/commands/ios/project.pbxproj,
but `wails3 ios xcode:gen` actually renders the project from
updatable_build_assets/ios/project.pbxproj.tmpl. Apply the same fixes there so
generated projects get them: SDKROOT=iphoneos (Xcode auto-selects the
simulator SDK for simulator destinations; the old hardcoded iphonesimulator
blocked device builds) and always rebuild the Go c-archive (the old
existence-only check served stale binaries after .go edits).

* feat(mobile): scroll off by default; enabling it adds a scrollable section

The mobile demo's iOS scroll toggle defaulted on but the page had nothing
to scroll, so scroll/bounce could not be exercised. Default scroll off and,
when it is turned on, append a tall filler section to the bottom of the page
so there is real content to scroll and rubber-band against; turning scroll
off removes the section (and the native scrollView) again.

* fix(mobile): align Bindings buttons and inputs to the Greet row

The Greet/Add/Divide buttons sized to their label text, so the button
column and the inputs beside them did not line up. Pin those three buttons
to a uniform width; with flex inputs the single Greet input and the Add/
Divide input pair then share the same left and right edges.

* fix(ios): populate ScreenManager so Screens.* returns data

Screens.GetAll()/GetPrimary() read from the ScreenManager, which is filled
by LayoutScreens(). Desktop platforms call that from their event loop and
Android from startup, but iOS never did — so Screens.* runtime calls
returned null. Populate it in the iOS app's run(), mirroring Android;
getScreens() always yields at least a fallback screen so this is safe.

* feat(mobile): card-render screen/device metrics, scrollable page, logo ratio

- Render Screen and Device info as labelled key/value cards instead of raw
  JSON, so they read cleanly and fit without an unscrollable blob.
- Make the content area (main) a scrollable region inside a viewport-height
  app shell, with the header/tabs/footer pinned, so long panes scroll.
- Stop forcing the header logo to a 44x44 square; fix its height and let the
  width follow so it keeps its 320x253 aspect ratio.

* fix(mobile): make iOS Scroll/Bounce toggles act on the native scrollView

The 100dvh app shell + inner-overflow main scroller made the document body
never overflow the viewport, so the native WKWebView scrollView was idle and
the Scroll/Bounce toggles (which set scrollEnabled/bounces/alwaysBounceVertical
on it) had no visible effect — bounce in particular looked broken.

Let the body be the native scroller again (min-height:100dvh + flex:1 main),
so the toggles drive the real scrollView. Bounce only manifests while scroll is
enabled (a disabled UIScrollView ignores drags), so gate the bounce checkbox on
the scroll toggle (dimmed+disabled until scroll is on), apply both toggles'
initial state at startup, and add a hint explaining the dependency.

* fix(mobile): scroll enabled by default so tall content is reachable

With scroll off by default, the System tab's device/screen cards overflowed
below the fold with no way to scroll to them (the toggle lives on the Native
tab), and the Native tab itself couldn't scroll. Default native scrolling to ON
so content is always reachable; the Scroll toggle now demonstrates *disabling*
it (freezing the page). Drop the dynamic scroll-filler — it was a crutch for the
old scroll-off default, cluttered every tab, and is redundant now that real
content overflows and alwaysBounceVertical bounces even short tabs.

* fix(mobile): restore the scroll-test filler section with scroll on

Keep scroll enabled by default (content stays reachable) but bring back the
tall filler section so there is always an obvious area to scroll and bounce
against. It is appended when scroll is on and removed when scroll is toggled
off.

* fix(mobile): scope the scroll-test filler to the Native pane

The filler was appended to <main>, so it appeared below every tab's content.
Append it into #pane-native instead, next to the Scroll/Bounce toggles, so it
only shows on the Native tab when scroll is enabled.

* fix(mobile): valid Go-template literal in android ensure-emulator task

The AVD-not-found help line wrote the template string literal as \"arm64\",
but Go's text/template rejects backslash-escaped quotes in an operand, so the
whole ensure-emulator command failed to parse ("unexpected \\ in operand")
and 'wails3 task android:run' aborted before doing anything. The block is a YAML
literal scalar, so the quotes need no escaping — use "arm64" directly.

* fix(mobile): keep auto-started android emulator alive through android:run

ensure-emulator backgrounded the emulator with a bare '... &'. go-task's shell
tracks background jobs by PID and reaps them when the command's interpreter
finishes (nohup/setsid don't help — the kill is direct), so the freshly-started
emulator died right after boot, before the install/launch steps, with
'adb install' failing 'no devices/emulators found'. Daemonize instead: a
short-lived child shell backgrounds the emulator and exits immediately, so it is
reparented to launchd/init and go-task has no handle to reap it.

Verified: 'wails3 task android:run' from a cold start (no emulator) now boots
the emulator, survives the build, installs, and launches the app unattended.

* feat(mobile): native system events (battery, network, lock, theme, lifecycle)

Surface OS signals to JS as "system:*" custom events on both iOS and Android,
so a Wails mobile app can react to battery/charging, network connectivity,
screen lock, light/dark theme, app foreground/background and low-memory
warnings - the kind of events Capacitor/React Native/Flutter expose.

Framework:
- iOS (pkg/application): ios_system_events.m registers NSNotificationCenter
  observers (battery + low-power, app lifecycle, memory, protected-data
  lock/unlock) and an NWPathMonitor for connectivity/type/expensive/constrained;
  live light/dark is caught in WailsViewController.traitCollectionDidChange.
  Each fires emitSystemEvent(name,json); emitMobileSystemEvent re-emits it as a
  "system:*" custom event via globalApplication.Event.Emit. Started from the iOS
  run path; adds the Network framework.
- Android (pkg/application + build_assets template): MainActivity registers
  BroadcastReceivers (ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED, POWER_SAVE_MODE_CHANGED,
  SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT) and a ConnectivityManager default-network callback
  (type, metered, signal strength), plus onConfigurationChanged for theme and
  lifecycle/memory hooks. Each calls bridge.emitSystemEvent -> JNI
  nativeEmitSystemEvent -> emitMobileSystemEvent. Adds ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE and
  uiMode to configChanges. A snapshot is pushed on page load so the UI starts
  populated.

Example: the Events tab gains a live System-events card + rolling log.

Verified end-to-end: Android live via adb (battery 15%/charging, wifi->cellular
metered with -50 dBm signal, light->dark); iOS via captured logs (appstate,
battery, NWPathMonitor wifi, live theme toggle). Payloads:
  system:battery {level,state,lowPowerMode}
  system:network {connected,type,metered|expensive,constrained,signal}
  system:theme {dark}  system:lock {locked}
  system:appstate {state}  system:memory {}

* refactor(mobile): system events as typed Application Events (Go-only)

Replace the ad-hoc "system:*" custom events (which were emitted to JS) with
proper ios:/android:/common: Application Events defined in events.txt and run
through the generator, per the framework's event taxonomy. These are delivered
to Go listeners only (OnApplicationEvent); no JS dispatch.

events.txt + generate: add ios:/android: Battery/Network/Theme/Screen{Locked,
Unlocked} and common: Battery/Network/Screen{Locked,Unlocked}/LowMemory
(reusing the existing common:ThemeChanged). `task generate:events` regenerates
events.go, events_ios.h and event_types.ts; known_events.go updated to match.

Data on the event context: Application Events already carry data via
ApplicationEventContext (filename/url/isDarkMode/...). iOS processApplicationEvent
now decodes a JSON-string data pointer into the context; Android gets
emitAndroidApplicationEventWithData. A public Context().Data() accessor exposes
the payload (battery level, network type, ...). Theme uses the existing
"isDarkMode" key. commonApplicationEventMap forwards platform->common and copies
the context, so common: events carry the same payload.

Native sources unchanged in spirit (iOS NSNotificationCenter + NWPathMonitor,
Android BroadcastReceivers + ConnectivityManager) but now call
processApplicationEvent / nativeEmitSystemEvent->typed event. Lifecycle and
memory reuse the existing platform Application Events (ios:ApplicationDidReceive
MemoryWarning / android:ApplicationLowMemory -> common:LowMemory).

logger_android.go: add a logcat slog handler + Android DefaultLogger so
app.Logger output is visible in `adb logcat` (Go stderr is not routed on
Android). iOS already routes app.Logger to NSLog.

Example: main.go registers OnApplicationEvent(events.Common.*) listeners that
log each event + its context data; the Events tab notes system events are
Go-side. Removed the JS system-events UI.

Verified end-to-end on both platforms (example listener fires with context data):
- Android (adb): battery 9%/charging, theme dark, network — app.Logger lines in
  logcat, plus commonApplicationEventMap forwarding 1281->1286 etc.
- iOS (NSLog): battery (level -1 on Simulator), network wifi via NWPathMonitor,
  live theme isDarkMode true/false.

* feat(mobile): forward system events to the frontend; throttle battery cadence

The native system events are Go-only application events, so the example app now
bridges them to the frontend: OnApplicationEvent(events.Common.*) listeners
re-emit them as "sys:*" custom events (Event.Emit), and the Events tab renders a
live card + log again. Battery/network/theme/lock/low-memory are all forwarded.

Battery is throttled before forwarding (the OS reports it far more often than is
useful — Android ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED also fires on temperature/voltage): send
every 10% while above 10%, then every 1% from 10% down, plus immediately on any
charge-state or low-power change.

Verified on the Android emulator: stepping 100→3% forwarded exactly
90,80,60,40,22,11 (>=10% steps, intermediate 96/84/14 skipped) then 10,9,8,7,5,3
(1% steps), and the Events-tab card shows battery/network/theme live. iOS (NSLog)
forwards sys:battery/network/theme too.

* fix(mobile): de-duplicate forwarded system events

The OS re-fires theme/network callbacks repeatedly with the same value (one
dark-mode toggle yields several common:ThemeChanged events, e.g. Android calls
onConfigurationChanged more than once), so the frontend saw duplicate sys:theme
events. The app forwarder now skips consecutive identical payloads, so each
actual change is forwarded once. Low memory is a pulse, not a state, so it is
left un-deduplicated.

Verified on Android: one dark-mode toggle now forwards exactly one sys:theme
(true on, false off) where it previously sent ~3.

* fix(mobile): debounce forwarded system events instead of dedup

Consecutive-dedup only collapsed identical repeats; a burst that interleaves
transient values (one dark-mode toggle firing dark/light/dark, or wifi-disable
flapping wifi->none->cellular) still forwarded each. Replace it with a trailing
debounce (300ms): forward only the value the burst settles on once it has been
quiet, with a last-value guard so a settle back to the same value emits nothing.

Verified on Android: an interleaved dark->light->dark burst (4 raw app events)
forwards one sys:theme=true; wifi-disable forwards only the settled
sys:network=cellular (no transient offline).

* fix(mobile): dedup forwarded events by last value per signal (not debounce)

The trailing debounce was the wrong tool: it also coalesced genuine alternations
(dark->light->dark settling to one) and delayed delivery. Revert to comparing
each event against the last value forwarded for that signal and skipping repeats.
Each signal keeps its own 'last', so interleaving other signals doesn't reset it:
dark->battery-low->dark->battery-low forwards 2 (first dark + first low), not 4;
genuine alternations still pass.

Verified on Android: a single dark-mode toggle re-fires android:ThemeChanged 3x
(same value) but forwards exactly one sys:theme.

* feat(mobile): add Phase A native features — share, open URL, keep awake, torch

Adds a cross-platform 'native:*' event bridge to the mobile kitchen sink and
the framework, exposing genuinely-mobile capabilities:

- Share sheet (UIActivityViewController / ACTION_SEND chooser)
- Open URL in system browser (UIApplication openURL / ACTION_VIEW)
- Keep screen awake (idleTimerDisabled / FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON)
- Torch / flashlight (AVCaptureDevice / CameraManager.setTorchMode)

Frontend emits native:* events; example Go listeners route them to exported
application.IOS*/Android* APIs backed by Objective-C (mobile_features_ios.m)
and the Java WailsBridge. Async results return to JS via a new generic
custom-event path (iosEmitNativeEvent / nativeEmitEvent JNI export).

New 'Mobile' tab groups these features (shown on iOS+Android).

Verified on Android emulator end-to-end (share→ChooserActivity, open→Chrome,
keep-awake→FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON, torch round-trip event); iOS builds, links the
added frameworks (LocalAuthentication/UserNotifications/AVFoundation) and runs.

* feat(mobile): add Phase B native features — safe area, brightness, app info, orientation, status bar

Adds state/query mobile capabilities to the kitchen sink and framework:

- Safe-area insets (window.safeAreaInsets / WindowInsets systemBars), pushed on
  change (iOS viewSafeAreaInsetsDidChange) and queryable on demand
- Screen brightness get/set (UIScreen.brightness / window screenBrightness)
- App info — name, version, build, bundle id (NSBundle / PackageManager)
- Orientation lock + current orientation (supportedInterfaceOrientations override
  + requestGeometryUpdate / setRequestedOrientation)
- Status bar style + hidden (preferredStatusBarStyle/prefersStatusBarHidden
  overrides / WindowInsetsController)

iOS adds WailsViewController overrides reading global appearance state.
Query features use a request→response event (native:getX → native:X).

Verified on Android emulator: app info (com.wails.app v1.0), safe-area insets
(top 136px, drops to 74px when status bar hidden), brightness set/read 25%,
orientation→landscape (SCREEN_ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE). iOS builds + launches.

* feat(mobile): add Phase C native features — biometrics, notifications, secure storage

Adds async/permission-gated mobile capabilities to the kitchen sink and framework:

- Biometric auth (Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint with device-credential
  fallback) via LAContext / androidx.biometric BiometricPrompt; result delivered
  as the native:biometric event
- Local notifications (UNUserNotificationCenter / NotificationManager + channel),
  requesting authorization / POST_NOTIFICATIONS as needed
- Secure storage set/get/delete via the iOS Keychain / Android
  EncryptedSharedPreferences (AES through the Keystore)

Adds a String(String) JNI bridge helper (callBridgeStringStringMethod) for
secure-storage reads, the androidx.biometric + security-crypto deps, and the
USE_BIOMETRIC / POST_NOTIFICATIONS manifest permissions.

Verified on Android emulator: secure storage round-trips and the on-disk prefs
contain 0 plaintext hits (encrypted at rest); notification posts (visible in
dumpsys notification); BiometricPrompt shows with a device credential and
completes to '✓ Authenticated', returns unavailable without enrollment. iOS
builds + links LocalAuthentication/UserNotifications/Security and launches.

* chore(mobile): mirror native-feature bridges to framework templates

Sync the new WailsBridge.java methods (share, open URL, keep awake, torch,
safe area, brightness, app info, orientation, status bar, biometrics,
notifications, secure storage + the emitEvent/nativeEmitEvent bridge), the
androidx.biometric + security-crypto gradle deps, the USE_BIOMETRIC /
POST_NOTIFICATIONS manifest permissions, and the LocalAuthentication /
UserNotifications / AVFoundation iOS link frameworks into both
internal/commands/{android,ios} and internal/commands/build_assets/{android,ios}
so newly-scaffolded Wails mobile apps get the same capabilities.

* Mobile: 10 new native feature bridges (sensors & hardware)

Adds Phase D to the mobile feature bridge: haptics, one-shot geolocation,
accelerometer stream, proximity sensor, text-to-speech, storage info, power/
battery state, network status, keyboard insets and screen-capture
protection/detection — exported as IOS*/Android* APIs and routed through the
existing native:* event plumbing (with a new zero-arg androidBridgeVoid helper).
iOS pulls in CoreLocation, CoreMotion and SystemConfiguration.

* Example: Hardware tab demoing the 10 new mobile features

New 'Hardware' tab wires haptics, location, accelerometer, proximity, speech,
storage, power, network, keyboard insets and screen-capture controls to the
native:* bridge. Pill tabs now wrap (flex-wrap) so the 7 tabs keep a readable
width. Android gains the Java implementations + location permissions; iOS gains
the geolocation/motion usage strings and the three new link frameworks.

* Templates: mirror Phase D bridge into new-project scaffolding

Sync WailsBridge.java, location permissions, iOS link frameworks and the
geolocation/motion Info.plist usage strings into internal/commands templates so
generated apps inherit the new sensor & hardware capabilities.

* Docs: document mobile system events + native feature bridge

Bring the mobile docs up to date with the full native surface:
- IOS.md / ANDROID.md: Status rows + 'Native mobile features' tables (all 22
  exported IOS*/Android* capabilities) and a 'System events' section
  (battery/network/theme/lock/low-memory → events.Common.*)
- examples/mobile/README.md: add the Mobile and Hardware tabs and explain the
  native:* event bridge + sys:* forwarding
- UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md: changelog entries for system events, the feature
  bridge and the sensors/hardware additions on both platforms

* Address PR review: iOS SDK-aware prebuild, drop armv7, JS escaping, thread pool

- iOS Xcode prebuild script now honors the build's PLATFORM_NAME/SDKROOT so the
  Go c-archive matches device vs simulator (was hardcoded to iphonesimulator
  while SDKROOT=iphoneos) — fixes device builds (templates + example projects)
- Remove obsolete armv7 from UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities (iOS 11+ is 64-bit;
  with MinimumOSVersion 15.0 it blocked install/App Store) — templates + example
- WailsJSBridge.escapeJsString now escapes U+2028/U+2029 line terminators
- WailsJSBridge.invokeAsync uses a pooled ExecutorService instead of unbounded
  new Thread() per call
- style.css: overflow-wrap instead of deprecated word-break: break-word
- android logcat task tolerates no-match grep (|| true); allowBackup documented

* Stop tracking Taskfile .task/ cache; gitignore .task/ and problems-report.html

* Mobile: pause sensors/torch/clock when backgrounded (battery)

On Android the app process keeps running in the background, so anything left
active keeps draining the battery; iOS suspends the app but the torch is hardware
state that persists. Pause battery-consuming work when the app leaves the
foreground and restore it on return:

- Accelerometer + proximity sensor are unregistered on background and re-enabled
  on foreground only if the user still has them switched on (iOS via
  UIApplication background/foreground notifications; Android via onStop/onStart).
  Verified on the Android emulator: a sensor change while backgrounded is ignored
  and picked up again after returning.
- Torch is switched off on background (it would otherwise keep the LED on while
  the app is suspended/hidden).
- Android system-event receivers (battery/network/screen) register in onStart and
  unregister in onStop instead of onCreate/onDestroy, so background broadcasts no
  longer wake the app.
- The example's 1 Hz clock ticker pauses while backgrounded (gated on the
  lifecycle events) instead of pushing an event into a hidden webview every
  second. Verified: the clock freezes when backgrounded and resumes on return.

* iOS: drop armv7 from remaining example Info.plists (arm64-only)

* Changelog: note background battery pausing for mobile sensors/torch/clock

* Example: make background clock-pausing an explicit opt-in flag

Expose pauseClockInBackground (default true) so it's clear how to let the ticker
keep running when backgrounded, with a comment on the iOS suspension / Android
Doze + foreground-service limits that govern whether it actually will.

* Mobile: camera capture, background-task & foreground-service APIs, iOS background-modes config

Framework additions (Phase E):
- iOS: IOSCapturePhoto/IOSCaptureVideo (UIImagePickerController → native:capture
  with a base64 thumbnail), IOSBeginBackgroundTask/IOSEndBackgroundTask (a
  UIApplication background-task window → native:backgroundTask)
- Android: AndroidCapturePhoto/Video and AndroidStart/StopForegroundService
  (exported bridge calls)
- iOS background modes are now configurable: ios.backgroundModes in
  build/config.yml templates UIBackgroundModes into the generated Info.plist
- iOS camera/microphone usage strings added to the iOS Info.plist templates

* Example: Camera tab — photo/video capture + foreground service / background task

New Camera tab capturing photos/videos with the system camera (FileProvider +
onActivityResult on Android; UIImagePickerController on iOS), shown back as a
base64 thumbnail. Background-execution controls demo the Android foreground
service (WailsForegroundService + ongoing notification) and the iOS
background-task window. Verified on the Android emulator end-to-end: a real
photo capture writes the JPEG to cache and renders its thumbnail, and the
foreground service starts/stops (isForeground + ongoing notification).

* Templates: mirror camera capture + foreground service into Android scaffolding

Sync WailsBridge (capturePhoto/captureVideo, start/stopForegroundService), the
new WailsForegroundService, the camera capture handling in MainActivity, the
FileProvider + camera <queries> + service manifest entries, and file_paths.xml
into both Android templates so generated apps inherit the capabilities.

* Changelog: camera capture, background task / foreground service, iOS background modes

* gofmt: realign iOSProjectConfig fields after BackgroundModes addition

* Example: Photo/Video pill toggle with a switched capture + playback area

The Camera tab now uses a Photo/Video pill toggle driving one capture button and
a switched preview area: photos render in an <img>, recorded videos play back in
a <video controls> element. Captures return the recording inline as a
data:video/mp4 (Android) / data:video/quicktime (iOS) URL (size-capped) so it can
play without serving cache files to the webview, and Android video capture falls
back to copying the result content URI when a camera app ignores EXTRA_OUTPUT.
Verified on the Android emulator: the pill toggle switches modes/labels/area, and
a data-URL video loads and plays back in the <video> (readyState 4, plays).

* Templates: sync camera result handling (video data URL + content-URI fallback)

* Camera: stream captured video from cache (Range) instead of a data URL

Recorded clips now play back by streaming from the app cache over the webview's
own origin, so any-length video works (no 12 MB inline cap) and seeking is
supported:
- Android: shouldInterceptRequest serves /__capture__/<cache-relative-path> with
  HTTP Range (206 Partial Content) from a path-traversal-guarded cache file.
- iOS: the wails:// scheme handler streams /__capture__/<name> from the temp dir
  with Range support.
- native:capture returns a streamUrl; the frontend prefers it over a data URL.
Verified on the Android emulator: a 5s clip loads via /__capture__, plays, and
SEEKS to 3.5s with no error (which requires working Range support).

* Templates: sync /__capture__ Range streaming into Android scaffolding

* Fix CI: iOS Info.plist template's UIBackgroundModes broke non-Xcode render paths

The shared updatable_build_assets/ios/Info.plist.tmpl is rendered by three
config types, but {{if .BackgroundModes}} only existed on iOSProjectConfig — so
GenerateBuildAssets (BuildConfig) and UpdateBuildAssets (UpdateConfig) failed
with 'can't evaluate field BackgroundModes'. Add the field to the shared
TemplateEnrichment (embedded by both) so the template evaluates everywhere;
it's populated only via the iOS Xcode generator, empty otherwise.

* Remove stray nfpm test-output packages (myapp.DEB/RPM/ARCHLINUX) + gitignore

tool_package_test emits these into the package dir; they were committed by
accident. Untrack them and ignore internal/commands/myapp.* so they don't
re-pollute the tree.

* Remove unused internal/commands/{ios,android} scaffolding copies

These 47 files were not go:embed'd or referenced by any code — the CLI generates
iOS/Android assets from internal/commands/{build_assets,updatable_build_assets}.
They were redundant committed copies; removing to slim the PR.

* gitignore internal/commands/{ios,android} (regenerated by commands tests)

* test: TestBuildAssetsDefaultArchNotX64 generates into a temp dir, not the source tree

It built BuildAssetsOptions without Dir; the default:"build" tag only applies via
CLI flag parsing, so Dir was "" and GenerateBuildAssets wrote the whole
build-assets tree (ios/android/darwin/linux/windows/...) into internal/commands/.
The test skips on amd64 (so CI stayed clean) but ran on arm64 (Apple Silicon)
devs, which is how those generated dirs got committed. Set Dir: t.TempDir().

feat(mobile): iOS and Android support for Wails v3 (experimental) (#5562)

Baseline iOS/Android command-template directories that the mobile support
commits build upon (wails3 project scaffolding for mobile targets).

- export events.IOS (was unexported iOS; events_common_ios.go references it)

  unconditionally; mobile_stub is !ios && !android)

Core fixes:
- single initial navigation: drop hardcoded loadRequest in viewDidLoad and
  manual loadView/viewDidLoad calls (page loaded twice, losing the
  wails:runtime:ready handshake); Go's window run() now loads the start URL

  ready, so Go->JS events/ExecJS work even if the postMessage handshake is
  dropped during load

  ApplicationDidFinishLaunching is emitted Go-side after listeners are wired

  delete pkg/events events_ios.go (duplicate C symbol + OOB array)

Features:

  UIDocumentPickerViewController open file/files/directory (files imported
  as sandbox copies); save dialogs return an explicit unsupported error

- screens: real UIScreen metrics (points, pixels, scale, safe-area work area)

Hygiene:

  WailsVLog); production builds are quiet
- GOOS=ios now compiles all of ./pkg/...: notifications/dock/updater/mac/
  doctor-ng darwin files no longer leak into iOS builds (ios implies the

- Taskfile platform parameterisation: IOS_PLATFORM=simulator|device picks
  SDK (iphonesimulator|iphoneos), target triple and version-min flags;

- ensure-simulator no longer hardcodes 'iPhone 15 Pro' when creating a device

Verified: simulator production package installs+launches with working
events/dialogs/bridge; device package produces LC_BUILD_VERSION platform 2
(PLATFORM_IOS) minos 15.0 binary; ipa contains signed Payload bundle.

* docs(ios)+chore: honest iOS guide, doctor checks, remove stale scratch scripts

- IOS.md: accurate status matrix, simulator/device quickstart, signing and

- delete repo-root scratch artifacts: build_ios.sh, test-new-ios-build.sh,

* chore(ios): regenerate example Info.plist (templated min version, armv7 dropped)

- new Building & Packaging guide at /guides/build/ios (experimental badge):

  porting notes; registered in the sidebar
- iOS entries in UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md (Added + Fixed)

Verified: astro build succeeds (1387 pages) and emits /guides/build/ios/.

* feat(android): runtime correctness + native dialogs/clipboard/screens/haptics

- events: generate iOS+Android event mappings from events.txt (generate:events
  now emits var IOS/var Android blocks, android: entries in eventToJS and
  event_types.ts; .m post-processing preserves blank lines; template carried
  the old 'var iOS' name that broke GOOS=ios builds on regen)
- fix build-tag leaks into GOOS=android: linux_cgo.c/.h, events_linux.go/.h,
  environment_linux.go now carry !android (android implies the linux tag);
  delete dead pkg/events/events_android.go (out-of-bounds MAX_EVENTS array)
- application_android.go rewrite: generic JNI call layer (attach/detach safe,
  exception-checked, leak-free), logcat-routed logging gated by
  androidVerboseLogging (debug/production consts), typed lifecycle events
  (ActivityCreated/Started/Resumed/Paused/Stopped/LowMemory, WebViewPage*),

- runtime handshake fixed: JS invoke messages route into windowMessageBuffer
  (plain 'wails:runtime:ready' passthrough mirrors iOS HandleJSMessage) +

- real dialogs (AlertDialog with button-role mapping + >3-button list,

* feat(android): JavascriptInterface runtime transport + screen manager wiring

The Android WebView does not deliver fetch() POST bodies to
shouldInterceptRequest, so the default HTTP runtime transport never reached
Go (a bindings call SIGSEGV'd reading a nil request body). Add an Android
transport that routes runtime calls through window.wails.invokeAsync to a new
nativeHandleRuntimeCall JNI export, with responses delivered via
window._wailsAndroidCallback. The runtime auto-installs it when the
JavascriptInterface bridge is detected (internal/runtime .../runtime.ts).

- nativeHandleRuntimeCall → handleRuntimeCallForAndroid: parses the call
  envelope and drives a per-app MessageProcessor, returning
  {ok,data|text|error}
- serveAssetForAndroid now sets req.Body = http.NoBody (handlers reached via
  ServeHTTP assume the server's non-nil-Body guarantee)
- WailsJSBridge.invokeAsync rewired to handleRuntimeCall; callback target is
  window._wailsAndroidCallback
- populate ScreenManager at startup + lazily (LayoutScreens), matching the
  desktop platforms — Screens.GetAll returned nil before; screen_android.go
  now supplies PhysicalWorkArea so WorkArea scales correctly

Verified on the API 34 arm64 emulator: assets load, JS→Go bindings render
'Hello Android!', Go→JS time events tick, native AlertDialog shows, clipboard
round-trips, Device.Info + Screens.GetAll return real data (412x915 dp,
WorkArea 412x839).

* docs(android): ANDROID.md + docs-site guide, doctor checks, changelog

- ANDROID.md: status matrix, quickstart, signing/release, porting notes,

- docs site: guides/build/android page (Experimental badge) + sidebar entry

- changelog: Added/Fixed Android entries

The Task runner cache (.task/) and the Gradle problems report

them from version control (the files remain on disk).

* fix(ios): add MinIOSVersion to build-asset config structs

The iOS Info.plist templates reference {{.MinIOSVersion}}, but the generic
build-asset generator renders all templates against BuildConfig/UpdateConfig,
which lacked the field — failing TestGenerateBuildAssets/TestUpdateBuildAssets
(internal/commands) on all platforms. Add MinIOSVersion (default 15.0) to
BuildAssetsOptions and UpdateBuildAssetsOptions so the templates resolve.

* fix(mobile): address PR review (Copilot + CodeRabbit)

Artifacts:
- examples/ios: untrack generated build/ios/xcode/overlay.json + gen/ (they
  held an absolute developer path) and gitignore them
- replace the text-placeholder icon.png files with a real 1024x1024 PNG
- regenerate the android example package-lock to match package.json ("latest");
  it had pinned a local file: path, breaking npm ci

Security / correctness:
- android: drop usesCleartextTraffic from the manifest (assets are served
  in-process over https://wails.localhost)
- ios: nil-guard the document-picker path callback (iosOpenFileCallback)
- ios: only take security-scoped access for directory (in-place) picks, not
  for asCopy file imports (avoids leaking scoped-resource handles)
- android: getScreen() returns an explicit error instead of (nil, nil)
- android: synchronize the file-picker check-and-set (MainActivity)
- android: guard native callbacks (dialog/file-picker/main-thread) so they
  no-op after shutdown() tears down the Go side
- android: treat an empty ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE as "unsigned" in build.gradle
- runtime(android transport): delete the pending entry if invokeAsync throws
  synchronously, so the callback map can't leak

Cross-platform / cleanup:
- doctor: detect the Android SDK on Windows (LOCALAPPDATA) and look for
  adb.exe; android Taskfile SDK fallback now covers Linux (~/Android/Sdk)
- ios Xcode project: SDKROOT=iphoneos (was iphonesimulator, which blocked
  device builds from Xcode) and always rebuild the Go c-archive (the old
  existence check served stale binaries when .go sources changed)
- android: remove the dead getMimeType() helper in WailsPathHandler

Android Java/manifest/gradle/Taskfile changes are synced across the example,
internal/commands, and build_assets copies.

* feat(examples): cross-platform mobile kitchen-sink demo

A single Wails v3 app that runs on iOS, Android and desktop from one main.go
and one adaptive frontend, exercising the full runtime surface:

- Bindings: JS->Go service calls (values, structs, error propagation)
- Events: Go->JS (time clock) and JS->Go->JS (ping/pong)
- Dialogs: native Info/Warning/Error/Question with callbacks
- System: clipboard round-trip, screen metrics, device info
- Native: iOS haptics + WKWebView toggles, Android vibrate + toast

The UI feature-detects the platform and shows only the controls each one
supports; navigation uses an in-page tab bar so the UX is identical
everywhere (no native iOS tab bar to avoid a second, divergent nav).

Also adds the Android runtime JS module (Runtime.Android.Haptics.Vibrate,
Device.Info, Toast.Show) mirroring Runtime.IOS, plus objectNames.Android, so
the frontend can call Android-native methods the same way as iOS.

Verified: built + launched on the API 34 Android emulator (every feature
exercised via CDP, including Go-error propagation and the native AlertDialog
callback) and on the iOS 26.5 simulator (renders, platform detection, runtime
bindings).

* fix(ios): apply SDKROOT/prebuild fix to the shipped pbxproj template

The earlier review fix edited the static internal/commands/ios/project.pbxproj,
but `wails3 ios xcode:gen` actually renders the project from
updatable_build_assets/ios/project.pbxproj.tmpl. Apply the same fixes there so
generated projects get them: SDKROOT=iphoneos (Xcode auto-selects the
simulator SDK for simulator destinations; the old hardcoded iphonesimulator
blocked device builds) and always rebuild the Go c-archive (the old
existence-only check served stale binaries after .go edits).

* feat(mobile): scroll off by default; enabling it adds a scrollable section

The mobile demo's iOS scroll toggle defaulted on but the page had nothing
to scroll, so scroll/bounce could not be exercised. Default scroll off and,
when it is turned on, append a tall filler section to the bottom of the page
so there is real content to scroll and rubber-band against; turning scroll
off removes the section (and the native scrollView) again.

* fix(mobile): align Bindings buttons and inputs to the Greet row

The Greet/Add/Divide buttons sized to their label text, so the button
column and the inputs beside them did not line up. Pin those three buttons
to a uniform width; with flex inputs the single Greet input and the Add/
Divide input pair then share the same left and right edges.

* fix(ios): populate ScreenManager so Screens.* returns data

Screens.GetAll()/GetPrimary() read from the ScreenManager, which is filled
by LayoutScreens(). Desktop platforms call that from their event loop and
Android from startup, but iOS never did — so Screens.* runtime calls
returned null. Populate it in the iOS app's run(), mirroring Android;
getScreens() always yields at least a fallback screen so this is safe.

* feat(mobile): card-render screen/device metrics, scrollable page, logo ratio

- Render Screen and Device info as labelled key/value cards instead of raw
  JSON, so they read cleanly and fit without an unscrollable blob.
- Make the content area (main) a scrollable region inside a viewport-height
  app shell, with the header/tabs/footer pinned, so long panes scroll.
- Stop forcing the header logo to a 44x44 square; fix its height and let the
  width follow so it keeps its 320x253 aspect ratio.

* fix(mobile): make iOS Scroll/Bounce toggles act on the native scrollView

The 100dvh app shell + inner-overflow main scroller made the document body
never overflow the viewport, so the native WKWebView scrollView was idle and
the Scroll/Bounce toggles (which set scrollEnabled/bounces/alwaysBounceVertical
on it) had no visible effect — bounce in particular looked broken.

Let the body be the native scroller again (min-height:100dvh + flex:1 main),
so the toggles drive the real scrollView. Bounce only manifests while scroll is
enabled (a disabled UIScrollView ignores drags), so gate the bounce checkbox on
the scroll toggle (dimmed+disabled until scroll is on), apply both toggles'
initial state at startup, and add a hint explaining the dependency.

* fix(mobile): scroll enabled by default so tall content is reachable

With scroll off by default, the System tab's device/screen cards overflowed
below the fold with no way to scroll to them (the toggle lives on the Native
tab), and the Native tab itself couldn't scroll. Default native scrolling to ON
so content is always reachable; the Scroll toggle now demonstrates *disabling*
it (freezing the page). Drop the dynamic scroll-filler — it was a crutch for the
old scroll-off default, cluttered every tab, and is redundant now that real
content overflows and alwaysBounceVertical bounces even short tabs.

* fix(mobile): restore the scroll-test filler section with scroll on

Keep scroll enabled by default (content stays reachable) but bring back the
tall filler section so there is always an obvious area to scroll and bounce
against. It is appended when scroll is on and removed when scroll is toggled
off.

* fix(mobile): scope the scroll-test filler to the Native pane

The filler was appended to <main>, so it appeared below every tab's content.
Append it into #pane-native instead, next to the Scroll/Bounce toggles, so it
only shows on the Native tab when scroll is enabled.

* fix(mobile): valid Go-template literal in android ensure-emulator task

The AVD-not-found help line wrote the template string literal as \"arm64\",
but Go's text/template rejects backslash-escaped quotes in an operand, so the
whole ensure-emulator command failed to parse ("unexpected \\ in operand")
and 'wails3 task android:run' aborted before doing anything. The block is a YAML
literal scalar, so the quotes need no escaping — use "arm64" directly.

* fix(mobile): keep auto-started android emulator alive through android:run

ensure-emulator backgrounded the emulator with a bare '... &'. go-task's shell
tracks background jobs by PID and reaps them when the command's interpreter
finishes (nohup/setsid don't help — the kill is direct), so the freshly-started
emulator died right after boot, before the install/launch steps, with
'adb install' failing 'no devices/emulators found'. Daemonize instead: a
short-lived child shell backgrounds the emulator and exits immediately, so it is
reparented to launchd/init and go-task has no handle to reap it.

Verified: 'wails3 task android:run' from a cold start (no emulator) now boots
the emulator, survives the build, installs, and launches the app unattended.

* feat(mobile): native system events (battery, network, lock, theme, lifecycle)

Surface OS signals to JS as "system:*" custom events on both iOS and Android,
so a Wails mobile app can react to battery/charging, network connectivity,
screen lock, light/dark theme, app foreground/background and low-memory
warnings - the kind of events Capacitor/React Native/Flutter expose.

Framework:
- iOS (pkg/application): ios_system_events.m registers NSNotificationCenter
  observers (battery + low-power, app lifecycle, memory, protected-data
  lock/unlock) and an NWPathMonitor for connectivity/type/expensive/constrained;
  live light/dark is caught in WailsViewController.traitCollectionDidChange.
  Each fires emitSystemEvent(name,json); emitMobileSystemEvent re-emits it as a
  "system:*" custom event via globalApplication.Event.Emit. Started from the iOS
  run path; adds the Network framework.
- Android (pkg/application + build_assets template): MainActivity registers
  BroadcastReceivers (ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED, POWER_SAVE_MODE_CHANGED,
  SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT) and a ConnectivityManager default-network callback
  (type, metered, signal strength), plus onConfigurationChanged for theme and
  lifecycle/memory hooks. Each calls bridge.emitSystemEvent -> JNI
  nativeEmitSystemEvent -> emitMobileSystemEvent. Adds ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE and
  uiMode to configChanges. A snapshot is pushed on page load so the UI starts
  populated.

Example: the Events tab gains a live System-events card + rolling log.

Verified end-to-end: Android live via adb (battery 15%/charging, wifi->cellular
metered with -50 dBm signal, light->dark); iOS via captured logs (appstate,
battery, NWPathMonitor wifi, live theme toggle). Payloads:
  system:battery {level,state,lowPowerMode}
  system:network {connected,type,metered|expensive,constrained,signal}
  system:theme {dark}  system:lock {locked}
  system:appstate {state}  system:memory {}

* refactor(mobile): system events as typed Application Events (Go-only)

Replace the ad-hoc "system:*" custom events (which were emitted to JS) with
proper ios:/android:/common: Application Events defined in events.txt and run
through the generator, per the framework's event taxonomy. These are delivered
to Go listeners only (OnApplicationEvent); no JS dispatch.

events.txt + generate: add ios:/android: Battery/Network/Theme/Screen{Locked,
Unlocked} and common: Battery/Network/Screen{Locked,Unlocked}/LowMemory
(reusing the existing common:ThemeChanged). `task generate:events` regenerates
events.go, events_ios.h and event_types.ts; known_events.go updated to match.

Data on the event context: Application Events already carry data via
ApplicationEventContext (filename/url/isDarkMode/...). iOS processApplicationEvent
now decodes a JSON-string data pointer into the context; Android gets
emitAndroidApplicationEventWithData. A public Context().Data() accessor exposes
the payload (battery level, network type, ...). Theme uses the existing
"isDarkMode" key. commonApplicationEventMap forwards platform->common and copies
the context, so common: events carry the same payload.

Native sources unchanged in spirit (iOS NSNotificationCenter + NWPathMonitor,
Android BroadcastReceivers + ConnectivityManager) but now call
processApplicationEvent / nativeEmitSystemEvent->typed event. Lifecycle and
memory reuse the existing platform Application Events (ios:ApplicationDidReceive
MemoryWarning / android:ApplicationLowMemory -> common:LowMemory).

logger_android.go: add a logcat slog handler + Android DefaultLogger so
app.Logger output is visible in `adb logcat` (Go stderr is not routed on
Android). iOS already routes app.Logger to NSLog.

Example: main.go registers OnApplicationEvent(events.Common.*) listeners that
log each event + its context data; the Events tab notes system events are
Go-side. Removed the JS system-events UI.

Verified end-to-end on both platforms (example listener fires with context data):
- Android (adb): battery 9%/charging, theme dark, network — app.Logger lines in
  logcat, plus commonApplicationEventMap forwarding 1281->1286 etc.
- iOS (NSLog): battery (level -1 on Simulator), network wifi via NWPathMonitor,
  live theme isDarkMode true/false.

* feat(mobile): forward system events to the frontend; throttle battery cadence

The native system events are Go-only application events, so the example app now
bridges them to the frontend: OnApplicationEvent(events.Common.*) listeners
re-emit them as "sys:*" custom events (Event.Emit), and the Events tab renders a
live card + log again. Battery/network/theme/lock/low-memory are all forwarded.

Battery is throttled before forwarding (the OS reports it far more often than is
useful — Android ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED also fires on temperature/voltage): send
every 10% while above 10%, then every 1% from 10% down, plus immediately on any
charge-state or low-power change.

Verified on the Android emulator: stepping 100→3% forwarded exactly
90,80,60,40,22,11 (>=10% steps, intermediate 96/84/14 skipped) then 10,9,8,7,5,3
(1% steps), and the Events-tab card shows battery/network/theme live. iOS (NSLog)
forwards sys:battery/network/theme too.

* fix(mobile): de-duplicate forwarded system events

The OS re-fires theme/network callbacks repeatedly with the same value (one
dark-mode toggle yields several common:ThemeChanged events, e.g. Android calls
onConfigurationChanged more than once), so the frontend saw duplicate sys:theme
events. The app forwarder now skips consecutive identical payloads, so each
actual change is forwarded once. Low memory is a pulse, not a state, so it is
left un-deduplicated.

Verified on Android: one dark-mode toggle now forwards exactly one sys:theme
(true on, false off) where it previously sent ~3.

* fix(mobile): debounce forwarded system events instead of dedup

Consecutive-dedup only collapsed identical repeats; a burst that interleaves
transient values (one dark-mode toggle firing dark/light/dark, or wifi-disable
flapping wifi->none->cellular) still forwarded each. Replace it with a trailing
debounce (300ms): forward only the value the burst settles on once it has been
quiet, with a last-value guard so a settle back to the same value emits nothing.

Verified on Android: an interleaved dark->light->dark burst (4 raw app events)
forwards one sys:theme=true; wifi-disable forwards only the settled
sys:network=cellular (no transient offline).

* fix(mobile): dedup forwarded events by last value per signal (not debounce)

The trailing debounce was the wrong tool: it also coalesced genuine alternations
(dark->light->dark settling to one) and delayed delivery. Revert to comparing
each event against the last value forwarded for that signal and skipping repeats.
Each signal keeps its own 'last', so interleaving other signals doesn't reset it:
dark->battery-low->dark->battery-low forwards 2 (first dark + first low), not 4;
genuine alternations still pass.

Verified on Android: a single dark-mode toggle re-fires android:ThemeChanged 3x
(same value) but forwards exactly one sys:theme.

* feat(mobile): add Phase A native features — share, open URL, keep awake, torch

Adds a cross-platform 'native:*' event bridge to the mobile kitchen sink and
the framework, exposing genuinely-mobile capabilities:

- Share sheet (UIActivityViewController / ACTION_SEND chooser)
- Open URL in system browser (UIApplication openURL / ACTION_VIEW)
- Keep screen awake (idleTimerDisabled / FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON)
- Torch / flashlight (AVCaptureDevice / CameraManager.setTorchMode)

Frontend emits native:* events; example Go listeners route them to exported
application.IOS*/Android* APIs backed by Objective-C (mobile_features_ios.m)
and the Java WailsBridge. Async results return to JS via a new generic
custom-event path (iosEmitNativeEvent / nativeEmitEvent JNI export).

New 'Mobile' tab groups these features (shown on iOS+Android).

Verified on Android emulator end-to-end (share→ChooserActivity, open→Chrome,
keep-awake→FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON, torch round-trip event); iOS builds, links the
added frameworks (LocalAuthentication/UserNotifications/AVFoundation) and runs.

* feat(mobile): add Phase B native features — safe area, brightness, app info, orientation, status bar

Adds state/query mobile capabilities to the kitchen sink and framework:

- Safe-area insets (window.safeAreaInsets / WindowInsets systemBars), pushed on
  change (iOS viewSafeAreaInsetsDidChange) and queryable on demand
- Screen brightness get/set (UIScreen.brightness / window screenBrightness)
- App info — name, version, build, bundle id (NSBundle / PackageManager)
- Orientation lock + current orientation (supportedInterfaceOrientations override
  + requestGeometryUpdate / setRequestedOrientation)
- Status bar style + hidden (preferredStatusBarStyle/prefersStatusBarHidden
  overrides / WindowInsetsController)

iOS adds WailsViewController overrides reading global appearance state.
Query features use a request→response event (native:getX → native:X).

Verified on Android emulator: app info (com.wails.app v1.0), safe-area insets
(top 136px, drops to 74px when status bar hidden), brightness set/read 25%,
orientation→landscape (SCREEN_ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE). iOS builds + launches.

* feat(mobile): add Phase C native features — biometrics, notifications, secure storage

Adds async/permission-gated mobile capabilities to the kitchen sink and framework:

- Biometric auth (Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint with device-credential
  fallback) via LAContext / androidx.biometric BiometricPrompt; result delivered
  as the native:biometric event
- Local notifications (UNUserNotificationCenter / NotificationManager + channel),
  requesting authorization / POST_NOTIFICATIONS as needed
- Secure storage set/get/delete via the iOS Keychain / Android
  EncryptedSharedPreferences (AES through the Keystore)

Adds a String(String) JNI bridge helper (callBridgeStringStringMethod) for
secure-storage reads, the androidx.biometric + security-crypto deps, and the
USE_BIOMETRIC / POST_NOTIFICATIONS manifest permissions.

Verified on Android emulator: secure storage round-trips and the on-disk prefs
contain 0 plaintext hits (encrypted at rest); notification posts (visible in
dumpsys notification); BiometricPrompt shows with a device credential and
completes to '✓ Authenticated', returns unavailable without enrollment. iOS
builds + links LocalAuthentication/UserNotifications/Security and launches.

* chore(mobile): mirror native-feature bridges to framework templates

Sync the new WailsBridge.java methods (share, open URL, keep awake, torch,
safe area, brightness, app info, orientation, status bar, biometrics,
notifications, secure storage + the emitEvent/nativeEmitEvent bridge), the
androidx.biometric + security-crypto gradle deps, the USE_BIOMETRIC /
POST_NOTIFICATIONS manifest permissions, and the LocalAuthentication /
UserNotifications / AVFoundation iOS link frameworks into both
internal/commands/{android,ios} and internal/commands/build_assets/{android,ios}
so newly-scaffolded Wails mobile apps get the same capabilities.

* Mobile: 10 new native feature bridges (sensors & hardware)

Adds Phase D to the mobile feature bridge: haptics, one-shot geolocation,
accelerometer stream, proximity sensor, text-to-speech, storage info, power/
battery state, network status, keyboard insets and screen-capture
protection/detection — exported as IOS*/Android* APIs and routed through the
existing native:* event plumbing (with a new zero-arg androidBridgeVoid helper).
iOS pulls in CoreLocation, CoreMotion and SystemConfiguration.

* Example: Hardware tab demoing the 10 new mobile features

New 'Hardware' tab wires haptics, location, accelerometer, proximity, speech,
storage, power, network, keyboard insets and screen-capture controls to the
native:* bridge. Pill tabs now wrap (flex-wrap) so the 7 tabs keep a readable
width. Android gains the Java implementations + location permissions; iOS gains
the geolocation/motion usage strings and the three new link frameworks.

* Templates: mirror Phase D bridge into new-project scaffolding

Sync WailsBridge.java, location permissions, iOS link frameworks and the
geolocation/motion Info.plist usage strings into internal/commands templates so
generated apps inherit the new sensor & hardware capabilities.

* Docs: document mobile system events + native feature bridge

Bring the mobile docs up to date with the full native surface:
- IOS.md / ANDROID.md: Status rows + 'Native mobile features' tables (all 22
  exported IOS*/Android* capabilities) and a 'System events' section
  (battery/network/theme/lock/low-memory → events.Common.*)
- examples/mobile/README.md: add the Mobile and Hardware tabs and explain the
  native:* event bridge + sys:* forwarding
- UNRELEASED_CHANGELOG.md: changelog entries for system events, the feature
  bridge and the sensors/hardware additions on both platforms

* Address PR review: iOS SDK-aware prebuild, drop armv7, JS escaping, thread pool

- iOS Xcode prebuild script now honors the build's PLATFORM_NAME/SDKROOT so the
  Go c-archive matches device vs simulator (was hardcoded to iphonesimulator
  while SDKROOT=iphoneos) — fixes device builds (templates + example projects)
- Remove obsolete armv7 from UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities (iOS 11+ is 64-bit;
  with MinimumOSVersion 15.0 it blocked install/App Store) — templates + example
- WailsJSBridge.escapeJsString now escapes U+2028/U+2029 line terminators
- WailsJSBridge.invokeAsync uses a pooled ExecutorService instead of unbounded
  new Thread() per call
- style.css: overflow-wrap instead of deprecated word-break: break-word
- android logcat task tolerates no-match grep (|| true); allowBackup documented

* Stop tracking Taskfile .task/ cache; gitignore .task/ and problems-report.html

* Mobile: pause sensors/torch/clock when backgrounded (battery)

On Android the app process keeps running in the background, so anything left
active keeps draining the battery; iOS suspends the app but the torch is hardware
state that persists. Pause battery-consuming work when the app leaves the
foreground and restore it on return:

- Accelerometer + proximity sensor are unregistered on background and re-enabled
  on foreground only if the user still has them switched on (iOS via
  UIApplication background/foreground notifications; Android via onStop/onStart).
  Verified on the Android emulator: a sensor change while backgrounded is ignored
  and picked up again after returning.
- Torch is switched off on background (it would otherwise keep the LED on while
  the app is suspended/hidden).
- Android system-event receivers (battery/network/screen) register in onStart and
  unregister in onStop instead of onCreate/onDestroy, so background broadcasts no
  longer wake the app.
- The example's 1 Hz clock ticker pauses while backgrounded (gated on the
  lifecycle events) instead of pushing an event into a hidden webview every
  second. Verified: the clock freezes when backgrounded and resumes on return.

* iOS: drop armv7 from remaining example Info.plists (arm64-only)

* Changelog: note background battery pausing for mobile sensors/torch/clock

* Example: make background clock-pausing an explicit opt-in flag

Expose pauseClockInBackground (default true) so it's clear how to let the ticker
keep running when backgrounded, with a comment on the iOS suspension / Android
Doze + foreground-service limits that govern whether it actually will.

* Mobile: camera capture, background-task & foreground-service APIs, iOS background-modes config

Framework additions (Phase E):
- iOS: IOSCapturePhoto/IOSCaptureVideo (UIImagePickerController → native:capture
  with a base64 thumbnail), IOSBeginBackgroundTask/IOSEndBackgroundTask (a
  UIApplication background-task window → native:backgroundTask)
- Android: AndroidCapturePhoto/Video and AndroidStart/StopForegroundService
  (exported bridge calls)
- iOS background modes are now configurable: ios.backgroundModes in
  build/config.yml templates UIBackgroundModes into the generated Info.plist
- iOS camera/microphone usage strings added to the iOS Info.plist templates

* Example: Camera tab — photo/video capture + foreground service / background task

New Camera tab capturing photos/videos with the system camera (FileProvider +
onActivityResult on Android; UIImagePickerController on iOS), shown back as a
base64 thumbnail. Background-execution controls demo the Android foreground
service (WailsForegroundService + ongoing notification) and the iOS
background-task window. Verified on the Android emulator end-to-end: a real
photo capture writes the JPEG to cache and renders its thumbnail, and the
foreground service starts/stops (isForeground + ongoing notification).

* Templates: mirror camera capture + foreground service into Android scaffolding

Sync WailsBridge (capturePhoto/captureVideo, start/stopForegroundService), the
new WailsForegroundService, the camera capture handling in MainActivity, the
FileProvider + camera <queries> + service manifest entries, and file_paths.xml
into both Android templates so generated apps inherit the capabilities.

* Changelog: camera capture, background task / foreground service, iOS background modes

* gofmt: realign iOSProjectConfig fields after BackgroundModes addition

* Example: Photo/Video pill toggle with a switched capture + playback area

The Camera tab now uses a Photo/Video pill toggle driving one capture button and
a switched preview area: photos render in an <img>, recorded videos play back in
a <video controls> element. Captures return the recording inline as a
data:video/mp4 (Android) / data:video/quicktime (iOS) URL (size-capped) so it can
play without serving cache files to the webview, and Android video capture falls
back to copying the result content URI when a camera app ignores EXTRA_OUTPUT.
Verified on the Android emulator: the pill toggle switches modes/labels/area, and
a data-URL video loads and plays back in the <video> (readyState 4, plays).

* Templates: sync camera result handling (video data URL + content-URI fallback)

* Camera: stream captured video from cache (Range) instead of a data URL

Recorded clips now play back by streaming from the app cache over the webview's
own origin, so any-length video works (no 12 MB inline cap) and seeking is
supported:
- Android: shouldInterceptRequest serves /__capture__/<cache-relative-path> with
  HTTP Range (206 Partial Content) from a path-traversal-guarded cache file.
- iOS: the wails:// scheme handler streams /__capture__/<name> from the temp dir
  with Range support.
- native:capture returns a streamUrl; the frontend prefers it over a data URL.
Verified on the Android emulator: a 5s clip loads via /__capture__, plays, and
SEEKS to 3.5s with no error (which requires working Range support).

* Templates: sync /__capture__ Range streaming into Android scaffolding

* Fix CI: iOS Info.plist template's UIBackgroundModes broke non-Xcode render paths

The shared updatable_build_assets/ios/Info.plist.tmpl is rendered by three
config types, but {{if .BackgroundModes}} only existed on iOSProjectConfig — so
GenerateBuildAssets (BuildConfig) and UpdateBuildAssets (UpdateConfig) failed
with 'can't evaluate field BackgroundModes'. Add the field to the shared
TemplateEnrichment (embedded by both) so the template evaluates everywhere;
it's populated only via the iOS Xcode generator, empty otherwise.

* Remove stray nfpm test-output packages (myapp.DEB/RPM/ARCHLINUX) + gitignore

tool_package_test emits these into the package dir; they were committed by
accident. Untrack them and ignore internal/commands/myapp.* so they don't
re-pollute the tree.

* Remove unused internal/commands/{ios,android} scaffolding copies

These 47 files were not go:embed'd or referenced by any code — the CLI generates
iOS/Android assets from internal/commands/{build_assets,updatable_build_assets}.
They were redundant committed copies; removing to slim the PR.

* gitignore internal/commands/{ios,android} (regenerated by commands tests)

* test: TestBuildAssetsDefaultArchNotX64 generates into a temp dir, not the source tree

It built BuildAssetsOptions without Dir; the default:"build" tag only applies via
CLI flag parsing, so Dir was "" and GenerateBuildAssets wrote the whole
build-assets tree (ios/android/darwin/linux/windows/...) into internal/commands/.
The test skips on amd64 (so CI stayed clean) but ran on arm64 (Apple Silicon)
devs, which is how those generated dirs got committed. Set Dir: t.TempDir().

commit.message:
fix(v3/darwin): copy screen id/name out of autoreleased UTF8String buffers (#5565)

* fix(v3/darwin): copy screen id/name out of autoreleased UTF8String buffers

processScreen stored the raw result of -[NSString UTF8String] in the C
Screen struct's id and name fields. UTF8String returns a pointer into an
autoreleased buffer whose lifetime ends when the enclosing autorelease
pool drains, which can happen before Go reads the strings with
C.GoString in cScreenToScreen — a use-after-free that intermittently
aborts the process with 'fatal error: invalid pointer found on stack'
when Wails' internal ApplicationDidChangeScreenParameters handler
refreshes the screen cache (display sleep/wake, monitor connect or
disconnect, resolution change). Because it is a runtime memory-safety
abort inside an internal handler, applications cannot recover from it.

The strings are now strdup'd into malloc'd memory owned by the struct
and freed by cScreenToScreen after conversion. name is also initialised
to NULL so the pre-10.15 path no longer leaves an uninitialised pointer.

getAllScreens and getScreenForWindow now run inside an explicit
autorelease pool: previously, calls from Go goroutine threads (which
have no ambient pool) leaked every autoreleased object created during
enumeration. The pool also makes the bug deterministic instead of
timing-dependent, which the new regression test exploits — run with
MallocScribble=1 it segfaults without the fix and passes with it.

Fixes #5556

* fix(v3/darwin): size screen slice from the enumeration snapshot count

Review follow-up: allScreens() sized its slice from a separate
GetNumScreens() call. If the display configuration changed between the
two calls, Go could read past the malloc'd array (freeing garbage
id/name pointers) or, when shrinking, leak the strdup'd strings in
unvisited tail entries. getAllScreens now returns the count from the
same [NSScreen screens] snapshot via an out-parameter.

commit.message:
fix(webview2): guard Focus() until controller initialisation completes (#5568)

* fix(webview2): guard Focus() until controller initialisation completes

The WndProc can dispatch WM_SETFOCUS re-entrantly while
CreateCoreWebView2ControllerCompleted is still configuring the
controller: e.controller is assigned partway through the callback, but
inited only flips after all COM setup succeeds. In that window
GetController() != nil checks at call sites pass, yet MoveFocus fails
with E_INVALIDARG and errorCallback exits the process. With no
controller at all, Focus() dereferenced nil.

Add IsReady() (atomic load of inited) and make Focus() a no-op until it
reports true. Dropping a focus request during startup is harmless; the
window manager re-delivers focus once the user interacts with the
window.

Fixes wailsapp/wails#5446

* fix(webview2): never treat a failed Focus as fatal

MoveFocus can fail after initialisation too: E_INVALIDARG when the
window is hidden or minimised to the tray (wailsapp/wails#4158
reproduces this 100% on tray-click restore). Routing that error
through errorCallback exits the process. Log it instead — a failed
focus request is never worth killing the application.

* fix(webview2): never treat a failed Eval as fatal

ExecuteScript fails transiently while the browser process reconfigures,
e.g. RESOURCE_NOT_IN_CORRECT_STATE during a DPI transition when the
window is dragged between mixed-DPI monitors (wailsapp/wails#5544
verification). Script execution is fire-and-forget: dropping a script
during a transition is recoverable, exiting the process is not. Log
instead, matching the Focus change.

commit.message:
fix(v3/linux): release WebKitURISchemeRequest on the GTK main context (#5566)

* fix(v3/linux): release WebKitURISchemeRequest on the GTK main context

request.Close() runs on the assetserver goroutine and dropped what may
be the last reference to the WebKitURISchemeRequest there. Finalizing a
WebKit GObject off the GTK main thread violates WebKitGTK's threading
rules and intermittently crashes long-running apps with a SIGSEGV in
g_object_unref during cgo execution.

Schedule the unref onto the default GMainContext with
g_main_context_invoke instead, in both the GTK3 (webkit2gtk-4.1) and
GTK4 (webkitgtk-6.0) request implementations, which share the pattern.

g_object_ref in NewRequest is unchanged: ref/unref themselves are
atomic; only the finalization triggered by the final unref is
main-thread-only.

Verified: gtk3 and gtk4 builds plus assetserver/application test suites
pass on Linux (Ubuntu, WebKitGTK 4.1/6.0). The equivalent workaround was
validated in production by the reporter over multi-day runs.

Fixes #5557

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha.100 and update changelog [skip ci]

chore(v3): populate unreleased changelog for alpha.100

Bundles content from the failed alpha.99 release (tag pushed but no
GitHub release created due to token misconfiguration) together with
the alpha.100 cycle. Includes:
- MacWebviewPreferences WKWebView extensions (#5549)
- generate bindings "Access is denied" fix on Windows (#5561)
- Linux frameless JS resize / scrollbar edge detection fix (#5368)
- Windows updater cross-volume rename fallback (#5560)

fix(ci): validate release token before pushing, fall back to github.token (#5583)

* fix(ci): validate release token before pushing, fall back to github.token

The 2026-06-10 nightly release half-failed: the version bump commit and the
v3.0.0-alpha.99 tag were pushed (git auth rode on the checkout step's
persisted credentials), then the GitHub release API call returned 401
'Requires authentication' — the signature of an expired fine-grained PAT.
The result was a tag with no release and an already-reset changelog.

Two changes:

- release.go now validates the token with a cheap authenticated read
  against the repo BEFORE committing to any push, so a dead token fails the
  run cleanly with nothing released and a clear 'expired or revoked?'
  error. If WAILS_REPO_TOKEN fails validation and a distinct GITHUB_TOKEN
  is available, the script falls back to it (with a warning) so the nightly
  still ships.
- The workflow previously set WAILS_REPO_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN to the same
  expression, making the script's fallback meaningless; it now passes the
  raw secret and github.token distinctly. github.token has contents:write
  and can create releases; the only degradation is that it cannot trigger
  downstream workflows, which none of the release steps rely on.

The expired WAILS_REPO_TOKEN secret still needs rotating; until then the
fallback keeps nightlies green.

* fix(ci): validate release token before any file mutation

Review follow-up (#5583): selectAPIToken ran after the changelog rewrite
and bump commit, so a dead token still dirtied the working tree locally.
Repo slug resolution and token validation now happen before any file is
touched; dry runs skip both since they never push and need no token.
