[skip ci] Publish @wailsio/runtime v3.0.0-alpha.88

fix(linux): enable JS resize for frameless windows; fix scrollbar edge detection (#4415, #4680) (#5368)

* fix(linux): enable JS resize for frameless windows; fix scrollbar edge detection

Frameless Wails windows on Linux had no resize capability: the drag.ts
resize-edge logic was gated behind `!IsWindows()`, so neither the
JS-side border detection nor the wails:resize:* messages ever fired on
Linux.  For decorated (non-frameless) windows the WM provides resize
handles, so no change is needed there.

Changes:
- drag.ts: extend the resize-edge condition to also execute on Linux
  when `window._wails.flags.frameless` is true, enabling
  gtk_window_begin_resize_drag to be triggered from the JS path.
- drag.ts (both platforms): account for a scrollbar at the window edge
  by computing rightContentEdge / bottomContentEdge as
  outerWidth/outerHeight minus the scrollbar width/height
  (innerWidth - clientWidth).  The 5 px resize zone is now placed *just
  before* the scrollbar rather than on top of it, so the native
  scrollbar cursor no longer hides the resize cursor and mousedown
  events reach JavaScript rather than being consumed by the scrollbar.
- linux_cgo.go / linux_cgo_gtk4.go: setResizable now calls execJS to
  keep window._wails.setResizable() in sync (mirrors Windows behaviour).
  setFrameless propagates window._wails.flags.frameless via execJS for
  runtime frameless toggles.
- webview_window_linux.go: the WindowLoadFinished hook now initialises
  both flags.frameless and calls setResizable() so the JS runtime has
  the correct state on first load.

Fixes: https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/4415
Fixes: https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/4680

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: multica-agent <github@multica.ai>

* fix(linux): address PR review comments on #5368

- drag.ts: use innerWidth/innerHeight instead of outerWidth/outerHeight as
  the base for rightContentEdge/bottomContentEdge; outerWidth can exceed
  innerWidth when a native menu bar is present (GTK vbox), making the bottom
  resize zone unreachable via event.clientY
- linux_cgo.go/linux_cgo_gtk4.go: guard execJS calls in setResizable and
  setFrameless with if(window._wails&&...) so they silently no-op before the
  JS runtime is initialised or after teardown
- webview_window_linux.go: same guard for the frameless flag assignment and
  setResizable call in WindowLoadFinished
- Rebuild runtime.js / runtime.debug.js from updated TypeScript

commit.message:
[v3, windows] Fix generate bindings failing with "Access is denied" when Vite dev server is running (#5561)

* fix(v3/windows): sync bindings into place instead of renaming over the output directory (#5515)

The atomic directory swap introduced in #5367 (RemoveAll+Rename) fails on
Windows with "Access is denied" when a file watcher such as Vite's dev
server is running: the watcher holds an open handle on the watched
bindings directory, so deleting it leaves the name in delete-pending
state and the subsequent rename over it is rejected.

Keep generating into the dot-prefixed temp directory (still invisible to
chokidar during generation), but install the result by syncing files into
the output directory instead of replacing the directory itself:

- the output directory is never deleted or renamed, so Windows watcher
  handles are never violated (#5515)
- the directory delete+recreate cascade that caused the chokidar
  rename-event loop still never happens (#3976)
- unchanged files are left untouched, so the dev server only reloads
  files that actually changed

File operations retry briefly with backoff on Windows to ride out
transient locks from watchers and antivirus scanners.

Fixes #5515

* fix(v3): don't sleep after the final retry attempt in withRetry

* fix(v3): address review feedback on bindings sync

- Handle the output path existing as a regular file: clear it and move
  the generated tree into place (with test)
- Fall back to remove+rename in replaceFile for destinations that
  os.Rename cannot replace on Windows (read-only attribute)
- Retry the final temp directory removal like other file operations
- Use 0o755 for created directories, consistent with the rest of the
  package

- For-loop {{.ITEM}} injection
- Fix include resolution: shared includes resolved once, tasks added per namespace
- Fix map iteration during template expansion (collect-then-update pattern)

* feat(wake): incremental build cache + reliability fixes

Native Go command auto-cache (exec/gocache.go): `go build` and
`go mod tidy` are skipped when their inputs are unchanged. Inputs are
derived wake-side (module .go files, go.mod/go.sum, and the generates of
dependency tasks so embedded assets like frontend/dist still force a
re-link). No-op cached builds drop from ~316ms to ~20ms (~94% faster
than the task CLI, which always re-runs both commands).

Fix glob prefix handling in recursiveGlob/recursiveMatch: patterns like
`frontend/dist/**/*` previously walked the whole tree and matched
unrelated files (e.g. .wake/cache.json), making sources/generates
caching unreliable. They now confine to the literal prefix subtree.

Fix nondeterministic var resolution: mergeVars expanded templated vars
in a single map-order-dependent pass, so self-referential vars like
`{{.OUTPUT | default .DEFAULT_OUTPUT}}` resolved to empty ~50% of runs
(stray root binary, cache thrash). It now iterates to a fixed point.

Also lands remaining Phase 4 work: taskfile AST fields, namespace
filtering, feature-support checks, and requires parsing.

* fix(wake): resolve short deps in the caller's namespace first

A bare dep/cmd name inside a namespaced task (e.g. `build` in
`darwin:package`) bound to a same-named top-level task instead of the
namespace-local one. The top-level `build` is a thin `task: {{OS}}:build`
wrapper that doesn't forward the caller's vars, so `PRODUCTION=true` was
dropped and `wails3 package` built with dev flags instead of production.

Resolve `prefix:<name>` before the bare name in both resolveDepNamespaces
(parse time) and resolveTaskName (runtime), matching Taskfile's
local-namespace-wins rule. `wails3 package` now emits the same flags as
the task CLI; dev builds are unchanged.

* feat(wake): layered local Taskfile overrides

Add support for Taskfile.local.* and Taskfile.override.* layering over a
base Taskfile.yml with local-wins precedence: a same-named task replaces
the base (list fields replace, env/vars merge per-key), local-only tasks
are added, and top-level vars layer over base. Override files stack
(.override committed, then .local personal which wins last).

Security hardening: WAILS_NO_OVERRIDES=true skips override discovery for
deterministic CI builds; Parse always returns a non-nil Tasks map and
MergeTaskfile guards a nil base to avoid panics on tasks-less Taskfiles.

Replaces the unused function-keyed override machinery with a direct
taskfile merge. Feature functions covered to 100%; documented in README.

* feat(wake): structured, colour-coded build reporting UI

Render wake builds through a dedicated reporting layer instead of flat
`[wake] cmd` lines, with progress, captured-on-failure output, and a
cross-process feedback channel for subprocess producers.

- internal/report: leaf Reporter contract, verbosity levels
  (silent/normal/verbose/debug), and a wire protocol so subprocesses can
  push live events to the build UI
- internal/report/termui: lipgloss renderer with a live per-step spinner,
  [k/N] counter, timings, status glyphs, bordered failure panels, and
  colour-coded debug lines; degrades to plain output on non-TTY/NO_COLOR
- exec: capture command output by default (shown only on failure, streamed
  when verbose); step accounting via a reported chokepoint (k<=N) with
  cache-pruned subtrees reported as cached so incremental builds reach N
- cmds: uniform Output streams on every command type for capture
- generator: under WAKE_REPORT, `wails3 generate bindings` emits live wire
  events to the build UI instead of its own spinner
- match the standard Wails command header/footer; suppress double-printing
  of already-rendered build failures

* feat(wake): Pulse build TUI renderer + executor artifact reporting

Adds a new build-reporter renderer at internal/report/pulse that paints
a pre-printed "skeleton" of one row per planned step at BuildStart, then
updates each row in place as steps progress through pending → active →
completed. The terminal does not scroll during a build; the end-of-build
summary unfolds beneath the settled skeleton.

Visual identity:
- Heartbeat spinner (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█▇▆▅▄▃▂) at ~1.1 s/beat in unison
- Opening dim→accent + closing accent→dim gradient rules (curtain-rise,
  curtain-fall) on TrueColor terminals
- Sub-cell eighths-block progress head; right-aligned duration ledger
- "Where time went" stacked phase bar (compile/test/package/prepare/other)
- "Output" panel listing build artifacts with OSC 8 hyperlinks + sizes
- Failure panels with exit-code badge, bold FAIL/PASS/ERROR keywords,
  OSC 8 file:line refs, and multi-failure aggregation banner
- Time-tier colouring on elapsed durations (snappy green, slow yellow,
  hung red); accent stripe on active rows

Wiring:
- report.Reporter grows an Artifact(Artifact) method; both termui and
  Pulse implement it; the wake executor walks each successful task's
  `generates:` patterns and registers each resolved file.
- wake.go selects the renderer by env: WAKE_TUI=pulse opts in; default
  remains termui for safety.

Zero third-party styling dependencies: ansi helpers, palette, profile
detection, and gradient interpolation are all hand-rolled in
internal/report/pulse/ansi and internal/report/pulse/{color,style}.go.
golang.org/x/term is kept for IsTerminal/GetSize, matching termui's
existing dependency footprint.

A scripted demo driver lives at cmd/waketui-demo for visualising every
state without a real wake build.

See internal/report/pulse/DESIGN.md for the full rationale and mockups.

* feat(wake): parallel-by-default builds; delete termui; many wake fixes

Parallel + Pulse defaults:
- Pulse is now the only renderer; delete report/termui entirely
- Parallel execution is the default (WAKE_SERIAL=true opts out)
- New WAKE_FORCE=true bypasses both task and Go caches for a clean build

Parallel correctness:
- report.Reporter.StepStart now returns a StepID; every step-scoped
  method (Info/Command/Output/End/Failed) takes that ID. The single
  r.serialID field in pulse went away — it was being clobbered by
  concurrent StepStart calls under parallel mode, causing StepEnd to
  finish the wrong slot (and lose visible rows in the skeleton).
- Executor.runTask now fans out task.Deps as concurrent goroutines when
  Parallel=true, matching upstream Taskfile semantics ("deps run in
  parallel before cmds"). The DAG layer-walker alone could not
  parallelise this build because most dep edges live inside cmd
  task-refs, which the DAG doesn't model.

Wake-side bugs surfaced by Pulse and fixed:
- Crash in failure path on a meta-task: cw.output() is now nil-safe,
  and a task-ref cmd's error no longer triggers a duplicate StepFailed
  on its parent (the leaf already rendered its own panel).
- Errors that abort before any step starts (task-not-found,
  precondition aborts) now synthesise a StepStart+StepFailed so the
  user actually sees why the build collapsed at 0 ms.
- OS / ARCH registered as template *functions* (not just variables),
  so {{if eq OS "darwin"}} parses in addition to {{OS}}.
- New parse.ExpandVarTemplates fixed-point pass on top-level vars
  resolves self-referencing defaults like
  {{.PACKAGE_MANAGER | default "npm"}}. Task-local vars are *not* run
  through it — they reference root vars not yet in scope and must wait
  for mergeVars at execution time.
- text/template now uses missingkey=zero, and tmplData is
  map[string]string (not interface{}), so undefined {{.X}} renders as
  "" instead of the literal text "<no value>".
- cmds.Route now shell-tokenises with shellSplit (single/double quotes,
  backslash escapes) instead of strings.Fields, so
  -ldflags="-w -s" no longer splits mid-string.
- cmd-level vars on a `task: foo` ref are now resolved against the
  caller's mergedVars before being passed to the sub-task — same path
  task.Deps vars already used.
- Task-local var passthroughs ({SCRIPT: "{{.SCRIPT}}"}) no longer
  overwrite the inherited dep-var value: mergeVars evaluates them
  against the current merged map first.

End-of-build UI polish:
- Counts now ride at the right edge of the verdict line, saving a row.
- Build artifacts no longer come from walking task.Generates patterns
  (which surfaced bindings / icons / intermediate outputs the user did
  not ask to see). Instead, reportGoBuildArtifact sniffs the `-o PATH`
  argument of a go-build cmd and registers only the resulting binary.

Icon-generation profiling cleanup:
- Drop the actool --version subprocess — redundant with the macOS
  major-version gate just above it (~12 ms saved).
- platformInfo()'s two sysctl calls now run in parallel; the build-
  number lookup is best-effort (~10 ms saved).
- generateMacAsset / generateWindowsIcon / generateMacIcon run as
  concurrent goroutines instead of sequentially (~50 ms saved).
  Floor for the icons step is now actool --compile itself (~800 ms
  on this machine), which wake's task cache skips on incremental
  builds.

* fix(wake): embedded task fallback, route wails3 task through wake, parse top-level env

Three independent fixes surfaced while proving wake build / package / run
work across every shipped Wails template:

1. fallback uses the embedded task runtime, not an external binary.
   The previous fallback path called exec.LookPath("task") and spawned a
   subprocess, which would fail on any clean machine that didn't already
   have task installed. github.com/wailsapp/task/v3 is already a direct
   dependency of wails3 (used by commands.RunTask) — the runtime is
   compiled into wails3. The new fallback constructs task.Executor
   directly, with no PATH lookup and no subprocess overhead. Verified
   by running a Taskfile with `dotenv:` (a wake-unsupported feature)
   under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin: the body runs, dotenv values load.

2. wails3 task <name> now routes through wake under WAILS_USE_WAKE=true.
   Previously only `wails3 build / package / sign` went through wake
   (via wrapTask); `wails3 task X` always took the embedded task path,
   so users got inconsistent execution semantics depending on which verb
   they invoked. The task subcommand now dispatches the same way, with
   introspection flags (--list / --watch / --dry / --status / --summary)
   falling through to the embedded runtime since wake doesn't model them.

3. Top-level Taskfile `env:` block is now parsed and applied. The
   parser previously had cases for version / includes / vars / tasks /
   shopt / silent / dotenv / output / run / interval / requires — but
   not env. A Taskfile declaring root-level env values had them
   silently dropped, leaving `$ROOT_ENV` empty in every subprocess.
   Added an Env map[string]string field to ast.Taskfile, a case for it
   in the top-level parser, and merging into the per-task env list in
   exec.go (with task-local env: winning on collisions to match
   upstream task semantics).

Net effect, with all three fixes in place:
- 16/18 shipped templates build / package / run cleanly through wake
  (the 2 qwik failures are template-level npm peer-dep conflicts that
  reproduce identically under the embedded task and outside any runner;
  separate template issue).
- 19/19 common Taskfile shell-command patterns execute correctly,
  including pipes, subshells, multi-line YAML blocks, env-section
  expansion, ldflags="-X foo -Y bar", and deps fanout.
- The fallback path works without an external task binary on PATH.

Verifier scripts retained at /tmp/verify-wake-templates.sh,
/tmp/verify-wake-package-run.sh, /tmp/verify-wake-shellcmds.sh,
/tmp/verify-wake-fallback.sh.

* docs(wake): expand the WAILS_USE_WAKE gate documentation

Make explicit what the env var covers, what it doesn't, and that the
default user path (no env var set) is unchanged. List the wake-specific
env vars users may reach for alongside it.

* chore(wake): drop committed cache/lockfile cruft and ad-hoc test scripts

The Phase 4b commit accidentally included an example project's .wake/
cache.json, its frontend package-lock.json, and two ad-hoc shell scripts
(test-wake-compare.sh, test-wake-speed.sh) that were used during
development. None of these belong in the repo; the bindings under
examples/badge/frontend/bindings/image/color/ are restored to match
master so the example stays buildable.

* docs(wake): mark wake as experimental in README and at runtime

Wake remains opt-in via WAILS_USE_WAKE=true, but the previous wording
implied it was production-ready alongside the embedded Task runtime.
Add an explicit "Experimental" callout at the top of the README and a
single-line runtime notice that prints on every wake-driven build, so
users running with the flag always know they're on the experimental
path.

The runtime notice can be silenced with WAKE_NOTICE=off (for CI logs or
scripts that grep wake output). It's also automatically suppressed
under WAKE_SILENT, which already implies a non-interactive invocation.

* docs(wake): rewrite README — elevator pitch up front, accurate differentiators

The previous README opened straight into "How to enable" without
explaining what wake actually is, and one of the touted differences vs
Task ("no external binary") was incorrect — both runtimes are compiled
into wails3; the user never installs an external `task` binary either
way.

Restructure:

1. New elevator pitch immediately after the experimental warning: wake
   is an experimental alternative build runner for wails3, reads the
   same Taskfile, purpose-built for Wails build semantics.

2. Drop the "no external binary" point. Replace with truthful, Wails-
   aligned differentiators:
   - Tailored to the Wails build pipeline (frontend embed, binary as
     first-class artefact).
   - Focused build semantics → faster incremental builds (the existing
     Go-cache point, retained as the substantive perf story).
   - Structured output controlled by wails3 (Pulse renderer, OSC 8
     file:line links, NO_COLOR / non-TTY graceful degradation).
   - Parallel execution by default.
   - Layered local overrides (existing content, kept).

3. Move "Enabling Wake" below the differentiators so a reader hits the
   "what" and "why" before the "how".

4. Single canonical Environment variables table. Drop the stale duplicate
   at the bottom that referenced the old WAKE_PARALLEL flag (parallel is
   now the default; the opt-out is WAKE_SERIAL).

* chore(wake): remove waketui-demo scratch command

The cmd/waketui-demo binary was authored alongside the Pulse renderer
to drive a scripted fake build for design inspection. It served its
purpose during development but doesn't belong shipped: it's a
maintenance burden, it duplicates Reporter-interface call sites, and
the same look can be seen by running an actual wake build.

Drop the binary and rewrite pulse/DESIGN.md's "How to inspect" section
to point at a real wails3 build under WAILS_USE_WAKE=true instead.

* chore(wake): scrub non-wake files that piggybacked on the Phase 4b commit

The original Phase 4b commit on the main branch bundled wake's template-
engine work with a large amount of in-progress, unrelated work that
happened to be in the author's working tree at the time:

  - internal/commands/android/* — entire Android scaffolding tree
    (build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml, MainActivity.java + the rest
    of the Java/Kotlin Bridge files, gradle wrapper, resource dirs,
    Java launcher icon PNGs)
  - internal/commands/darwin/* — Assets.car, Info.dev.plist, etc.
  - internal/commands/windows/* — MSIX manifest, NSIS scripts,
    wails.exe.manifest, etc.
  - internal/commands/appicon.icon/* — icon-composer source files
  - internal/commands/Taskfile.yml + config.yml — top-level
    project-scaffolding files
  - Stale committed bindings under examples/badge/frontend/bindings/...
  - generated linux package fixtures (myapp.{ARCHLINUX,DEB,RPM})

None of this has any relation to the wake build runner. It came in
because the cherry-pick that brought wake into this PR replayed the
original commit verbatim. Restore those files to master's state so
the PR diff reflects only the wake work it claims to land:

  79 files dropped/restored, +125 / −5,060 across this commit.

Sanity-checked by rebuilding `cmd/wails3` and re-running the wake and
report tests; everything still passes.

* fix(wake): address Copilot review on PR #5535

Seven targeted fixes from the automated review pass:

- cmds/native.go GoTestCmd: `-count` formatting used
  `string(rune('0'+Count))`, which only works for 0-9 and produces
  non-ASCII for Count > 9. Switch to strconv.Itoa.

- cmds/shell.go parseGoTestArgs: same digit class of bug on the parse
  side — `args[i+1][0]-'0'` only read the first character of the count
  string, so `-count 10` became 1. Switch to strconv.Atoi. Pinned with
  a TestParseGoTestCount table over "1", "10", "100", "1000".

- cmds/native.go GoFmtCmd: `go fmt` does not accept `-w` (that flag
  lives on the underlying `gofmt` binary). When the caller wants
  rewrite-in-place we now exec `gofmt -w …` directly.

- exec/runner.go isUpToDate: `cache.lastRuns` was read without taking
  the cache mutex, while `RecordRun` writes it from any goroutine.
  Under Parallel=true that's a concurrent map read/write race; Go's
  runtime checker can panic on it. Take cache.mu for the read too.

- exec/runner.go {isUpToDate, globExists}: both used `filepath.Glob`,
  which doesn't understand Taskfile's recursive `**` patterns. The
  cache layer already has a `globMatches` helper that does. Reuse it
  so up-to-date checks behave consistently with the rest of the
  caching logic.

- override/override.go LoadLocal: path was built via `dir + "/" + name`,
  which produces wrong path separators on Windows. Switch to
  filepath.Join.

- parse/expr.go ResolveVarShell: previously hard-coded `sh -c …` for
  every platform. On Windows that fails because `sh` isn't installed,
  silently breaking any Taskfile that declares `vars: {X: {sh: ...}}`.
  Move shell selection into shell_unix.go / shell_windows.go build-
  tagged files so Windows uses `cmd /C` and Unix keeps `sh -c`.

- resolve/dag.go topologicalSort: only sorted the initial zero-in-
  degree queue. Subsequent appends followed Go's randomised map
  iteration of `dag.Edges`, making the DAG order non-deterministic
  across runs and any UI derived from it flicker. Re-sort the ready
  set on each iteration.

- resolve/merge.go MergeTask: documented the existing OR-merge
  semantics for boolean fields (Silent/Internal/Interactive). The
  reviewer is right that an override file can't currently turn a true
  base value back to false; that's because ast.Task models these as
  bare bool and the parser cannot tell "unset" apart from "explicitly
  false". The conservative OR behaviour is intentional given that
  constraint, but the limitation is now spelled out in the merge code
  for the next reader. Promoting to *bool is a separate, larger change
  and none of the wake-routed paths currently read these fields.

README contradiction Copilot flagged (WAKE_SERIAL vs WAKE_PARALLEL in
two places): already resolved in the earlier README rewrite — there is
now a single canonical env-var table.

* fix(wake): address CodeRabbit review on PR #5535

Sixteen targeted fixes from the CodeRabbit review pass, covering three
buckets: concurrency races under parallel mode, cross-platform
portability (Windows), and assorted functionality bugs.

Concurrency / data-race fixes:

- exec/cache.go TaskCache: add sync.RWMutex around Entries and Save.
  RecordTask/RecordGoCmd write while ShouldSkip/ShouldSkipGoCmd read
  from parallel goroutines; the previous unlocked access could panic
  with "concurrent map read and map write".
- exec/exec.go depRuns: take e.mu for the lazy-init and every read/
  write. With parallel deps fanout multiple goroutines mutate this map
  concurrently; same race class.
- (lastRuns and ResolveVarShell already addressed in 36c2c93.)

Cross-platform portability — wake hard-coded `sh -c` in three places
and `/`-prefix as the "absolute path" test, both of which break on
Windows:

- New platform.ShellCommand helper (build-tagged: `sh -c` on Unix,
  `cmd /C` on Windows). Replaces the inline `exec.Command("sh", "-c", …)`
  in exec/cache.go (status checks), exec/runner.go (preconditions and
  status checks), and the parse/expr.go ResolveVarShell that used to
  live in a separate shell_unix/shell_windows pair under parse — those
  are removed in favour of the shared platform helper.
- exec/exec.go: replace `strings.HasPrefix(dir, "/")` with
  `filepath.IsAbs`, which understands `C:\…` on Windows. The previous
  check would treat a Windows absolute path as relative and prefix it
  with e.Dir, producing nonsense paths.
- exec/cache.go applyExcludes: normalise both file paths and exclude
  patterns to forward-slash before glob-matching. filepath.Rel returns
  backslashes on Windows but Taskfile globs are slash-based; without
  this exclude rules silently fail on Windows.
- exec/exec.go matchesPlatform: fall back from os.Getenv("GOOS") to
  platform.OS() when the env var is unset. GOOS is only reliably set
  during cross-compile; at normal run time it's "" and every platform-
  gated task was being skipped.

Functionality bugs:

- commands/task.go: the wake fast-path was bypassing `--dir` and
  `--taskfile`. Make wakeRoutableInvocation also return false when
  either is set, so those bypass wake and fall through to the embedded
  task runtime that knows how to honour them.
- report/pulse/pulse.go StepFailed: was computing the failed-step
  duration as time.Since(buildStart), overstating it badly. Pass 0
  and let finishLocked derive from the slot's startedAt.
- report/pulse/style.go truncate + visibleWidth: replace the ad-hoc
  OSC parsing with a shared escState state machine. The previous code
  treated any backslash inside an OSC region as a terminator, so a
  hyperlink whose URI contained `\` (e.g. file:///C:\path\to.go) ended
  the OSC early and miscounted/truncated the wrapped text. Pinned with
  TestVisibleWidth and TestTruncatePreservesOSC8Wrapper cases over
  backslash-bearing URIs.
- cmds/frontend.go DetectPackageManager: replace the map iteration
  (Go-randomised) with an ordered slice. On a tree containing more than
  one lockfile the previous code could pick a different package manager
  on each run.
- exec/exec.go runForLoop: resolve the per-cmd `vars:` block against
  loopVars before passing them to runTask, so a template like
  `{{.ITEM}}` actually receives the current loop item. The previous
  code threaded fl.Vars through unresolved.
- exec/exec.go runCmd: only call reportGoBuildArtifact when the
  executor.Run() actually succeeded. The previous `defer` ran on every
  exit path and could surface a stale pre-existing binary in the
  Output panel after a failed rebuild.
- exec/gocache.go parseOutputFlag: also accept `-o=<path>` (previously
  only `-o <path>` worked). With `-o=` the go-cache short-circuited
  with output="" and could skip without checking the binary existed.
- parse/parse.go parseFor: handle scalar (`for: var`) and sequence
  (`for: [a, b, c]`) forms, plus a nested `items:` key inside the
  mapping form. The previous code only read the mapping form and
  ignored items entirely.
- parse/parse.go resolveVar: stop short-circuiting `vr.Value = vr.Shell`
  for shell-bearing vars. ResolveAllVarShells detects unresolved shell
  vars by `Shell != "" && Value == ""` and would skip them after this
  short-circuit, leaving raw command strings to propagate into
  templates instead of the command's stdout.
- wake.go filterTaskNamespaces: replace SplitN(name, ":", 2) with
  Split(name, ":") so the nested-namespace platform-prefix branch
  (`darwin:linux:foo` on a darwin build) is actually reachable. Was
  dead code with SplitN capped at 2.
- override/override.go LoadLocal: stop swallowing non-IsNotExist stat
  errors. A permission or I/O error on an override file is a
  misconfiguration, not an "absent override" — surface it.

Tests: regression for the OSC 8 parsing fix (Windows-style URI with
backslashes), and a TestTruncatePreservesOSC8Wrapper invariant that
truncation must not eat the OSC wrapper sequences.

feat(wake): experimental Go-native build runner (opt-in via WAILS_USE_WAKE=true) (#5535)

* feat(wake): Phase 4 - Incremental Builds with content-addressed cache

- Fix duplicate DAG traversal: track executed tasks, skip if already run
- Add content-addressed cache (.wake/cache/) with SHA-256 hashing
- Recursive glob support for ** patterns in source tracking
- Cache skips unchanged tasks, rebuilds on source modification
- Wire cache into Executor with LoadTaskCache/RecordTask/ShouldSkip

* feat(wake): Phase 4b - Template engine, dep execution, namespace resolution

- Full Go template engine with {{if eq}}, {{default}}, Sprig functions
- Bare variable support: {{OS}} -> {{.OS}} conversion
- Deps execution: run task deps before cmds
- Namespace resolution: unqualified task refs resolved to include namespace
- exclude: pattern support in sources/generates
- sh: var execution: run shell commands, capture stdout
- Deps vars propagation: pass vars from dep to subtask
- Cmd-level vars for sub-task calls
- Runtime var expansion in cmd strings
- For-loop {{.ITEM}} injection
- Fix include resolution: shared includes resolved once, tasks added per namespace
- Fix map iteration during template expansion (collect-then-update pattern)

* feat(wake): incremental build cache + reliability fixes

Native Go command auto-cache (exec/gocache.go): `go build` and
`go mod tidy` are skipped when their inputs are unchanged. Inputs are
derived wake-side (module .go files, go.mod/go.sum, and the generates of
dependency tasks so embedded assets like frontend/dist still force a
re-link). No-op cached builds drop from ~316ms to ~20ms (~94% faster
than the task CLI, which always re-runs both commands).

Fix glob prefix handling in recursiveGlob/recursiveMatch: patterns like
`frontend/dist/**/*` previously walked the whole tree and matched
unrelated files (e.g. .wake/cache.json), making sources/generates
caching unreliable. They now confine to the literal prefix subtree.

Fix nondeterministic var resolution: mergeVars expanded templated vars
in a single map-order-dependent pass, so self-referential vars like
`{{.OUTPUT | default .DEFAULT_OUTPUT}}` resolved to empty ~50% of runs
(stray root binary, cache thrash). It now iterates to a fixed point.

Also lands remaining Phase 4 work: taskfile AST fields, namespace
filtering, feature-support checks, and requires parsing.

* fix(wake): resolve short deps in the caller's namespace first

A bare dep/cmd name inside a namespaced task (e.g. `build` in
`darwin:package`) bound to a same-named top-level task instead of the
namespace-local one. The top-level `build` is a thin `task: {{OS}}:build`
wrapper that doesn't forward the caller's vars, so `PRODUCTION=true` was
dropped and `wails3 package` built with dev flags instead of production.

Resolve `prefix:<name>` before the bare name in both resolveDepNamespaces
(parse time) and resolveTaskName (runtime), matching Taskfile's
local-namespace-wins rule. `wails3 package` now emits the same flags as
the task CLI; dev builds are unchanged.

* feat(wake): layered local Taskfile overrides

Add support for Taskfile.local.* and Taskfile.override.* layering over a
base Taskfile.yml with local-wins precedence: a same-named task replaces
the base (list fields replace, env/vars merge per-key), local-only tasks
are added, and top-level vars layer over base. Override files stack
(.override committed, then .local personal which wins last).

Security hardening: WAILS_NO_OVERRIDES=true skips override discovery for
deterministic CI builds; Parse always returns a non-nil Tasks map and
MergeTaskfile guards a nil base to avoid panics on tasks-less Taskfiles.

Replaces the unused function-keyed override machinery with a direct
taskfile merge. Feature functions covered to 100%; documented in README.

* feat(wake): structured, colour-coded build reporting UI

Render wake builds through a dedicated reporting layer instead of flat
`[wake] cmd` lines, with progress, captured-on-failure output, and a
cross-process feedback channel for subprocess producers.

- internal/report: leaf Reporter contract, verbosity levels
  (silent/normal/verbose/debug), and a wire protocol so subprocesses can
  push live events to the build UI
- internal/report/termui: lipgloss renderer with a live per-step spinner,
  [k/N] counter, timings, status glyphs, bordered failure panels, and
  colour-coded debug lines; degrades to plain output on non-TTY/NO_COLOR
- exec: capture command output by default (shown only on failure, streamed
  when verbose); step accounting via a reported chokepoint (k<=N) with
  cache-pruned subtrees reported as cached so incremental builds reach N
- cmds: uniform Output streams on every command type for capture
- generator: under WAKE_REPORT, `wails3 generate bindings` emits live wire
  events to the build UI instead of its own spinner
- match the standard Wails command header/footer; suppress double-printing
  of already-rendered build failures

* feat(wake): Pulse build TUI renderer + executor artifact reporting

Adds a new build-reporter renderer at internal/report/pulse that paints
a pre-printed "skeleton" of one row per planned step at BuildStart, then
updates each row in place as steps progress through pending → active →
completed. The terminal does not scroll during a build; the end-of-build
summary unfolds beneath the settled skeleton.

Visual identity:
- Heartbeat spinner (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█▇▆▅▄▃▂) at ~1.1 s/beat in unison
- Opening dim→accent + closing accent→dim gradient rules (curtain-rise,
  curtain-fall) on TrueColor terminals
- Sub-cell eighths-block progress head; right-aligned duration ledger
- "Where time went" stacked phase bar (compile/test/package/prepare/other)
- "Output" panel listing build artifacts with OSC 8 hyperlinks + sizes
- Failure panels with exit-code badge, bold FAIL/PASS/ERROR keywords,
  OSC 8 file:line refs, and multi-failure aggregation banner
- Time-tier colouring on elapsed durations (snappy green, slow yellow,
  hung red); accent stripe on active rows

Wiring:
- report.Reporter grows an Artifact(Artifact) method; both termui and
  Pulse implement it; the wake executor walks each successful task's
  `generates:` patterns and registers each resolved file.
- wake.go selects the renderer by env: WAKE_TUI=pulse opts in; default
  remains termui for safety.

Zero third-party styling dependencies: ansi helpers, palette, profile
detection, and gradient interpolation are all hand-rolled in
internal/report/pulse/ansi and internal/report/pulse/{color,style}.go.
golang.org/x/term is kept for IsTerminal/GetSize, matching termui's
existing dependency footprint.

A scripted demo driver lives at cmd/waketui-demo for visualising every
state without a real wake build.

See internal/report/pulse/DESIGN.md for the full rationale and mockups.

* feat(wake): parallel-by-default builds; delete termui; many wake fixes

Parallel + Pulse defaults:
- Pulse is now the only renderer; delete report/termui entirely
- Parallel execution is the default (WAKE_SERIAL=true opts out)
- New WAKE_FORCE=true bypasses both task and Go caches for a clean build

Parallel correctness:
- report.Reporter.StepStart now returns a StepID; every step-scoped
  method (Info/Command/Output/End/Failed) takes that ID. The single
  r.serialID field in pulse went away — it was being clobbered by
  concurrent StepStart calls under parallel mode, causing StepEnd to
  finish the wrong slot (and lose visible rows in the skeleton).
- Executor.runTask now fans out task.Deps as concurrent goroutines when
  Parallel=true, matching upstream Taskfile semantics ("deps run in
  parallel before cmds"). The DAG layer-walker alone could not
  parallelise this build because most dep edges live inside cmd
  task-refs, which the DAG doesn't model.

Wake-side bugs surfaced by Pulse and fixed:
- Crash in failure path on a meta-task: cw.output() is now nil-safe,
  and a task-ref cmd's error no longer triggers a duplicate StepFailed
  on its parent (the leaf already rendered its own panel).
- Errors that abort before any step starts (task-not-found,
  precondition aborts) now synthesise a StepStart+StepFailed so the
  user actually sees why the build collapsed at 0 ms.
- OS / ARCH registered as template *functions* (not just variables),
  so {{if eq OS "darwin"}} parses in addition to {{OS}}.
- New parse.ExpandVarTemplates fixed-point pass on top-level vars
  resolves self-referencing defaults like
  {{.PACKAGE_MANAGER | default "npm"}}. Task-local vars are *not* run
  through it — they reference root vars not yet in scope and must wait
  for mergeVars at execution time.
- text/template now uses missingkey=zero, and tmplData is
  map[string]string (not interface{}), so undefined {{.X}} renders as
  "" instead of the literal text "<no value>".
- cmds.Route now shell-tokenises with shellSplit (single/double quotes,
  backslash escapes) instead of strings.Fields, so
  -ldflags="-w -s" no longer splits mid-string.
- cmd-level vars on a `task: foo` ref are now resolved against the
  caller's mergedVars before being passed to the sub-task — same path
  task.Deps vars already used.
- Task-local var passthroughs ({SCRIPT: "{{.SCRIPT}}"}) no longer
  overwrite the inherited dep-var value: mergeVars evaluates them
  against the current merged map first.

End-of-build UI polish:
- Counts now ride at the right edge of the verdict line, saving a row.
- Build artifacts no longer come from walking task.Generates patterns
  (which surfaced bindings / icons / intermediate outputs the user did
  not ask to see). Instead, reportGoBuildArtifact sniffs the `-o PATH`
  argument of a go-build cmd and registers only the resulting binary.

Icon-generation profiling cleanup:
- Drop the actool --version subprocess — redundant with the macOS
  major-version gate just above it (~12 ms saved).
- platformInfo()'s two sysctl calls now run in parallel; the build-
  number lookup is best-effort (~10 ms saved).
- generateMacAsset / generateWindowsIcon / generateMacIcon run as
  concurrent goroutines instead of sequentially (~50 ms saved).
  Floor for the icons step is now actool --compile itself (~800 ms
  on this machine), which wake's task cache skips on incremental
  builds.

* fix(wake): embedded task fallback, route wails3 task through wake, parse top-level env

Three independent fixes surfaced while proving wake build / package / run
work across every shipped Wails template:

1. fallback uses the embedded task runtime, not an external binary.
   The previous fallback path called exec.LookPath("task") and spawned a
   subprocess, which would fail on any clean machine that didn't already
   have task installed. github.com/wailsapp/task/v3 is already a direct
   dependency of wails3 (used by commands.RunTask) — the runtime is
   compiled into wails3. The new fallback constructs task.Executor
   directly, with no PATH lookup and no subprocess overhead. Verified
   by running a Taskfile with `dotenv:` (a wake-unsupported feature)
   under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin: the body runs, dotenv values load.

2. wails3 task <name> now routes through wake under WAILS_USE_WAKE=true.
   Previously only `wails3 build / package / sign` went through wake
   (via wrapTask); `wails3 task X` always took the embedded task path,
   so users got inconsistent execution semantics depending on which verb
   they invoked. The task subcommand now dispatches the same way, with
   introspection flags (--list / --watch / --dry / --status / --summary)
   falling through to the embedded runtime since wake doesn't model them.

3. Top-level Taskfile `env:` block is now parsed and applied. The
   parser previously had cases for version / includes / vars / tasks /
   shopt / silent / dotenv / output / run / interval / requires — but
   not env. A Taskfile declaring root-level env values had them
   silently dropped, leaving `$ROOT_ENV` empty in every subprocess.
   Added an Env map[string]string field to ast.Taskfile, a case for it
   in the top-level parser, and merging into the per-task env list in
   exec.go (with task-local env: winning on collisions to match
   upstream task semantics).

Net effect, with all three fixes in place:
- 16/18 shipped templates build / package / run cleanly through wake
  (the 2 qwik failures are template-level npm peer-dep conflicts that
  reproduce identically under the embedded task and outside any runner;
  separate template issue).
- 19/19 common Taskfile shell-command patterns execute correctly,
  including pipes, subshells, multi-line YAML blocks, env-section
  expansion, ldflags="-X foo -Y bar", and deps fanout.
- The fallback path works without an external task binary on PATH.

Verifier scripts retained at /tmp/verify-wake-templates.sh,
/tmp/verify-wake-package-run.sh, /tmp/verify-wake-shellcmds.sh,
/tmp/verify-wake-fallback.sh.

* docs(wake): expand the WAILS_USE_WAKE gate documentation

Make explicit what the env var covers, what it doesn't, and that the
default user path (no env var set) is unchanged. List the wake-specific
env vars users may reach for alongside it.

* chore(wake): drop committed cache/lockfile cruft and ad-hoc test scripts

The Phase 4b commit accidentally included an example project's .wake/
cache.json, its frontend package-lock.json, and two ad-hoc shell scripts
(test-wake-compare.sh, test-wake-speed.sh) that were used during
development. None of these belong in the repo; the bindings under
examples/badge/frontend/bindings/image/color/ are restored to match
master so the example stays buildable.

* docs(wake): mark wake as experimental in README and at runtime

Wake remains opt-in via WAILS_USE_WAKE=true, but the previous wording
implied it was production-ready alongside the embedded Task runtime.
Add an explicit "Experimental" callout at the top of the README and a
single-line runtime notice that prints on every wake-driven build, so
users running with the flag always know they're on the experimental
path.

The runtime notice can be silenced with WAKE_NOTICE=off (for CI logs or
scripts that grep wake output). It's also automatically suppressed
under WAKE_SILENT, which already implies a non-interactive invocation.

* docs(wake): rewrite README — elevator pitch up front, accurate differentiators

The previous README opened straight into "How to enable" without
explaining what wake actually is, and one of the touted differences vs
Task ("no external binary") was incorrect — both runtimes are compiled
into wails3; the user never installs an external `task` binary either
way.

Restructure:

1. New elevator pitch immediately after the experimental warning: wake
   is an experimental alternative build runner for wails3, reads the
   same Taskfile, purpose-built for Wails build semantics.

2. Drop the "no external binary" point. Replace with truthful, Wails-
   aligned differentiators:
   - Tailored to the Wails build pipeline (frontend embed, binary as
     first-class artefact).
   - Focused build semantics → faster incremental builds (the existing
     Go-cache point, retained as the substantive perf story).
   - Structured output controlled by wails3 (Pulse renderer, OSC 8
     file:line links, NO_COLOR / non-TTY graceful degradation).
   - Parallel execution by default.
   - Layered local overrides (existing content, kept).

3. Move "Enabling Wake" below the differentiators so a reader hits the
   "what" and "why" before the "how".

4. Single canonical Environment variables table. Drop the stale duplicate
   at the bottom that referenced the old WAKE_PARALLEL flag (parallel is
   now the default; the opt-out is WAKE_SERIAL).

* chore(wake): remove waketui-demo scratch command

The cmd/waketui-demo binary was authored alongside the Pulse renderer
to drive a scripted fake build for design inspection. It served its
purpose during development but doesn't belong shipped: it's a
maintenance burden, it duplicates Reporter-interface call sites, and
the same look can be seen by running an actual wake build.

Drop the binary and rewrite pulse/DESIGN.md's "How to inspect" section
to point at a real wails3 build under WAILS_USE_WAKE=true instead.

* chore(wake): scrub non-wake files that piggybacked on the Phase 4b commit

The original Phase 4b commit on the main branch bundled wake's template-
engine work with a large amount of in-progress, unrelated work that
happened to be in the author's working tree at the time:

  - internal/commands/android/* — entire Android scaffolding tree
    (build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml, MainActivity.java + the rest
    of the Java/Kotlin Bridge files, gradle wrapper, resource dirs,
    Java launcher icon PNGs)
  - internal/commands/darwin/* — Assets.car, Info.dev.plist, etc.
  - internal/commands/windows/* — MSIX manifest, NSIS scripts,
    wails.exe.manifest, etc.
  - internal/commands/appicon.icon/* — icon-composer source files
  - internal/commands/Taskfile.yml + config.yml — top-level
    project-scaffolding files
  - Stale committed bindings under examples/badge/frontend/bindings/...
  - generated linux package fixtures (myapp.{ARCHLINUX,DEB,RPM})

None of this has any relation to the wake build runner. It came in
because the cherry-pick that brought wake into this PR replayed the
original commit verbatim. Restore those files to master's state so
the PR diff reflects only the wake work it claims to land:

  79 files dropped/restored, +125 / −5,060 across this commit.

Sanity-checked by rebuilding `cmd/wails3` and re-running the wake and
report tests; everything still passes.

* fix(wake): address Copilot review on PR #5535

Seven targeted fixes from the automated review pass:

- cmds/native.go GoTestCmd: `-count` formatting used
  `string(rune('0'+Count))`, which only works for 0-9 and produces
  non-ASCII for Count > 9. Switch to strconv.Itoa.

- cmds/shell.go parseGoTestArgs: same digit class of bug on the parse
  side — `args[i+1][0]-'0'` only read the first character of the count
  string, so `-count 10` became 1. Switch to strconv.Atoi. Pinned with
  a TestParseGoTestCount table over "1", "10", "100", "1000".

- cmds/native.go GoFmtCmd: `go fmt` does not accept `-w` (that flag
  lives on the underlying `gofmt` binary). When the caller wants
  rewrite-in-place we now exec `gofmt -w …` directly.

- exec/runner.go isUpToDate: `cache.lastRuns` was read without taking
  the cache mutex, while `RecordRun` writes it from any goroutine.
  Under Parallel=true that's a concurrent map read/write race; Go's
  runtime checker can panic on it. Take cache.mu for the read too.

- exec/runner.go {isUpToDate, globExists}: both used `filepath.Glob`,
  which doesn't understand Taskfile's recursive `**` patterns. The
  cache layer already has a `globMatches` helper that does. Reuse it
  so up-to-date checks behave consistently with the rest of the
  caching logic.

- override/override.go LoadLocal: path was built via `dir + "/" + name`,
  which produces wrong path separators on Windows. Switch to
  filepath.Join.

- parse/expr.go ResolveVarShell: previously hard-coded `sh -c …` for
  every platform. On Windows that fails because `sh` isn't installed,
  silently breaking any Taskfile that declares `vars: {X: {sh: ...}}`.
  Move shell selection into shell_unix.go / shell_windows.go build-
  tagged files so Windows uses `cmd /C` and Unix keeps `sh -c`.

- resolve/dag.go topologicalSort: only sorted the initial zero-in-
  degree queue. Subsequent appends followed Go's randomised map
  iteration of `dag.Edges`, making the DAG order non-deterministic
  across runs and any UI derived from it flicker. Re-sort the ready
  set on each iteration.

- resolve/merge.go MergeTask: documented the existing OR-merge
  semantics for boolean fields (Silent/Internal/Interactive). The
  reviewer is right that an override file can't currently turn a true
  base value back to false; that's because ast.Task models these as
  bare bool and the parser cannot tell "unset" apart from "explicitly
  false". The conservative OR behaviour is intentional given that
  constraint, but the limitation is now spelled out in the merge code
  for the next reader. Promoting to *bool is a separate, larger change
  and none of the wake-routed paths currently read these fields.

README contradiction Copilot flagged (WAKE_SERIAL vs WAKE_PARALLEL in
two places): already resolved in the earlier README rewrite — there is
now a single canonical env-var table.

* fix(wake): address CodeRabbit review on PR #5535

Sixteen targeted fixes from the CodeRabbit review pass, covering three
buckets: concurrency races under parallel mode, cross-platform
portability (Windows), and assorted functionality bugs.

Concurrency / data-race fixes:

- exec/cache.go TaskCache: add sync.RWMutex around Entries and Save.
  RecordTask/RecordGoCmd write while ShouldSkip/ShouldSkipGoCmd read
  from parallel goroutines; the previous unlocked access could panic
  with "concurrent map read and map write".
- exec/exec.go depRuns: take e.mu for the lazy-init and every read/
  write. With parallel deps fanout multiple goroutines mutate this map
  concurrently; same race class.
- (lastRuns and ResolveVarShell already addressed in 36c2c93.)

Cross-platform portability — wake hard-coded `sh -c` in three places
and `/`-prefix as the "absolute path" test, both of which break on
Windows:

- New platform.ShellCommand helper (build-tagged: `sh -c` on Unix,
  `cmd /C` on Windows). Replaces the inline `exec.Command("sh", "-c", …)`
  in exec/cache.go (status checks), exec/runner.go (preconditions and
  status checks), and the parse/expr.go ResolveVarShell that used to
  live in a separate shell_unix/shell_windows pair under parse — those
  are removed in favour of the shared platform helper.
- exec/exec.go: replace `strings.HasPrefix(dir, "/")` with
  `filepath.IsAbs`, which understands `C:\…` on Windows. The previous
  check would treat a Windows absolute path as relative and prefix it
  with e.Dir, producing nonsense paths.
- exec/cache.go applyExcludes: normalise both file paths and exclude
  patterns to forward-slash before glob-matching. filepath.Rel returns
  backslashes on Windows but Taskfile globs are slash-based; without
  this exclude rules silently fail on Windows.
- exec/exec.go matchesPlatform: fall back from os.Getenv("GOOS") to
  platform.OS() when the env var is unset. GOOS is only reliably set
  during cross-compile; at normal run time it's "" and every platform-
  gated task was being skipped.

Functionality bugs:

- commands/task.go: the wake fast-path was bypassing `--dir` and
  `--taskfile`. Make wakeRoutableInvocation also return false when
  either is set, so those bypass wake and fall through to the embedded
  task runtime that knows how to honour them.
- report/pulse/pulse.go StepFailed: was computing the failed-step
  duration as time.Since(buildStart), overstating it badly. Pass 0
  and let finishLocked derive from the slot's startedAt.
- report/pulse/style.go truncate + visibleWidth: replace the ad-hoc
  OSC parsing with a shared escState state machine. The previous code
  treated any backslash inside an OSC region as a terminator, so a
  hyperlink whose URI contained `\` (e.g. file:///C:\path\to.go) ended
  the OSC early and miscounted/truncated the wrapped text. Pinned with
  TestVisibleWidth and TestTruncatePreservesOSC8Wrapper cases over
  backslash-bearing URIs.
- cmds/frontend.go DetectPackageManager: replace the map iteration
  (Go-randomised) with an ordered slice. On a tree containing more than
  one lockfile the previous code could pick a different package manager
  on each run.
- exec/exec.go runForLoop: resolve the per-cmd `vars:` block against
  loopVars before passing them to runTask, so a template like
  `{{.ITEM}}` actually receives the current loop item. The previous
  code threaded fl.Vars through unresolved.
- exec/exec.go runCmd: only call reportGoBuildArtifact when the
  executor.Run() actually succeeded. The previous `defer` ran on every
  exit path and could surface a stale pre-existing binary in the
  Output panel after a failed rebuild.
- exec/gocache.go parseOutputFlag: also accept `-o=<path>` (previously
  only `-o <path>` worked). With `-o=` the go-cache short-circuited
  with output="" and could skip without checking the binary existed.
- parse/parse.go parseFor: handle scalar (`for: var`) and sequence
  (`for: [a, b, c]`) forms, plus a nested `items:` key inside the
  mapping form. The previous code only read the mapping form and
  ignored items entirely.
- parse/parse.go resolveVar: stop short-circuiting `vr.Value = vr.Shell`
  for shell-bearing vars. ResolveAllVarShells detects unresolved shell
  vars by `Shell != "" && Value == ""` and would skip them after this
  short-circuit, leaving raw command strings to propagate into
  templates instead of the command's stdout.
- wake.go filterTaskNamespaces: replace SplitN(name, ":", 2) with
  Split(name, ":") so the nested-namespace platform-prefix branch
  (`darwin:linux:foo` on a darwin build) is actually reachable. Was
  dead code with SplitN capped at 2.
- override/override.go LoadLocal: stop swallowing non-IsNotExist stat
  errors. A permission or I/O error on an override file is a
  misconfiguration, not an "absent override" — surface it.

Tests: regression for the OSC 8 parsing fix (Windows-style URI with
backslashes), and a TestTruncatePreservesOSC8Wrapper invariant that
truncation must not eat the OSC wrapper sequences.

fix(buildinfo): Development should reflect local source, not vcs=git (#5531)

* fix(buildinfo): Development should reflect local source, not vcs=git

`buildinfo.Info.Development` was implemented as "the binary's BuildInfo
carries a `vcs=git` build setting." That setting is emitted by Go's
toolchain for any binary built inside a git checkout, including release
artefacts produced by CI from a tagged commit. As a result, every
released `wails3` binary reported `Development=true` on every user's
machine.

The only consumer of the field — `templates.Install` in
`internal/templates/templates.go` — uses it to decide whether to inject
a local `replace github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 => …` directive into the
scaffolded `go.mod`. With `Development=true` but the source tree absent
(`debug.LocalModulePath == ""`), the replace path collapses to `/v3` on
Windows (different `filepath.VolumeName` for an empty path) and the
generated `go.mod` is broken from the start:

    go: changeme imports
        github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application:
        github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3@v3.0.0-alpha.95:
        replacement directory /v3 does not exist

Redefine `Development` as: "this binary was built from a local Wails
source tree that is still resolvable on disk at runtime" — exactly the
precondition the templates code needs. The single source of truth is
`debug.LocalModulePath`, which is set by `debug`'s `init()` only when
`.git` is found relative to the live source-file location, and is empty
on every binary that was built then shipped to a different machine.

Two regression tests pin the new semantics in place.

* Potential fix for pull request finding

commit.message:
fix(linux): stop forcing SA_ONSTACK on SIGUSR1 to prevent WebKit freeze (#5530)

WebKit's JavaScriptCore uses SIGUSR1 to suspend/resume threads for
conservative GC stack scanning. The signal-handler fix added in
alpha.97 (#5507) re-applied SA_ONSTACK to every signal it touched,
including SIGUSR1. Once JSC installs its own SIGUSR1 handler it owns the
signal (Go no longer handles it), so forcing SA_ONSTACK makes that
handler run on Go's alternate signal stack, breaking GC thread
synchronisation. This froze the WebKit UI during idle garbage
collection (most visibly with the inspector open) while the Go backend
kept running.

Remove fix_signal(SIGUSR1) from install_signal_handlers in v3 (GTK4 +
GTK3) and v2. The genuine #5506 fix for SIGSEGV/SIGBUS (which Go needs
SA_ONSTACK for) is unaffected.

Fixes #5527

fix(v3): regenerate go.sum after refresh v1.0.0 bump (#5526) (#5532)

Commit #5526 bumped github.com/atterpac/refresh to v1.0.0 in v3/go.mod
but left v3/go.sum with only the v0.8.6 checksums. Any build that runs
with -mod=readonly (e.g. `task install` -> `go install ./cmd/wails3`,
the "Build Wails3 CLI" CI step) therefore fails with:

    internal/commands/watcher.go:6:2: missing go.sum entry for module
    providing package github.com/atterpac/refresh/engine

This breaks the template-build matrix on every open PR. The Go test
jobs masked it because `task test:examples` runs `go mod tidy` first.

`go mod tidy` regenerates the missing refresh v1.0.0 checksums and
propagates the indirect bump of lmittmann/tint v1.0.3 -> v1.1.3 that
refresh v1.0.0's go.mod requires (a refresh-only patch would next fail
on a missing tint checksum).

commit.message:
fix(bindings): strip debug info on Windows to avoid Go 1.25 DWARF5 PE bug (#5524)

Go 1.25 switched to DWARF5 debug format by default. On Windows, the
internal linker emits malformed PE section headers when DWARF5 sections
are present, producing a binary that Windows refuses to execute:

  fork/exec wailsbindings.exe: %1 is not a valid Win32 application.
  fork/exec wailsbindings.exe: This version of %1 is not compatible
    with the version of Windows you're running.

Pass -ldflags="-s -w" when building wailsbindings.exe on Windows.
Stripping debug info removes DWARF5 sections entirely, producing clean
PE headers. This is appropriate for a temporary tool binary that is
deleted immediately after use and never debugged.

The fix works regardless of whether the user's project uses CGO.

Upstream: golang/go#75077, golang/go#75121
Fixes #4605
Fixes #4551

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha.97 and update changelog [skip ci]

fix(build): copy frontend build output to embed target when frontend:dir is non-default (#5251)

* fix(build): copy frontend build output to embed target when frontend:dir is non-default

When the frontend directory is configured via frontend:dir in wails.json
to a non-default path (e.g. ./jsfrontend), the build system correctly
builds the frontend in that directory but the Go embed directive still
references frontend/dist. This means the built assets are not included
in the compiled binary.

After BuildFrontend, if the actual frontend directory differs from the
default frontend/ directory, the built dist files are copied to the
embed target directory discovered via static analysis of //go:embed
directives.

Fixes #5034

* fix(build): restore frontend/dist to .gitkeep after build

SyncFrontendDistToEmbedTarget now returns a cleanup func that removes
the copied assets and restores a .gitkeep placeholder after the build
completes, keeping the working tree clean. The cleanup runs via defer
so it fires whether the build succeeds or fails.

CFBundleIdentifier was generated as com.wails.{{.Name}} which could
contain spaces and special characters, violating Apple's requirement

non-alphanumeric runs with hyphens, then strips leading/trailing
dashes. Applied to both Info.plist and Info.dev.plist templates.

Removing `_ "embed"` from complex_json/main.go and marshalers/main.go shifted
line numbers by 1, invalidating the golden warning log snapshots.

Windows OS timer granularity is ~15ms so time.Sleep(1ms) can actually
sleep 15ms, exceeding the 5ms debounce window and causing the timer to
fire mid-loop. Raise debounceAfter to 100ms and inter-call sleep to 5ms
so the ratio holds even on loaded CI runners.

commit.message:
fix: preserve size constraints across maximise/unmaximise cycle (#5204)

DisableSizeConstraints() was overwriting the original MinWidth/MinHeight/
MaxWidth/MaxHeight option values with 0, so EnableSizeConstraints() could
never restore them. This caused ToggleMaximise and UnMaximise to permanently
lose window size constraints.

Save the original constraint values before zeroing and restore from saved
values when re-enabling constraints.

commit.message:
fix: clamp zoom to minimum 1.0 on Windows and macOS (#5205)

When SetZoom is called with a value less than 1.0, the rendered web
content shrinks but the window's hit-testing area is not adjusted. This
causes the invisible region outside the content to still be draggable
and resizable. Linux already clamps to 1.0 minimum.

Apply the same guard on Windows and macOS for consistency and to
prevent the drag/resize area mismatch bug.

Fixes #4590

commit.message:
fix(windows): prevent mouse click-through in fullscreen for transparent windows (#5195)

When a window with both Frameless and BackgroundType (transparent)
options enters fullscreen, mouse clicks pass through to underlying
windows because WS_EX_LAYERED uses alpha-based hit-testing where
transparent pixels don't capture events.

commit.message:
fix: use 0,0 for min dimensions in Linux disableSizeConstraints (#5206)

The Linux disableSizeConstraints() method was incorrectly passing the
monitor's position coordinates (x, y) as the minimum width and height
parameters to setMinMaxSize(). On multi-monitor setups, this could set
nonsensical minimum sizes (e.g., minX=1920 for a monitor at x=1920).

Pass 0, 0 for min dimensions instead, which is consistent with Windows
and macOS behavior.

Fixes #4429

commit.message:
fix(linux): preserve display name in .desktop file generation (#5182)

GenerateDotDesktop was calling normaliseName() on the Name field,
which lowercased it and replaced spaces with dashes. This altered
the Name= value in the .desktop entry, affecting how the app appears
in desktop menus.

The Name field in a .desktop file should be the human-readable display
name per the FreeDesktop spec. Only the output filename needs to be
normalized.

Before: wails3 generate .desktop -name "My app" → Name=my-app
After:  wails3 generate .desktop -name "My app" → Name=My app

Fixes #5072

commit.message:
fix(v3): allow valid URL characters in Browser.OpenURL (#5222)

Remove parentheses, square brackets, curly braces, asterisk, tilde,
and exclamation mark from the shell metacharacter blocklist in the URL
validator. These characters are valid in URLs per RFC 3986 and are
commonly found in URLs like Wikipedia articles with disambiguation
titles.

Parse the URL before applying the shell metacharacter check so that
dangerous schemes (javascript, data, file) are caught first with a more
accurate error message.

Fixes: #4669

fix(v3/linux): use normalized binary name in Taskfile for consistent packaging (#5247)

* fix(v3/linux): use normalized binary name in Taskfile for consistent packaging

Linux packaging fails when the project name contains capital letters
because the Taskfile APP_NAME uses the raw project name while the
nfpm template uses the lowercased BinaryName. This causes the build
to produce 'bin/Wails' but nfpm expects 'bin/wails'.

Fix by setting BinaryName (lowercased) in the init template data and
using it for APP_NAME in the root Taskfile template.

v3: replace 11 direct dependencies with internal stdlib implementations (#5508)

* v3: replace 11 direct dependencies with internal stdlib implementations

Removes the following direct dependencies from go.mod by inlining
lightweight stdlib-only replacements:

- github.com/Masterminds/semver v1     → internal/semver
- github.com/bep/debounce              → internal/debounce
- github.com/google/shlex             → inline splitShell() in internal/s
- github.com/google/uuid              → internal/uuid
- github.com/leaanthony/go-ansi-parser → pluggable SystemTrayLabelParser var
- github.com/leaanthony/gosod         → internal/gosod
- github.com/leaanthony/u             → internal/optional
- github.com/lmittmann/tint           → internal/tint
- github.com/pkg/browser              → internal/browser
- github.com/pkg/errors               → fmt.Errorf / stdlib errors
- github.com/samber/lo                → internal/lo (generics)

The SystemTrayLabelParser change makes macOS system tray ANSI label
rendering pluggable: the default implementation strips escape codes,
and callers can replace the var with a full ANSI parser such as
go-ansi-parser or any compatible library.

All replacements tested: go build ./..., wails3 init, wails3 generate
build-assets, and wails3 service init all pass cleanly.

* v3: fix review issues in internal replacement packages

- sqlite: guard errors.Wrap replacement so nil err returns nil (critical
  bug: every successful Stmt.Close was returning a non-nil error)
- debounce: use generation counter to drop callbacks from superseded
  timers that fire after Stop() returns false
- semver: implement SemVer 2.0-correct prerelease comparison (numeric
  identifiers compared numerically, numeric < alphanumeric, dot-split)
- tint: make defensive copies in WithAttrs/WithGroup to prevent slice
  aliasing between parent and child handlers
- s/splitShell: operate on []rune to fix UTF-8 multi-byte corruption;
  track inWord flag to correctly preserve empty quoted arguments
- systemtray_darwin: free C strings allocated by partToCStrings after
  each createAttributedString/appendAttributedString call

* v3: fix remaining review issues

- browser: reap child process with go cmd.Wait() to avoid zombies
- syso: use %w instead of %s for icon-close error to allow unwrapping
- templates: fix error reporting when template.yaml exists but is
  unreadable — surface the real yamlErr instead of the json not-found
  message; check both files are absent before reporting "not found"

* v3: add tests for all new internal packages; split browser by platform

- internal/browser: split open() into per-platform files (darwin/windows/other)
  so each platform achieves 100% statement coverage; removes unreachable
  branches that the GOOS switch compiled in on every platform
- internal/uuid: drop unreachable error check after crypto/rand.Read; Go 1.20+
  calls runtime.fatal internally and never returns an error
- Add _test.go files for all 8 new packages:
  browser(100%), debounce(100%), lo(100%), optional(100%),
  semver(100%), tint(100%), uuid(100%), gosod(97.9% — two error
  paths structurally unreachable: filepath.Abs needs deleted CWD,
  os.File.Close needs concrete-type mock)
- Debounce generation-mismatch branch covered deterministically by holding
  d.mu externally while timer fires then bumping generation before Unlock
- SemVer prerelease tests cover all §11.4 comparison branches including the
  full alpha<alpha.1<alpha.beta<beta<beta.2<beta.11<rc.1<1.0.0 ordering

* v3/internal/gosod: reach 100% coverage via injectable hooks

Add absPath and osCreateFile package-level variables (default to
filepath.Abs and os.Create) so tests can substitute failing stubs to
cover the two previously unreachable error paths:
- Extract: filepath.Abs error branch
- processTemplates: w.Close() error branch

* v3: address coderabbit review comments on test files

- internal/browser: move OS-launching tests to integration build tag
  (browser_integration_test.go); add openCmd injectable var to all
  platform files so unit tests can stub without real side effects;
  TestOpen_Success stubs with os.Args[0] -test.run=^$ (exits 0, cross-platform)
- internal/gosod: move TestExtract_MkdirAllFails to gosod_unix_test.go
  with //go:build unix to avoid Windows CI failures on chmod semantics
- internal/tint: check error return from h.Handle() instead of discarding
  it with _ in TestHandle_NoColor_ProducesNoEscapeCodes and
  TestHandle_Color_ContainsEscapeCodes

commit.message:
fix(linux): re-apply signal handlers periodically to survive JSC lazy init (#5507)

* fix(linux): re-apply signal handlers periodically to survive JSC lazy init

WebKit's JavaScriptCore (JSC) lazily installs signal handlers (SIGSEGV for
JIT crash recovery, SIGUSR1 for GC thread sync) when JavaScript first
executes - not at WebView creation. These handlers are registered without
SA_ONSTACK, overwriting Go's handler which requires it.

The existing one-shot fix runs before any JS executes, so JSC wipes it out
immediately when it initialises. A 50ms periodic timer (100 iterations =
5s) running on the GTK main thread re-applies install_signal_handlers()
throughout the JSC initialisation window, ensuring Go's SA_ONSTACK
requirement is always satisfied.

Fixes #5506

* fix(linux): add SIGUSR1, WEBKIT_LOAD_FINISHED hook, and anchor GTK4 timer

Addresses code review feedback on #5507:

- Add SIGUSR1 to install_signal_handlers(): JSC uses SIGUSR1 for GC
  thread synchronisation and installs it without SA_ONSTACK (visible as
  "Overriding existing handler for signal 10" in stderr). The fix_signal
  helper only adds SA_ONSTACK to whatever handler is already registered,
  so this is safe for both Go's and JSC's handler.

- Hook WEBKIT_LOAD_FINISHED (v3 GTK4/GTK3) and DomReady (v2): by
  page-load completion JSC is guaranteed to have initialised and
  installed all its signal handlers. A targeted call to
  install_signal_handlers() here provides a deterministic, event-driven
  fix that complements the periodic timer.

- Anchor the GTK4 periodic timer to first WebView creation (sync.Once
  inside windowNewWebview) rather than appNew(), mirroring the GTK3
  pattern. This ensures the 5s coverage window starts when JSC can
  actually initialise, not before any WebView exists.

* fix(linux): immediate install_signal_handlers in GTK4 fixSignalHandlers.Do

commit.message: chore(v3): bump to v3.0.0-alpha.96 and update changelog [skip ci]

feat(v3:obfuscation): add Garble support with stable binding IDs (#5337)

* Add Garble obfuscation support: stable binding method IDs

- Introduce application.RegisterBindingMethodID, a sync.Map keyed by
  the method's function pointer that getMethods consults before
  falling back to the FQN hash. Function-pointer identity survives
  Garble's exported-name renaming, so the lookup stays valid in
  obfuscated builds.
- Add `wails3 generate bindings -obfuscated`, which emits a single
  aggregated wails_obfuscated.gen.go (build-tagged wails_obfuscated)
  next to the loaded `package main`, registering every service
  method's stable ID via init(). Pass `-obfuscated-output <dir>` to
  override the destination (useful for monorepos with no main package
  among the loaded patterns).
- Add `wails3 build --obfuscated --garbleargs ...` and the matching
  Taskfile plumbing: a `wails_obfuscated` build tag, a garble
  invocation gated on `OBFUSCATED=true`, env propagation through
  nested tasks, and a `command -v garble` precondition so missing
  garble fails fast instead of silently producing an unobfuscated
  binary. The cross-compile Dockerfile installs garble.

Refs #4563

* Lock JSON wire format on runtime payloads under Garble

Garble obfuscates exported field names of types in obfuscated
packages. The runtime ships several structs to the frontend via
encoding/json, where reflection picks up the renamed fields and
breaks the wire contract. Adding explicit json:"…" tags pins the
wire-level field names so the wire format is identical with or
without obfuscation.

Tagged: EnvironmentInfo, operatingsystem.OS, Screen, Rect, Point,
Size, Capabilities. CustomEvent and deviceInfo were already tagged.

Refs #4563

* fix(v3:obfuscation): address CodeRabbit review feedback on garble PR

- Pin garble install to @v0.16.0 in all three platform Taskfiles to avoid
  incompatibility with Go versions outside the garble-supported range
- Normalize obfuscated-output path via filepath.Abs before self-package
  lookup in resolveObfuscatedOutput, fixing the relative-path bug that
  caused empty selfPkgPath and invalid self-imports
- Reserve "application" alias in buildPackageAliases to prevent alias
  collision when a service package is also named "application"
- Add UnregisterBindingMethodID for test-cleanup and use it in
  TestRegisteredBindingMethodID to keep the global registry hermetic

feat(v3:obfuscation): add Garble support with stable binding IDs (#5337)

* Add Garble obfuscation support: stable binding method IDs

- Introduce application.RegisterBindingMethodID, a sync.Map keyed by
  the method's function pointer that getMethods consults before
  falling back to the FQN hash. Function-pointer identity survives
  Garble's exported-name renaming, so the lookup stays valid in
  obfuscated builds.
- Add `wails3 generate bindings -obfuscated`, which emits a single
  aggregated wails_obfuscated.gen.go (build-tagged wails_obfuscated)
  next to the loaded `package main`, registering every service
  method's stable ID via init(). Pass `-obfuscated-output <dir>` to
  override the destination (useful for monorepos with no main package
  among the loaded patterns).
- Add `wails3 build --obfuscated --garbleargs ...` and the matching
  Taskfile plumbing: a `wails_obfuscated` build tag, a garble
  invocation gated on `OBFUSCATED=true`, env propagation through
  nested tasks, and a `command -v garble` precondition so missing
  garble fails fast instead of silently producing an unobfuscated
  binary. The cross-compile Dockerfile installs garble.

Refs #4563

* Lock JSON wire format on runtime payloads under Garble

Garble obfuscates exported field names of types in obfuscated
packages. The runtime ships several structs to the frontend via
encoding/json, where reflection picks up the renamed fields and
breaks the wire contract. Adding explicit json:"…" tags pins the
wire-level field names so the wire format is identical with or
without obfuscation.

Tagged: EnvironmentInfo, operatingsystem.OS, Screen, Rect, Point,
Size, Capabilities. CustomEvent and deviceInfo were already tagged.

Refs #4563

  collision when a service package is also named "application"

fix(v3/templates): fix generate template to use embedded FS (#5503)

* fix(templates): fix generate template to use embedded FS instead of runtime.Caller

GenerateTemplate previously used runtime.Caller(0) to locate _common and base
files on the OS filesystem. This only worked when running directly from source;
installed binaries failed silently because the source paths don't exist at
runtime.

Fix: use the already-embedded `templates` FS (via //go:embed *) with os.CopyFS,
matching the pattern used by Install() for internal templates. The generated
skeleton is now self-contained, portable, and works correctly from any installed
binary.

Also:
- Remove leftover debug println from getLocalTemplate
- Fix error message field name in parseTemplate: 'version' → 'schema'
- Expand remote template warning to show template name/author and use
  explicit acceptance language ("Do you accept responsibility...")
- Rewrite base/NEXTSTEPS.md with comprehensive template author guidance:
  file structure, available template variables, how to publish on GitHub,
  version tagging, and the third-party disclaimer model

* fix(templates): address PR review feedback

- os.Stat check in GenerateTemplate: separate 'already exists' (err==nil)
  from other stat failures (e.g. permission denied) which now propagate as-is
- NEXTSTEPS.md: use wails3 prefix in CLI examples (v3 CLI is wails3, not wails)
- NEXTSTEPS.md: fix docs link /guides/custom-templates → /guides/advanced/custom-templates

* fix(templates): address second-round PR review feedback

- Strip ANSI/control sequences from remote template metadata (Name, Author,
  HelpURL) before printing in confirmRemote — prevents terminal spoofing via
  malicious template.json
- Add 'text' language tag to fenced code block in NEXTSTEPS.md (MD040)

* feat(templates): use template.yaml for v3, detect v2 by format

The template metadata format now signals the Wails version by file type:

  template.yaml → Wails v3 (new, preferred format)
  template.json → legacy: schema:3 = old v3 compat, schema:0 = v2 error

template.yaml requires `wailsVersion: 3` (mandatory field). Any other value
or an absent field is a clear error. This removes ambiguity: a template.json
with no schema produces the message "This template is probably for Wails v2"
rather than a cryptic schema error.

Changes:
- parseTemplate: tries template.yaml first, falls back to template.json.
  YAML path validates wailsVersion; JSON path validates schema (backwards
  compat for existing remote v3 templates that pre-date this change).
- BaseTemplate: add WailsVersion field with yaml/json tags.
- Template: add yaml:",inline" to BaseTemplate embed so YAML unmarshalling
  flattens the embedded fields correctly.
- getRemoteTemplate: fix tempDir leak — temp directory was never cleaned up
  when parseTemplate returned an error (e.g. v2 template detected).
- Install: deferred cleanup now removes both template.yaml and template.json.
- GenerateTemplate: writes template.yaml (with wailsVersion: 3) instead of
  template.json.
- All 21 built-in templates: convert template.json → template.yaml, removing
  the schema field in favour of wailsVersion: 3.

* docs(templates): update NEXTSTEPS.md for template.yaml format

* test(templates): add test suite for parseTemplate, GenerateTemplate, stripUnsafe

Covers:
- YAML path: valid wailsVersion:3, missing wailsVersion, wrong wailsVersion
- JSON path: schema:3 backwards compat, no schema (v2 error), bad schema
- Neither file present → error
- YAML takes precedence over JSON when both exist
- Subdirectory prefix (built-in template path)
- stripUnsafe: ESC, control chars, DEL removal; newline/tab preserved
- GenerateTemplate: expected files created, template.yaml contains wailsVersion:3,
  no template.json written, errors on existing output dir, round-trip parse succeeds

* fix: strip newline/tab from template metadata to prevent multiline terminal spoofing

stripUnsafe now drops all C0/C1 control characters (< 0x20 and 0x7f–0x9f),
closing the multiline injection vector where a crafted template name or author
field containing \n could forge extra lines in the third-party warning banner.

* docs: fix stale template.json references in NEXTSTEPS.md

Update line 86 ("template.json" → "template.yaml") and the link title
on line 121 ("Template JSON Schema" → "Template Schema") to be consistent
with the YAML-based template format introduced in this PR.

* feat: add JSON Schema for template.yaml and yaml-language-server modelines

- Add docs/public/schemas/template.v3.json — a JSON Schema (draft-07)
  describing the v3 template.yaml format, served at
  https://v3.wails.io/schemas/template.v3.json

- Prepend a yaml-language-server modeline to all 21 built-in template.yaml
  files and to templates generated by `wails generate template`, giving
  editors (VS Code + redhat.vscode-yaml, JetBrains) autocomplete and
  inline validation for template metadata out of the box

* docs: rewrite custom-templates guide for v3 YAML format

- Replace all template.json/schema:3 references with template.yaml/wailsVersion:3
- Document the yaml-language-server modeline and schema for editor autocomplete
- Fix GitHub URL format (@ syntax for version pinning)
- Add Steps component for the publish workflow
- Document NEXTSTEPS.md and the third-party template warning
- Update template variable table (add ModulePath, Opn, Cls)
- Rewrite best practices section

* docs: move custom-templates guide to guides/advanced/ to match sidebar link
