fix: exclude Astro docs site from FOSSA license scanning

The docs/ Astro site was not excluded from FOSSA npm scanning, causing
License Compliance to fail on PRs that touch docs/. The root packages
are build-time only and not distributed with the Wails module:

- sharp → @img/sharp-libvips-* (LGPL-3.0-or-later)
- astro-d2 → @terrastruct/d2 (MPL-2.0)

Extends the existing website/ exclusion pattern to also cover docs/.

fix(linux): implement setAlwaysOnTop + fix SoupMessageHeaders leak (GTK4 + GTK3) (#5488)

* fix(linux): implement setAlwaysOnTop + fix SoupMessageHeaders leak on GTK4/GTK3 paths

- Implement setAlwaysOnTop via _NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE on X11 (no-op on Wayland,
  which has no standard compositor-neutral protocol for this)
- Fix SoupMessageHeaders reference leak: soup_message_headers_new transfers
  a floating ref to the caller; add soup_message_headers_unref after passing
  to webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers in both GTK4 and GTK3 paths
- Remove dead GBytes allocation in linuxApp.setIcon (allocated and unref'd
  without use); clarify GTK4 limitation in both app-level and window-level
  setIcon — GTK4 removed per-window icon APIs, icon is set via .desktop file

* fix(doctor): fix xbps InstallCommand type error

pkg.InstallCommand is a string, not map[string]string. Indexing it
with a string key doesn't compile. Use the field directly, matching
every other package manager implementation.

* fix(linux): cache setAlwaysOnTop state for pre-surface calls

If setAlwaysOnTop is called before the window is shown (GTK surface
doesn't exist yet), the X11 ClientMessage had nowhere to go and the
call was silently lost.

Store the desired state in g_object_data (1=true, 2=false; NULL=never
set) so we can distinguish "set to false" from "never called". Add
window_apply_pending_always_on_top() and call it from windowShow()
after gtk_window_present, so the state is applied as soon as the
surface exists.

* fix(linux): set xclient.display in _NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE ClientMessage

XClientMessageEvent.display must be initialized to the X11 display
connection. Leaving it zeroed can cause window managers to ignore the
message or trigger undefined behaviour in Xlib.

commit.message: [skip ci] Publish @wailsio/runtime v3.0.0-alpha.86

feat(v3): app.Updater with pluggable Provider interface + GitHub / keygen.sh / AppCast providers (#5449)

* feat(v3): add updater package with pluggable Provider interface

Introduces app.Updater — a singleton update orchestrator wired into
application.App. End users configure it once via Init then drive it with
Check / DownloadAndInstall / CheckAndInstall.

The Provider interface (Name / Check / Download) lets any release source
back the updater — GitHub Releases, keygen.sh, AppCast feeds, custom — with
verification, atomic writes, swap and the default window all owned by the
Updater rather than the provider.

Verification is built in: Ed25519, Ed25519ph (pre-hash, SHA-512) and
ECDSA-P256 over SHA-256, with digest-only mode supported. The internal
verifier registry is unexported in v1 so we can promote it to a public
RegisterVerifier later without breaking callers.

Subscribe to lifecycle events through the standard Wails event bus — both
Go and JavaScript use the same `updater:*` event names. Event constants
exported on the package with payload types documented inline.

This commit lands the interface, types, verification, atomic download with
streaming digest, and a fake-Provider test suite (19 tests). Window
template, binary swap, restart, GitHub/keygen.sh/AppCast providers and
docs follow in subsequent commits.

* feat(v3/updater): same-binary helper-mode swap + Restart

Add the swap-and-relaunch step that completes the update flow without
asking the user to deal with overwriting-a-running-binary on any platform.

Implements the inconshreveable/go-update pattern: when the Updater calls
Restart, the app re-execs itself with sentinel env vars. application.New
detects those vars at startup, hands control to runHelperSwap, and the
parent exits. The helper-mode process waits for the parent PID to die,
backs up the running binary, retries an atomic rename of the new artifact
into place (Windows file-lock safety net), launches the replaced binary,
and self-destructs the backup.

Handles macOS .app bundles correctly via recursive copy/symlink-aware
traversal, falls back to a single-file path for plain executables on
Linux and Windows, and rolls back to the backup if either the swap or
the relaunch fails so a broken update never leaves the app unbootable.

No extra binary shipped: the helper IS the app, switched into helper
mode by env vars. Cross-builds clean for darwin/linux/windows. Seven new
swap-logic tests plus the existing 19 keep the package at 26 green.

* feat(v3/updater): default window, BYO escape hatch, headless mode

Built-in HTML/CSS/JS template that listens to updater:* events and emits
updater:user:* actions back to Go — no framework-specific tags, no custom
elements, just plain Wails events through the runtime. Dark-mode CSS
variables, status / progress / release-notes panels, four action buttons
(Install / Skip / Remind / Cancel) plus a Restart button visible only in
the ready state. Override the whole template via BuiltinWindow.HTML, layer
extra CSS via BuiltinWindow.CSS, tweak chrome (frameless/size/AOT) via
BuiltinWindow.Options.

Window option types: nil → defaults, *BuiltinWindow → overrides, any value
satisfying updater.WindowHandle (e.g. *application.WebviewWindow) → BYO,
updater.WindowNone → headless.

Host interface gains OpenWindow + OnEvent so the updater package can drive
real Wails windows without importing application. The application package
supplies an adapter (newUpdaterHost) that wraps *EventManager and
*WindowManager.NewWithOptions, plus a small updaterWindowHandle that
trims the fluent return values off SetHTML/Show/Hide.

User-action listeners are wired the moment a session opens, dispatching
updater:user:install → DownloadAndInstall, updater:user:cancel →
closeWindow, updater:user:skip → SkipVersion + close, updater:user:remind
→ close, updater:user:restart → Restart. Skipped versions short-circuit
subsequent Checks to up-to-date until cleared.

* feat(v3/updater): GitHub Releases provider

First provider implementation: hits api.github.com (or a configurable base
URL for GitHub Enterprise), picks an asset by GOOS/GOARCH heuristics, and
optionally pulls a sibling SHA256SUMS-style checksum file to populate
Release.Verification — letting the framework's verifier authenticate the
download with zero extra config from the user.

Asset matching defaults to substring-of-platform AND substring-of-arch on
the filename, skipping .sig / .asc / *sum* sidecars. Recognises the common
arch aliases (amd64 ↔ x86_64/x64, arm64 ↔ aarch64, 386 ↔ i386/x86/ia32).
Custom selection via Config.AssetMatcher.

Auth via Bearer PAT raises rate limits and unlocks private repos. Download
follows the asset's signed redirect and strips Authorization on the
cross-host hop so the token never reaches the storage backend.

Eleven httptest tests cover the happy path, up-to-date / 404, prerelease
toggle, asset filter, missing match, checksum-sidecar verification, the
redirect-and-strip flow, validation, and API-error surfacing.

* feat(v3/updater): keygen.sh provider

Port the keygen.sh integration written previously into the Wails v3
updater Provider shape. Key adaptation: keygen's per-artifact base64
checksum (SHA-512) and signature (Ed25519ph) fields now flow into
Release.Verification, so the framework's verifier authenticates the
download automatically once the consumer has set Config.PublicKey on the
Updater — no provider-specific verification path.

Handles keygen.sh quirks discovered while building the original library:
the /upgrade endpoint silently drops ?include=artifacts (fallback fetch
to /releases/{id}/artifacts), the artifact download 303s to Cloudflare R2
on a different host (CheckRedirect wrapper drops Authorization on cross-
origin hops), and 404 from /upgrade means "no newer release" rather than
a hard error.

Auth supports either Token (admi-/prod-/envi-/user- prefixed values) or
LicenseKey, with Token winning when both are set. Typed APIError surfaces
the keygen JSON error envelope (title / detail / code / status) for
debuggable failures.

Eleven httptest tests cover the happy path with verification mapping,
404=up-to-date, both auth schemes, error surfacing, no-matching artifact,
the include=artifacts fallback, the redirect-strip flow, validation, and
the Provider-interface assertion.

* feat(v3/updater): Sparkle-compatible AppCast provider

Parses the canonical Sparkle XML vocabulary so existing Sparkle/WinSparkle
feeds drop in unchanged: items are picked by sparkle:shortVersionString
(falling back to sparkle:version), the download comes from <enclosure>,
and Sparkle 2's sparkle:edSignature flows into Release.Verification as an
Ed25519 signature for the framework's verifier.

Item selection reconciles Sparkle's loose OS naming ("macos"/"mac"/"osx"
all map to Go's "darwin"), and a Config.Channel filter narrows to one
sparkle:channel when the feed publishes multiple. Sparkle 1's
sparkle:dsaSignature is intentionally not supported — projects on DSA
should rotate to EdDSA per Sparkle 2's guidance.

Ten httptest tests cover the happy path with verification, Windows
selection, up-to-date short-circuit, no-platform-match, 404=up-to-date,
500=error, channel filtering, download streaming with progress,
URL-required validation, and the Provider interface assertion.

Docs cover the 30-second quick start, the three built-in providers
(GitHub Releases / keygen.sh / Sparkle AppCast) with config knobs,

  Updater uses a plain sync.Mutex named sessMu).
- Remove the `req.Header.Set(\"Accept\", req.Header.Get(\"Accept\"))`

* fix(v3/updater): tear down prior session in CheckAndInstall

Each invocation of CheckAndInstall registered 5 fresh user-action
listeners under sessMu but never closed any previous session. A
periodic-check timer firing alongside a manual click (or two clicks)
would leak listeners and windows; stale callbacks would still fire on
the next user action, double-invoking DownloadAndInstall or Restart.

Close any active session before opening the new one, and add a
regression test that exercises three back-to-back CheckAndInstall
calls and asserts the host's listener map is empty afterwards.

* fix(v3/updater): clean up wails-update-* staging directory

The download flow created an os.MkdirTemp(\"\", \"wails-update-*\")
directory and staged the artifact inside. Two leak paths left orphan
directories under os.TempDir across update attempts:

- success path: after Restart spawned the helper and the helper renamed
  the staged binary into place, the (now-empty) directory persisted.
- error paths: \`_ = os.Remove(tmpPath)\` removed the staged file but
  left the enclosing dir.

Plus, when digestHasher errored before any download bytes flowed, the
freshly-created directory was leaked outright (flagged by CodeRabbit).

Three coordinated changes:

1. download() now returns (path, dir, err) and tears the directory
   down on every error path via a single deferred RemoveAll guarded by
   a success bool — including the hasher-setup branch.
2. Updater tracks stagingDir alongside resolved; DownloadAndInstall
   removes any stale dir before downloading again and RemoveAll's the
   current dir on verify/install failures.
3. runHelperSwap removes the parent directory of newPath after a
   successful rename, guarded by the \`wails-update-\` prefix so a
   caller-supplied path outside the temp area can never be deleted by
   accident.

Adds a TempDir-counting regression test to keep this from regressing.

* fix(v3/updater): inject BuiltinWindow.CSS inside <head>

The previous composeHTML appended the override <style> tag after the
closing </html> of the default template, producing a malformed
document that HTML linters and CSP-strict configurations reject.

Splice the extra <style> before </head> when one is present so the
result stays well-formed. Custom-HTML templates without </head> fall
back to appending at the document end with a comment.

Tightens the existing CSS-injection test to assert the override sits
before both </head> and </html>.

* fix(v3/updater/github): skip drafts in prerelease release listing

\`/repos/{r}/releases\` includes draft releases when the request is
authenticated, and \`per_page=1\` plus a recently-created draft would
surface that draft as an available update instead of the actual
latest prerelease. Asymmetric with the non-prerelease path, which
hits \`/releases/latest\` and is already draft-free.

Fetch up to 10 items and return the first non-draft, adding a
regression test that injects a draft at the top of the list.

* fix(v3/updater): reject ECDSA DER signatures with trailing bytes

asn1.Unmarshal returns the unconsumed tail of its input; the previous
splitECDSASig discarded it, accepting non-canonical signatures with
arbitrary trailing data. That is a known signature-malleability
hazard and conforming signers never emit such data.

Require asn1.Unmarshal to consume the entire signature and return an
error otherwise. Includes a regression test that appends four bytes
of junk to a valid signature and asserts verification fails closed.

* refactor(v3/updater): share SemVer comparator across providers

The github and appcast providers each shipped a near-byte-identical
isNewer/compareSemver/splitNumeric. Beyond duplication the home-rolled
comparator had three correctness problems flagged in review:

- prereleases sorted *newer* than the corresponding release
  (\"1.2.3-rc.1\" > \"1.2.3\" instead of <)
- build metadata (\"+build.456\") was parsed as a numeric run rather
  than ignored, so two releases that differ only in metadata compared
  as different
- non-semver inputs returned monotonic-ish ordering that depended on
  digit-run alignment

Introduce v3/pkg/updater/internal/semver wrapping golang.org/x/mod/semver
(already an indirect dep — go mod tidy promotes it to direct).
Providers call IsNewer / TrimPrefix; tests cover the prerelease,
numeric-segment, and build-metadata cases that the previous
implementation got wrong.

* fix(v3/updater): wire updater:window:ready handler

The default window template emits updater:window:ready on load to ask
the host for a state snapshot — useful when the window opens after a
periodic-check timer already advanced the flow, e.g. straight into
StateAvailable, so it can't rely on the live event stream alone.

openSession previously registered listeners for the five user-action
events but ignored EventWindowReady, so the window stayed in its
initial \"looking for updates...\" state until the next event fired.

Subscribe to EventWindowReady and replay the lifecycle event matching
the current State (update-available, download-started, verifying,
installing, update-ready, or no-update). Idle / unconfigured / error
have nothing useful to replay and are skipped.

* fix(v3/updater): Windows isAlive used wrong probe

The Windows helper's waitForPID polled isAlive, which called
os.Process.Signal(nil). On Windows that always errors (EWINDOWS for
live processes, ErrProcessDone for dead ones), so isAlive reported
every pid as dead. Result: the helper never actually waited for the
parent to release the binary on Windows — it spun straight into the
swap-retry loop and grinding the file lock.

Split isAlive's per-platform probe into a platformIsAlive helper.

- Unix path: unchanged — proc.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)).
- Windows path: OpenProcess + GetExitCodeProcess. Pulling the exit
  code directly from the kernel distinguishes STILL_ACTIVE (alive)
  from any terminated state without requiring x/sys/windows.

* test(v3/updater): make user-cancel test deterministic

The previous test raced a 10ms time.Sleep against listener
registration in openSession: a slow CI runner could fire
EventUserCancel before openSession installed its handler, so the
cancel was dropped and the 500ms poll loop quietly timed out.

The full CheckAndInstall flow is synchronous when the fake provider
returns immediately, and StateReady leaves the window open by design.
Drive it to completion first (listeners now guaranteed wired), then
fire the cancel emit. fakeHost dispatches callbacks on the calling
goroutine so closeWindow finishes before Emit returns — no polling,
no sleep, no time import.

20x -count run stays green.

* fix(v3/updater): provider robustness improvements

github:
- followAndStrip now preserves a caller-supplied CheckRedirect by
  wrapping it (matches keygen / appcast) and uses
  strings.EqualFold on host comparison.
- isChecksumName is anchored to suffixes / whole tokens so primary
  artifacts whose names contain a hash algorithm (e.g.
  \"myapp-sha256-amd64.zip\") are no longer mis-classified as
  sidecars and silently skipped.

keygen:
- Upgrade response body is now wrapped in io.LimitReader(8 MiB) —
  previously an unbounded io.ReadAll on a misbehaving / compromised

- Check stashes the chosen artifact's keygen.sh ID under
  rel.Metadata[\"keygen.artifact.id\"]; Download prefers that over

- pickArtifact normalises operator-defined aliases via case-
  insensitive matchers — \"macos\" matches darwin, \"x86_64\"/\"x64\"
  matches amd64, \"aarch64\" matches arm64, \"i386\"/\"x86\" matches

Regression tests cover the github false-positive case, the keygen

* fix(v3/updater): runtime injection, event ordering, restart, exec bit

Four fixes from @atterpac's Arch Linux testing on the PR:

- SetHTML on webkit2gtk loads into the about:blank context which
  has no Wails runtime, so the bound JS could not Emit events
  back. Pass the HTML at construction via
  WebviewWindowOptions.HTML instead; drop SetHTML from the
  WindowHandle interface (it was dead surface).

- Wails' EventProcessor.Emit dispatches to listeners + JS on fresh
  goroutines, so events arrive at the frontend out of source
  order (\"installing → verifying → update-ready →
  download-complete\" was observed). Fixing the bus is out of
  scope for this PR; instead make the default window
  state-monotonic — rank the lifecycle states, reject backward
  transitions, gate side effects on setState() returning true,
  and only paint download progress while we're still in the
  downloading state.

- Restart() spawned the helper and returned, leaving the caller
  responsible for app.Quit() — which everyone missed, so the
  helper sat blocked on waitForPID until its 30s timeout. Add
  Quit() to the Host interface, have Restart() call it after
  the spawn so the helper handoff actually completes. Regression
  test mocks the spawn via new export_test.go seams.

- The downloaded artifact is opened with os.Create which masks
  0o666 against umask, dropping the executable bit on Unix. The
  swap renamed it into place and the relaunch then failed with
  EACCES. Snapshot the original target's mode before the swap
  and chmod the new file to match after.

* fix(v3/updater): cross-platform test and macOS bundle path for Restart

TestRestart_QuitsAfterSpawn used /bin/true which doesn't exist on
Windows. Replace with os.Executable + -test.run=^$ so the spawned
command is the test binary itself, running no tests, and exits cleanly
on all platforms.

Restart() passed the raw os.Executable path as WAILS_UPDATER_HELPER_TARGET.
On macOS, swapping the binary inside a .app bundle invalidates the code
signature and Gatekeeper blocks relaunch. bundleTarget() now walks the
path for a .app segment and returns the bundle root on darwin; on all
other platforms it is a no-op passthrough.

Also replace the hand-rolled constantTimeEqual with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare
to handle the length-mismatch case in constant time.

* fix(updater): guard against concurrent DownloadAndInstall calls

Add dlMu sync.Mutex to Updater and TryLock at the top of
DownloadAndInstall. A second caller while a download is already in
progress returns the new ErrDownloadInProgress sentinel immediately
rather than racing on discardStaging and spawning a second download
goroutine.

* fix(updater): security and correctness hardening from review

Six fixes addressing review feedback against the updater design.

* Trust root pinning. Verification.PublicKey is removed from the public
  API; signatures verify against Config.PublicKey and nothing else. The
  earlier model let a Provider populate Release.Verification.PublicKey
  and have it take precedence over Config.PublicKey, which a compromised
  release source could exploit to self-attest with an attacker-chosen
  key. Three existing signed-release tests now thread the key through
  Config via a newConfiguredWithKey helper, and a new
  TestDownloadAndInstall_Signature_RejectsAttackerKey asserts an
  attacker-signed payload is rejected when Config pins a different key.

* CheckAndInstall session race. The previous closeWindow → openSession
  → assign sequence held sessMu only across the final assignment. Two
  concurrent callers could both tear down then reopen, orphaning each
  other's listeners and leaking the half-built window. Hold sessMu for
  the whole sequence.

* Helper aborts on parent-wait timeout. The 30s wait for the parent PID
  used to log "proceeding anyway" and continue. On Windows the swap
  then grinds against the file lock; on macOS `open -n` launches a
  second instance alongside the still-running parent, leaving two
  copies of the app racing on shared state. Abort with exit code 17
  before touching the target instead.

* Keygen artifact list cap. listReleaseArtifacts streamed
  json.NewDecoder(resp.Body) with no size bound. Wrap with
  io.LimitReader(8 MiB), matching the upgrade-envelope cap.

* finaliseDownload filename guards. base == ".." and slash-bearing
  bases would resolve outside the staging tempdir; substitute the
  default wails-update.bin in those cases too.

* Per-PID helper log path. Restart's logPath was a fixed
  wails-update.log under TempDir; concurrent helpers (test runs,
  several Wails apps updating at once) truncated each other's logs.
  Include os.Getpid().

* feat(updater): extract .zip / .tar.gz artifacts before swap

The PR description claimed ".app bundles ... all handled" but the swap
code only ever renamed a single downloaded file into place: a release
shipping MyApp.app as a .zip would have left the helper trying to
replace /Applications/MyApp.app (a directory) with a single .zip file.
Functionally a no-op on macOS — the backup-restore path always
recovered, but no update ever stuck.

DownloadAndInstall now runs an extraction step between finaliseDownload
and StateReady. .zip and .tar.gz / .tgz artifacts are recognised by
filename extension and unpacked in place: the archive is expanded into
a scratch sibling directory, the original archive is removed, and the
single top-level entry of the archive is promoted to where the archive
used to live. Non-archive artifacts pass through untouched, so the
flat-binary distribution model on Linux keeps working without a
configuration change.

Constraints the extractor enforces:

* Exactly one top-level entry per archive — multiple entries are
  ambiguous because the helper swaps into a single target path.
* Zip-slip protection: entries whose normalised path escapes the
  extraction root (via "../" or absolute paths or backslash-slashed
  names from Windows producers) are rejected before any bytes hit
  disk.
* Symlink escape protection: in-archive symlinks must resolve to a
  path inside the extraction root. Absolute targets are refused.
  Internal symlinks (common in .app/Contents/Frameworks layouts) are
  preserved.
* Total uncompressed size capped at 2 GiB and entry count capped at
  50 000 — comfortable headroom for any sane bundle but defends
  against decompression-bomb archives.
* File modes from Unix-produced archives are preserved (so the
  binary inside a .app bundle keeps its +x bit); zero-mode entries
  from Windows-produced archives get safe defaults (0644 / 0755).

The artifact-formats guide in the docs spells out the new rules and
flags .dmg / .pkg / .msi as unsupported (would need hdiutil / xar /
msiexec, out of scope for v1; ship a .zip of the bundle instead).

Tests cover the zip + tar.gz happy paths, single-binary passthrough,
multi-top-level rejection, zip-slip and tar-slip rejection,
symlink-escape rejection, internal-symlink preservation, and an
end-to-end DownloadAndInstall against a synthetic .zip carrying a
.app-shaped tree.

* fix(updater): scrub helper-mode env before launching new binary

End-to-end testing against wailsapp/updater-demo on macOS arm64 surfaced
this: after a successful swap, the launched binary silently exits with
code 11 instead of starting in normal mode.

Cause: exec.Command defaults cmd.Env to os.Environ(), so the new
binary inherits WAILS_UPDATER_HELPER=1 (and the other four sentinels)
that Restart set when it spawned us. HandleHelperMode at the top of the
new process therefore matches, tries to perform another swap against a
staging path we already cleaned up, fails the stat, and exits.

User-visible effect: clicking Restart kills the app and never reopens
it — the update appears to "uninstall" the application.

Fix: clear the sentinels in the helper just before calling launch, so
the new process boots with a clean environment.

Verified on mac-node1 against the live wailsapp/updater-demo v2.0.1
release: before the fix the relaunched binary died with exit 11; after
the fix it boots into the updated Wails app normally. Added
TestRunHelperSwap_ClearsHelperEnvBeforeLaunch as a regression.

* fix(updater): rename target aside on Windows instead of unlinking

End-to-end testing against wailsapp/updater-demo on Windows 11 amd64
surfaced this: the helper retried os.Remove(target) 20 times over 10
seconds and every attempt failed with "Access is denied," then the
backup-restore failed for the same reason. The user-visible effect was
that the swap never succeeded — Windows updates were broken.

Cause: even though the parent process has exited (verified via
GetExitCodeProcess returning STILL_ACTIVE → exited), Windows holds the
executable's image file long enough that direct deletion fails. The
loader cleanup is not synchronous with process exit, and our 10s retry
budget wasn't enough.

Windows does, however, permit renaming a file whose image is still
mapped — only deletion is blocked. So we lift the swap logic into a
platform-specific helper:

* Unix (helper_unix.go) keeps the existing RemoveAll + Rename — open
  fds remain valid against the unlinked inode, and .app bundles need
  RemoveAll for directories.
* Windows (helper_windows.go) tries the cheap path first (in case
  nothing is holding the file), and on failure renames target aside
  to "<target>.old.<nanos>" and moves newPath into the freed slot.
  The .old file is deleted best-effort; if the kernel still has it
  open, the leftover sits next to the binary harmlessly until a later
  sweep or app uninstall.

Verified end-to-end on win-node1: the same swap that previously
exhausted 20 retries now succeeds first try, and the relaunched binary
boots in normal mode (the env-scrub from e4a436c is what gets us there
once the swap completes).

* fix(updater/windows): sweep stale .old siblings on next swap

The rename-aside trick leaves a .<target>.old.<nanos> sibling behind
because the kernel often holds the just-renamed binary's image open
for a while after process exit, and our immediate best-effort delete
fails. Without a sweep, every Windows update grows the install
directory by one stale executable.

On the next update the helper now globs <target>.old.* and removes
whatever it can — the previous update's leftover is normally
deletable by then. Best-effort: anything still held by the kernel
gets skipped and tried again the update after.

* fix(updater): wire JS event channel + redesign default window

The updater window was rendering its initial static HTML on every
platform — JS event handlers never received state updates from Go.

Cause: the old template polled `window.wails.Events.On`, but the Wails
v3 runtime exposes Events only as an ES module export from /runtime.js.
That bundle can't be imported from an InitialHTML page either, because
`loadHTMLString:baseURL:nil` (macOS) and `NavigateToString` (Windows)
load the page with `window.location.origin === "null"` so the modern
HTTP-fetch transport fails for relative URLs. The previous "modern runtime
exposes Events on window.wails" assumption was simply wrong.

Two fixes:

1. **Page side** — replace the broken polling with a minimal shim. Install
   `window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent` ourselves to receive events (the
   framework's pre-injected `window._wails` doesn't provide it), and emit
   user actions via the existing `window._wails.invoke` postMessage
   channel. After invoke becomes available, fire `wails:runtime:ready` to
   flush the ExecJS pending-queue — without this signal every state
   event the framework dispatched during page load sat in `pendingJS`
   forever and the UI never advanced past the initial HTML.

2. **Framework side** — add a `wails:event:emit:<name>` case in
   `WebviewWindow.HandleMessage` so InitialHTML pages have a return
   channel. Bare names only (no payload) — enough for user-action
   buttons; pages that need structured data should use the full runtime.

While I was in there, redesigned the template itself:

- Hero icon + state-driven colour (blue for available/downloading, green
  for ready/up-to-date, red for error).
- Version pill: `v1.0.0 → v2.0.1 · 8.8 MB` so users know what they're
  installing and how big it is.
- Scrollable release-notes panel sized for multi-paragraph notes
  (60–240 px, grows with window).
- State-driven visibility via `data-show` attributes: each state shows
  only what's relevant. No more "Update Available" header with
  "Looking for updates…" body desync.
- Single clear primary action per state (Install / Restart & Apply / Try
  Again); secondaries (Skip / Remind) demoted to ghost buttons.
- Indeterminate progress shimmer when total size is unknown, real progress
  bar with percentage + bytes + rate when known.
- Spinner during checking/verifying/installing.
- Better default dimensions: 520×540 (was 480×420) to fit release notes
  comfortably.
- System fonts: -apple-system / Segoe UI Variable / Inter.

Discovered while capturing screenshots on lin-node1 (Xvfb + scrot) and
win-node1 (PrintWindow + scheduled task in the multica console session).
Confirmed working end-to-end on macOS — the captures show real state
transitions populating version, release notes, and the correct primary
action.

* fix(linux): bind webkit messageHandlers.external.postMessage receiver

Direct testing of the updater window on lin-node1 (Ubuntu 26.04 GTK4 +
WebKitGTK 2.52.3) revealed every `window._wails.invoke(...)` call from
the page silently dropping on the floor. The Wails runtime Core JS was
loaded, `_wails.invoke` was a function, but no script messages ever
reached `sendMessageToBackend` on the Go side.

Cause: the historical Linux setup was a bare reference assignment

    window._wails.invoke=window.webkit.messageHandlers.external.postMessage;

When code later called `window._wails.invoke(msg)`, the `this` receiver
became the global object instead of the handler. WebKitGTK's
postMessage refuses the call without surfacing an error to JS — the
message is just lost. Darwin already wraps the call in a closure for
the same reason; Windows works either way because WebView2's
postMessage tolerates the loose receiver. Match darwin's pattern.

Bonus: this also lifts the broken "JS event emits work" comment in the
helper-mode commit message into something true on Linux.

* feat(updater): wire Config.CheckInterval — the docs claimed it, code didn't

The Config field has shipped since the original commit with the
"Pop-up-on-found behaviour is the same as a manual Check" promise but
zero implementation behind it — the value was read into the struct and
never consulted again. Init now starts a goroutine on a ticker when

session-setup machinery as a manual click.

Ticks that arrive while a flow is already in progress (checking /
downloading / verifying / installing) are dropped — concurrent state
machines aren't supported and CheckAndInstall's own lock would defer

* feat(updater): public BYOWindow constructor + WebviewWindow.AsUpdaterWindow

The BYO path was nominally supported by the type switch in
classifyWindowOption (case WindowHandle:) but unreachable in practice
— Config.Window is typed as WindowOption with an unexported marker
method that *application.WebviewWindow can't satisfy, and a
WebviewWindow's fluent Show()/Close() return types don't match
WindowHandle's bare Show()/Close() signatures either. The path was
dead code.

Two bridges close the gap:

  updater.BYOWindow(handle)        — wraps any WindowHandle into a
                                     WindowOption usable in Config.Window.
  (*WebviewWindow).AsUpdaterWindow() — returns the existing
                                     updaterWindowHandle adapter that
                                     reconciles the fluent/bare method
                                     signature difference.

Together:

  myWin := app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{...})
  app.Updater.Init(updater.Config{
      Window: updater.BYOWindow(myWin.AsUpdaterWindow()),
      ...,
  })

updater drives a completely custom-styled WebviewWindow (pink
gradient, no builtin CSS) through the full Check / Download / Verify /

* fix: xbps InstallCommand type mismatch + two-pass symlink extraction

Two unrelated CI failures on the latest merge of master:

* internal/doctor/packagemanager/xbps.go and pkg/doctor-ng/packagemanager/xbps.go
  copied a v2-shaped expression into v3 — `pkg.InstallCommand[x.osid]`
  indexes a `string` by a `string`. The v3 Package struct made
  InstallCommand a flat string (matching the other v3 PMs); xbps just
  needs to return it directly like apt/dnf do.

* CodeQL's go/unsafe-unzip-symlink rule flagged the archive extractor
  for the classic zip-slip-via-symlink escalation: planting a symlink
  followed by a write through it (archive contains "link → /etc",
  then "link/passwd" — the write resolves the symlink and escapes
  root). The existing root-relative check on the symlink target is
  necessary but not sufficient.

  Standard mitigation: two-pass extraction. Pass 1 writes regular
  files and directories only, recording symlinks as pending. Pass 2
  creates the symlinks last. Because no symlink exists on disk
  during pass 1, no file write can be redirected through one.
  Pass-1 symlink entries are still validated up-front so a malicious
  archive is rejected before any disk work happens. Pass 2 re-runs
  the same validation as defence in depth.

Both fixes verified by go test + cross-build on darwin/linux/windows.

change, but it's blocking the PR from going green.

* feat(application): gate wails:event:emit on AllowSimpleEventEmit + docs/screenshots

The `wails:event:emit:<name>` postMessage shortcut introduced for the
updater's InitialHTML window was wired globally — every WebviewWindow
in every Wails app accepted it. Apps that load any untrusted HTML
(remote URLs, user-supplied content) into a webview gained an
unintended attack surface: a compromised page could synthesise any
custom event the host code listens for via
`window._wails.invoke("wails:event:emit:whatever")`. Bare names only,
no payload, no binding bypass — but privileged custom-event handlers
were exposed.

Add an opt-in field, WebviewWindowOptions.AllowSimpleEventEmit
(default false). Handler now rejects the message unless the window
opted in. The updater's framework-owned window sets it internally;
BYO updater windows set it explicitly via WebviewWindowOptions.

    GoDoc threat-model documentation.
  * pkg/application/webview_window.go — gate the existing handler
    on the new field.
  * pkg/application/updater_host.go — opt the updater's builtin
    window in. Also expanded AsUpdaterWindow's GoDoc to document
    the BYO requirement.
  * cmd/updater-ui-driver-byo/main.go — set the field so the live
    BYO driver continues to work as a working example.

* docs(updater): make screenshot window corners transparent

The PNGs Peekaboo produced had a thin white buffer in the four corners
where the macOS window's rounded edge curved inward but the PNG
bounding rectangle was still solid. Two earlier attempts to handle
this in CSS (border-radius 12px, then no clip with box-shadow) each
showed slightly different artefacts — the radius cut into the
window content past the curve, the no-clip version showed white
slivers in the corners.

Fix it at the source: flood-fill near-white pixels reachable from
each corner with alpha=0, fading anti-aliased edge pixels so the
curve still looks smooth. After the pass, the PNG's alpha channel
matches the actual macOS window outline. No CSS clipping needed,
and the `filter: drop-shadow()` already in place now follows the
real window shape because drop-shadow respects alpha.

Verified the (0,0)/(3,3) corners are alpha=0 and the (5,5)/(6,6)
content interior is alpha=255 in all three doc assets.

* docs(updater): more aggressive corner transparency + crop to bust browser cache

Two layered issues in the previous pass:

* The flood-fill cut-off was too lenient (brightness >= 240). The macOS
  title bar's TOP-edge gradient is around brightness 200–225, which fell
  outside the cut-off and stayed opaque. Against a light docs page
  background those pixels read as white artifacts hugging the corners.
  Lower the cut-off to 180; anti-aliased pixels in the 120-180 band get
  a linearly interpolated alpha so the curve still looks smooth, just
  with the lightest title-bar gradient pixels faded.

* Astro generates /_image URLs keyed by source path + dimensions but
  not by content. When we updated the PNGs in place, the URL stayed
  identical and browsers happily reused the cached webp from the
  previous build. Crop 2 px off the top of each PNG: it shaves the
  lightest title-bar gradient stripe AND changes origHeight in the
  generated URL (571 → 569), forcing a cache miss on next load.

feat(v3): app.Updater with pluggable Provider interface + GitHub / keygen.sh / AppCast providers (#5449)

* feat(v3): add updater package with pluggable Provider interface

Introduces app.Updater — a singleton update orchestrator wired into
application.App. End users configure it once via Init then drive it with
Check / DownloadAndInstall / CheckAndInstall.

The Provider interface (Name / Check / Download) lets any release source
back the updater — GitHub Releases, keygen.sh, AppCast feeds, custom — with
verification, atomic writes, swap and the default window all owned by the
Updater rather than the provider.

Verification is built in: Ed25519, Ed25519ph (pre-hash, SHA-512) and
ECDSA-P256 over SHA-256, with digest-only mode supported. The internal
verifier registry is unexported in v1 so we can promote it to a public
RegisterVerifier later without breaking callers.

Subscribe to lifecycle events through the standard Wails event bus — both
Go and JavaScript use the same `updater:*` event names. Event constants
exported on the package with payload types documented inline.

This commit lands the interface, types, verification, atomic download with
streaming digest, and a fake-Provider test suite (19 tests). Window
template, binary swap, restart, GitHub/keygen.sh/AppCast providers and
docs follow in subsequent commits.

* feat(v3/updater): same-binary helper-mode swap + Restart

Add the swap-and-relaunch step that completes the update flow without
asking the user to deal with overwriting-a-running-binary on any platform.

Implements the inconshreveable/go-update pattern: when the Updater calls
Restart, the app re-execs itself with sentinel env vars. application.New
detects those vars at startup, hands control to runHelperSwap, and the
parent exits. The helper-mode process waits for the parent PID to die,
backs up the running binary, retries an atomic rename of the new artifact
into place (Windows file-lock safety net), launches the replaced binary,
and self-destructs the backup.

Handles macOS .app bundles correctly via recursive copy/symlink-aware
traversal, falls back to a single-file path for plain executables on
Linux and Windows, and rolls back to the backup if either the swap or
the relaunch fails so a broken update never leaves the app unbootable.

No extra binary shipped: the helper IS the app, switched into helper
mode by env vars. Cross-builds clean for darwin/linux/windows. Seven new
swap-logic tests plus the existing 19 keep the package at 26 green.

* feat(v3/updater): default window, BYO escape hatch, headless mode

Built-in HTML/CSS/JS template that listens to updater:* events and emits
updater:user:* actions back to Go — no framework-specific tags, no custom
elements, just plain Wails events through the runtime. Dark-mode CSS
variables, status / progress / release-notes panels, four action buttons
(Install / Skip / Remind / Cancel) plus a Restart button visible only in
the ready state. Override the whole template via BuiltinWindow.HTML, layer
extra CSS via BuiltinWindow.CSS, tweak chrome (frameless/size/AOT) via
BuiltinWindow.Options.

Window option types: nil → defaults, *BuiltinWindow → overrides, any value
satisfying updater.WindowHandle (e.g. *application.WebviewWindow) → BYO,
updater.WindowNone → headless.

Host interface gains OpenWindow + OnEvent so the updater package can drive
real Wails windows without importing application. The application package
supplies an adapter (newUpdaterHost) that wraps *EventManager and
*WindowManager.NewWithOptions, plus a small updaterWindowHandle that
trims the fluent return values off SetHTML/Show/Hide.

User-action listeners are wired the moment a session opens, dispatching
updater:user:install → DownloadAndInstall, updater:user:cancel →
closeWindow, updater:user:skip → SkipVersion + close, updater:user:remind
→ close, updater:user:restart → Restart. Skipped versions short-circuit
subsequent Checks to up-to-date until cleared.

8 new lifecycle tests on top of the prior 26; full suite 34 green. App
package tests still green.

* feat(v3/updater): GitHub Releases provider

First provider implementation: hits api.github.com (or a configurable base
URL for GitHub Enterprise), picks an asset by GOOS/GOARCH heuristics, and
optionally pulls a sibling SHA256SUMS-style checksum file to populate
Release.Verification — letting the framework's verifier authenticate the
download with zero extra config from the user.

Asset matching defaults to substring-of-platform AND substring-of-arch on
the filename, skipping .sig / .asc / *sum* sidecars. Recognises the common
arch aliases (amd64 ↔ x86_64/x64, arm64 ↔ aarch64, 386 ↔ i386/x86/ia32).
Custom selection via Config.AssetMatcher.

Auth via Bearer PAT raises rate limits and unlocks private repos. Download
follows the asset's signed redirect and strips Authorization on the
cross-host hop so the token never reaches the storage backend.

Eleven httptest tests cover the happy path, up-to-date / 404, prerelease
toggle, asset filter, missing match, checksum-sidecar verification, the
redirect-and-strip flow, validation, and API-error surfacing.

* feat(v3/updater): keygen.sh provider

Port the keygen.sh integration written previously into the Wails v3
updater Provider shape. Key adaptation: keygen's per-artifact base64
checksum (SHA-512) and signature (Ed25519ph) fields now flow into
Release.Verification, so the framework's verifier authenticates the
download automatically once the consumer has set Config.PublicKey on the
Updater — no provider-specific verification path.

Handles keygen.sh quirks discovered while building the original library:
the /upgrade endpoint silently drops ?include=artifacts (fallback fetch
to /releases/{id}/artifacts), the artifact download 303s to Cloudflare R2
on a different host (CheckRedirect wrapper drops Authorization on cross-
origin hops), and 404 from /upgrade means "no newer release" rather than
a hard error.

Auth supports either Token (admi-/prod-/envi-/user- prefixed values) or
LicenseKey, with Token winning when both are set. Typed APIError surfaces
the keygen JSON error envelope (title / detail / code / status) for
debuggable failures.

Eleven httptest tests cover the happy path with verification mapping,
404=up-to-date, both auth schemes, error surfacing, no-matching artifact,
the include=artifacts fallback, the redirect-strip flow, validation, and
the Provider-interface assertion.

* feat(v3/updater): Sparkle-compatible AppCast provider

Parses the canonical Sparkle XML vocabulary so existing Sparkle/WinSparkle
feeds drop in unchanged: items are picked by sparkle:shortVersionString
(falling back to sparkle:version), the download comes from <enclosure>,
and Sparkle 2's sparkle:edSignature flows into Release.Verification as an
Ed25519 signature for the framework's verifier.

Item selection reconciles Sparkle's loose OS naming ("macos"/"mac"/"osx"
all map to Go's "darwin"), and a Config.Channel filter narrows to one
sparkle:channel when the feed publishes multiple. Sparkle 1's
sparkle:dsaSignature is intentionally not supported — projects on DSA
should rotate to EdDSA per Sparkle 2's guidance.

Ten httptest tests cover the happy path with verification, Windows
selection, up-to-date short-circuit, no-platform-match, 404=up-to-date,
500=error, channel filtering, download streaming with progress,
URL-required validation, and the Provider interface assertion.

* docs(v3): updater guide + runnable example

Docs cover the 30-second quick start, the three built-in providers
(GitHub Releases / keygen.sh / Sparkle AppCast) with config knobs,
fallback chain semantics, cryptographic verification (Ed25519, Ed25519ph,
ECDSA-P256, digest-only), default-window theming through CSS variables,
full template replacement, window chrome override, BYO via
application.Window, headless mode, the full event taxonomy for both Go
and JavaScript, how to write your own provider, and how the same-binary
helper-mode swap works under the hood.

Example app exercises the GitHub provider end-to-end: APP_VERSION +
GH_REPOSITORY env vars, "Check for Updates…" menu item that drives
CheckAndInstall, a small JS-side log mirroring updater:* events
alongside the framework's default window.

* chore(v3/updater): mechanical cleanups from PR review

- Drop dead import-stabilising stubs: `var _ = url.Parse` + `net/url`
  import in github.go, `var _ = errors.New` in github_test.go, `var _
  = io.EOF` in appcast_test.go.
- Drop dead `sessionMu` type from window_lifecycle.go (never used —
  Updater uses a plain sync.Mutex named sessMu).
- Remove the `req.Header.Set(\"Accept\", req.Header.Get(\"Accept\"))`
  no-op round-trip in github.Provider.setAuth.
- Replace hand-rolled path concatenation with filepath.Join in
  download.go.
- Drop the unused `target` parameter and vestigial `_ = path` /
  `_ = target` blanks from openHelperLog.
- Use filepath.Dir instead of hand-rolled \"/\"-based parentOf in
  updater_test.go (broke on Windows).
- Drop the package-level mockHost in github_test.go in favour of a
  test-local host variable (so future t.Parallel() doesn't race).
- writeFile uses 0o644 for files instead of 0o755.

* fix(v3/updater): tear down prior session in CheckAndInstall

Each invocation of CheckAndInstall registered 5 fresh user-action
listeners under sessMu but never closed any previous session. A
periodic-check timer firing alongside a manual click (or two clicks)
would leak listeners and windows; stale callbacks would still fire on
the next user action, double-invoking DownloadAndInstall or Restart.

Close any active session before opening the new one, and add a
regression test that exercises three back-to-back CheckAndInstall
calls and asserts the host's listener map is empty afterwards.

* fix(v3/updater): clean up wails-update-* staging directory

The download flow created an os.MkdirTemp(\"\", \"wails-update-*\")
directory and staged the artifact inside. Two leak paths left orphan
directories under os.TempDir across update attempts:

- success path: after Restart spawned the helper and the helper renamed
  the staged binary into place, the (now-empty) directory persisted.
- error paths: \`_ = os.Remove(tmpPath)\` removed the staged file but
  left the enclosing dir.

Plus, when digestHasher errored before any download bytes flowed, the
freshly-created directory was leaked outright (flagged by CodeRabbit).

Three coordinated changes:

1. download() now returns (path, dir, err) and tears the directory
   down on every error path via a single deferred RemoveAll guarded by
   a success bool — including the hasher-setup branch.
2. Updater tracks stagingDir alongside resolved; DownloadAndInstall
   removes any stale dir before downloading again and RemoveAll's the
   current dir on verify/install failures.
3. runHelperSwap removes the parent directory of newPath after a
   successful rename, guarded by the \`wails-update-\` prefix so a
   caller-supplied path outside the temp area can never be deleted by
   accident.

Adds a TempDir-counting regression test to keep this from regressing.

* fix(v3/updater): inject BuiltinWindow.CSS inside <head>

The previous composeHTML appended the override <style> tag after the
closing </html> of the default template, producing a malformed
document that HTML linters and CSP-strict configurations reject.

Splice the extra <style> before </head> when one is present so the
result stays well-formed. Custom-HTML templates without </head> fall
back to appending at the document end with a comment.

Tightens the existing CSS-injection test to assert the override sits
before both </head> and </html>.

* fix(v3/updater/github): skip drafts in prerelease release listing

\`/repos/{r}/releases\` includes draft releases when the request is
authenticated, and \`per_page=1\` plus a recently-created draft would
surface that draft as an available update instead of the actual
latest prerelease. Asymmetric with the non-prerelease path, which
hits \`/releases/latest\` and is already draft-free.

Fetch up to 10 items and return the first non-draft, adding a
regression test that injects a draft at the top of the list.

* fix(v3/updater): reject ECDSA DER signatures with trailing bytes

asn1.Unmarshal returns the unconsumed tail of its input; the previous
splitECDSASig discarded it, accepting non-canonical signatures with
arbitrary trailing data. That is a known signature-malleability
hazard and conforming signers never emit such data.

Require asn1.Unmarshal to consume the entire signature and return an
error otherwise. Includes a regression test that appends four bytes
of junk to a valid signature and asserts verification fails closed.

* refactor(v3/updater): share SemVer comparator across providers

The github and appcast providers each shipped a near-byte-identical
isNewer/compareSemver/splitNumeric. Beyond duplication the home-rolled
comparator had three correctness problems flagged in review:

- prereleases sorted *newer* than the corresponding release
  (\"1.2.3-rc.1\" > \"1.2.3\" instead of <)
- build metadata (\"+build.456\") was parsed as a numeric run rather
  than ignored, so two releases that differ only in metadata compared
  as different
- non-semver inputs returned monotonic-ish ordering that depended on
  digit-run alignment

Introduce v3/pkg/updater/internal/semver wrapping golang.org/x/mod/semver
(already an indirect dep — go mod tidy promotes it to direct).
Providers call IsNewer / TrimPrefix; tests cover the prerelease,
numeric-segment, and build-metadata cases that the previous
implementation got wrong.

* fix(v3/updater): wire updater:window:ready handler

The default window template emits updater:window:ready on load to ask
the host for a state snapshot — useful when the window opens after a
periodic-check timer already advanced the flow, e.g. straight into
StateAvailable, so it can't rely on the live event stream alone.

openSession previously registered listeners for the five user-action
events but ignored EventWindowReady, so the window stayed in its
initial \"looking for updates...\" state until the next event fired.

Subscribe to EventWindowReady and replay the lifecycle event matching
the current State (update-available, download-started, verifying,
installing, update-ready, or no-update). Idle / unconfigured / error
have nothing useful to replay and are skipped.

* fix(v3/updater): Windows isAlive used wrong probe

The Windows helper's waitForPID polled isAlive, which called
os.Process.Signal(nil). On Windows that always errors (EWINDOWS for
live processes, ErrProcessDone for dead ones), so isAlive reported
every pid as dead. Result: the helper never actually waited for the
parent to release the binary on Windows — it spun straight into the
swap-retry loop and grinding the file lock.

Split isAlive's per-platform probe into a platformIsAlive helper.

- Unix path: unchanged — proc.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)).
- Windows path: OpenProcess + GetExitCodeProcess. Pulling the exit
  code directly from the kernel distinguishes STILL_ACTIVE (alive)
  from any terminated state without requiring x/sys/windows.

* test(v3/updater): make user-cancel test deterministic

The previous test raced a 10ms time.Sleep against listener
registration in openSession: a slow CI runner could fire
EventUserCancel before openSession installed its handler, so the
cancel was dropped and the 500ms poll loop quietly timed out.

The full CheckAndInstall flow is synchronous when the fake provider
returns immediately, and StateReady leaves the window open by design.
Drive it to completion first (listeners now guaranteed wired), then
fire the cancel emit. fakeHost dispatches callbacks on the calling
goroutine so closeWindow finishes before Emit returns — no polling,
no sleep, no time import.

20x -count run stays green.

* fix(v3/updater): provider robustness improvements

github:
- followAndStrip now preserves a caller-supplied CheckRedirect by
  wrapping it (matches keygen / appcast) and uses
  strings.EqualFold on host comparison.
- isChecksumName is anchored to suffixes / whole tokens so primary
  artifacts whose names contain a hash algorithm (e.g.
  \"myapp-sha256-amd64.zip\") are no longer mis-classified as
  sidecars and silently skipped.

keygen:
- Upgrade response body is now wrapped in io.LimitReader(8 MiB) —
  previously an unbounded io.ReadAll on a misbehaving / compromised
  endpoint could OOM the host.
- Check stashes the chosen artifact's keygen.sh ID under
  rel.Metadata[\"keygen.artifact.id\"]; Download prefers that over
  the filename so releases that ship two artifacts with the same
  filename across platforms are unambiguous.
- pickArtifact normalises operator-defined aliases via case-
  insensitive matchers — \"macos\" matches darwin, \"x86_64\"/\"x64\"
  matches amd64, \"aarch64\" matches arm64, \"i386\"/\"x86\" matches
  386.

appcast:
- Download explicitly clears any Authorization header on the
  enclosure request — even though Check never sets one, a caller-
  supplied default on the http.Request would otherwise leak
  cross-origin on the initial CDN hop (the redirect wrapper only
  covers subsequent hops).

Regression tests cover the github false-positive case, the keygen
ID stash + download-by-ID flow, and the keygen alias matching.

* fix(v3/updater): three follow-up review nits

- appcast.pickBestItem: an explicit Config.Channel no longer matches
  items that ship without a sparkle:channel. Sparkle's contract is
  that items opt *in* to a channel, so the previous
  "channel mismatch only if both sides non-empty" check could leak
  unlabelled (stable-default) items into a non-stable filter.
- github.containsArch: a 386 request no longer false-positive-matches
  x86_64 / amd64 / x64 assets through the bare "x86" alias. 64-bit
  aliases on the filename now veto a 386 match outright.
- window_test custom-HTML assertion: guard the 60-char preview slice
  so a short InitialHTML doesn't panic and mask the real failure.

Regression tests cover both provider fixes.

* test(v3/updater/github): pin linux/386 edge case in matcher table

The existing TestDefaultAssetMatcher_386_DoesNotMatchX86_64 covers
this in a dedicated test, but adding the case to the table-driven
TestDefaultAssetMatcher keeps the alias check next to the other
matcher cases — where future readers (and reviewers) naturally look
when expanding the matrix. Suggested in CodeRabbit's review nitpick.

* docs(v3/examples/updater): default to wailsapp/updater-demo

The previous default of wailsapp/wails fails because Wails' own
release artifacts don't match the platform-naming heuristic the
updater's DefaultAssetMatcher expects ("darwin"/"arm64" tokens in
the filename, no `wails*` suffix etc.) — running the example
out-of-the-box surfaces "no asset for darwin/arm64" instead of
demoing the actual flow.

Point at wailsapp/updater-demo, a dedicated repo whose releases
publish updater-demo_<goos>_<goarch>.<ext> archives plus a
SHA256SUMS sidecar. The example also opts into ChecksumAsset
verification by default so digest-mismatch is exercised on first
run. Env-var overrides still work for users pointing at their own
repos.

* docs(v3/updater): drop misleading wailsapp/wails example repo

The GitHub-provider example config used \`Repository: \"wailsapp/wails\"\`
which suggests pointing at the wails repository itself — but wails's
own release artifacts don't match the updater's filename heuristics
("darwin"/"arm64" tokens, no \`wails*\` prefix). A first-time user
copy/pasting hits "no asset for darwin/arm64" instead of seeing the
flow work.

Use \`myorg/myapp\` to match the Quick Start at the top of the page,
and call out the runnable example + its dedicated demo repo right
under the snippet so readers know where to look for a working
end-to-end target.

* docs(v3/examples/updater): clarify the two verification modes

The README's Verification section talked only about
publicKey/signature verification, but the example now ships
ChecksumAsset: \"SHA256SUMS\" by default — so digest verification
runs out of the box against the demo repo's sidecar. Lead with
that (matching what the example actually does), then describe
the publicKey path as the next step up.

* fix(v3/updater): runtime injection, event ordering, restart, exec bit

Four fixes from @atterpac's Arch Linux testing on the PR:

- SetHTML on webkit2gtk loads into the about:blank context which
  has no Wails runtime, so the bound JS could not Emit events
  back. Pass the HTML at construction via
  WebviewWindowOptions.HTML instead; drop SetHTML from the
  WindowHandle interface (it was dead surface).

- Wails' EventProcessor.Emit dispatches to listeners + JS on fresh
  goroutines, so events arrive at the frontend out of source
  order (\"installing → verifying → update-ready →
  download-complete\" was observed). Fixing the bus is out of
  scope for this PR; instead make the default window
  state-monotonic — rank the lifecycle states, reject backward
  transitions, gate side effects on setState() returning true,
  and only paint download progress while we're still in the
  downloading state.

- Restart() spawned the helper and returned, leaving the caller
  responsible for app.Quit() — which everyone missed, so the
  helper sat blocked on waitForPID until its 30s timeout. Add
  Quit() to the Host interface, have Restart() call it after
  the spawn so the helper handoff actually completes. Regression
  test mocks the spawn via new export_test.go seams.

- The downloaded artifact is opened with os.Create which masks
  0o666 against umask, dropping the executable bit on Unix. The
  swap renamed it into place and the relaunch then failed with
  EACCES. Snapshot the original target's mode before the swap
  and chmod the new file to match after.

* fix(v3/updater): cross-platform test and macOS bundle path for Restart

TestRestart_QuitsAfterSpawn used /bin/true which doesn't exist on
Windows. Replace with os.Executable + -test.run=^$ so the spawned
command is the test binary itself, running no tests, and exits cleanly
on all platforms.

Restart() passed the raw os.Executable path as WAILS_UPDATER_HELPER_TARGET.
On macOS, swapping the binary inside a .app bundle invalidates the code
signature and Gatekeeper blocks relaunch. bundleTarget() now walks the
path for a .app segment and returns the bundle root on darwin; on all
other platforms it is a no-op passthrough.

Also replace the hand-rolled constantTimeEqual with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare
to handle the length-mismatch case in constant time.

* fix(updater): guard against concurrent DownloadAndInstall calls

Add dlMu sync.Mutex to Updater and TryLock at the top of
DownloadAndInstall. A second caller while a download is already in
progress returns the new ErrDownloadInProgress sentinel immediately
rather than racing on discardStaging and spawning a second download
goroutine.

* fix(updater): security and correctness hardening from review

Six fixes addressing review feedback against the updater design.

* Trust root pinning. Verification.PublicKey is removed from the public
  API; signatures verify against Config.PublicKey and nothing else. The
  earlier model let a Provider populate Release.Verification.PublicKey
  and have it take precedence over Config.PublicKey, which a compromised
  release source could exploit to self-attest with an attacker-chosen
  key. Three existing signed-release tests now thread the key through
  Config via a newConfiguredWithKey helper, and a new
  TestDownloadAndInstall_Signature_RejectsAttackerKey asserts an
  attacker-signed payload is rejected when Config pins a different key.

* CheckAndInstall session race. The previous closeWindow → openSession
  → assign sequence held sessMu only across the final assignment. Two
  concurrent callers could both tear down then reopen, orphaning each
  other's listeners and leaking the half-built window. Hold sessMu for
  the whole sequence.

* Helper aborts on parent-wait timeout. The 30s wait for the parent PID
  used to log "proceeding anyway" and continue. On Windows the swap
  then grinds against the file lock; on macOS `open -n` launches a
  second instance alongside the still-running parent, leaving two
  copies of the app racing on shared state. Abort with exit code 17
  before touching the target instead.

* Keygen artifact list cap. listReleaseArtifacts streamed
  json.NewDecoder(resp.Body) with no size bound. Wrap with
  io.LimitReader(8 MiB), matching the upgrade-envelope cap.

* finaliseDownload filename guards. base == ".." and slash-bearing
  bases would resolve outside the staging tempdir; substitute the
  default wails-update.bin in those cases too.

* Per-PID helper log path. Restart's logPath was a fixed
  wails-update.log under TempDir; concurrent helpers (test runs,
  several Wails apps updating at once) truncated each other's logs.
  Include os.Getpid().

* feat(updater): extract .zip / .tar.gz artifacts before swap

The PR description claimed ".app bundles ... all handled" but the swap
code only ever renamed a single downloaded file into place: a release
shipping MyApp.app as a .zip would have left the helper trying to
replace /Applications/MyApp.app (a directory) with a single .zip file.
Functionally a no-op on macOS — the backup-restore path always
recovered, but no update ever stuck.

DownloadAndInstall now runs an extraction step between finaliseDownload
and StateReady. .zip and .tar.gz / .tgz artifacts are recognised by
filename extension and unpacked in place: the archive is expanded into
a scratch sibling directory, the original archive is removed, and the
single top-level entry of the archive is promoted to where the archive
used to live. Non-archive artifacts pass through untouched, so the
flat-binary distribution model on Linux keeps working without a
configuration change.

Constraints the extractor enforces:

* Exactly one top-level entry per archive — multiple entries are
  ambiguous because the helper swaps into a single target path.
* Zip-slip protection: entries whose normalised path escapes the
  extraction root (via "../" or absolute paths or backslash-slashed
  names from Windows producers) are rejected before any bytes hit
  disk.
* Symlink escape protection: in-archive symlinks must resolve to a
  path inside the extraction root. Absolute targets are refused.
  Internal symlinks (common in .app/Contents/Frameworks layouts) are
  preserved.
* Total uncompressed size capped at 2 GiB and entry count capped at
  50 000 — comfortable headroom for any sane bundle but defends
  against decompression-bomb archives.
* File modes from Unix-produced archives are preserved (so the
  binary inside a .app bundle keeps its +x bit); zero-mode entries
  from Windows-produced archives get safe defaults (0644 / 0755).

The artifact-formats guide in the docs spells out the new rules and
flags .dmg / .pkg / .msi as unsupported (would need hdiutil / xar /
msiexec, out of scope for v1; ship a .zip of the bundle instead).

* fix(updater): scrub helper-mode env before launching new binary

End-to-end testing against wailsapp/updater-demo on macOS arm64 surfaced
this: after a successful swap, the launched binary silently exits with
code 11 instead of starting in normal mode.

Cause: exec.Command defaults cmd.Env to os.Environ(), so the new
binary inherits WAILS_UPDATER_HELPER=1 (and the other four sentinels)
that Restart set when it spawned us. HandleHelperMode at the top of the
new process therefore matches, tries to perform another swap against a
staging path we already cleaned up, fails the stat, and exits.

User-visible effect: clicking Restart kills the app and never reopens
it — the update appears to "uninstall" the application.

Fix: clear the sentinels in the helper just before calling launch, so
the new process boots with a clean environment.

Verified on mac-node1 against the live wailsapp/updater-demo v2.0.1
release: before the fix the relaunched binary died with exit 11; after
the fix it boots into the updated Wails app normally. Added
TestRunHelperSwap_ClearsHelperEnvBeforeLaunch as a regression.

* fix(updater): rename target aside on Windows instead of unlinking

End-to-end testing against wailsapp/updater-demo on Windows 11 amd64
surfaced this: the helper retried os.Remove(target) 20 times over 10
seconds and every attempt failed with "Access is denied," then the
backup-restore failed for the same reason. The user-visible effect was
that the swap never succeeded — Windows updates were broken.

Cause: even though the parent process has exited (verified via
GetExitCodeProcess returning STILL_ACTIVE → exited), Windows holds the
executable's image file long enough that direct deletion fails. The
loader cleanup is not synchronous with process exit, and our 10s retry
budget wasn't enough.

Windows does, however, permit renaming a file whose image is still
mapped — only deletion is blocked. So we lift the swap logic into a
platform-specific helper:

* Unix (helper_unix.go) keeps the existing RemoveAll + Rename — open
  fds remain valid against the unlinked inode, and .app bundles need
  RemoveAll for directories.
* Windows (helper_windows.go) tries the cheap path first (in case
  nothing is holding the file), and on failure renames target aside
  to "<target>.old.<nanos>" and moves newPath into the freed slot.
  The .old file is deleted best-effort; if the kernel still has it
  open, the leftover sits next to the binary harmlessly until a later
  sweep or app uninstall.

Verified end-to-end on win-node1: the same swap that previously
exhausted 20 retries now succeeds first try, and the relaunched binary
boots in normal mode (the env-scrub from e4a436c is what gets us there
once the swap completes).

* fix(updater/windows): sweep stale .old siblings on next swap

The rename-aside trick leaves a .<target>.old.<nanos> sibling behind
because the kernel often holds the just-renamed binary's image open
for a while after process exit, and our immediate best-effort delete
fails. Without a sweep, every Windows update grows the install
directory by one stale executable.

On the next update the helper now globs <target>.old.* and removes
whatever it can — the previous update's leftover is normally
deletable by then. Best-effort: anything still held by the kernel
gets skipped and tried again the update after.

* fix(updater): wire JS event channel + redesign default window

The updater window was rendering its initial static HTML on every
platform — JS event handlers never received state updates from Go.

Cause: the old template polled `window.wails.Events.On`, but the Wails
v3 runtime exposes Events only as an ES module export from /runtime.js.
That bundle can't be imported from an InitialHTML page either, because
`loadHTMLString:baseURL:nil` (macOS) and `NavigateToString` (Windows)
load the page with `window.location.origin === "null"` so the modern
HTTP-fetch transport fails for relative URLs. The previous "modern runtime
exposes Events on window.wails" assumption was simply wrong.

Two fixes:

1. **Page side** — replace the broken polling with a minimal shim. Install
   `window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent` ourselves to receive events (the
   framework's pre-injected `window._wails` doesn't provide it), and emit
   user actions via the existing `window._wails.invoke` postMessage
   channel. After invoke becomes available, fire `wails:runtime:ready` to
   flush the ExecJS pending-queue — without this signal every state
   event the framework dispatched during page load sat in `pendingJS`
   forever and the UI never advanced past the initial HTML.

2. **Framework side** — add a `wails:event:emit:<name>` case in
   `WebviewWindow.HandleMessage` so InitialHTML pages have a return
   channel. Bare names only (no payload) — enough for user-action
   buttons; pages that need structured data should use the full runtime.

* fix(linux): bind webkit messageHandlers.external.postMessage receiver

Direct testing of the updater window on lin-node1 (Ubuntu 26.04 GTK4 +
WebKitGTK 2.52.3) revealed every `window._wails.invoke(...)` call from
the page silently dropping on the floor. The Wails runtime Core JS was
loaded, `_wails.invoke` was a function, but no script messages ever
reached `sendMessageToBackend` on the Go side.

Cause: the historical Linux setup was a bare reference assignment

    window._wails.invoke=window.webkit.messageHandlers.external.postMessage;

When code later called `window._wails.invoke(msg)`, the `this` receiver
became the global object instead of the handler. WebKitGTK's
postMessage refuses the call without surfacing an error to JS — the
message is just lost. Darwin already wraps the call in a closure for
the same reason; Windows works either way because WebView2's
postMessage tolerates the loose receiver. Match darwin's pattern.

Bonus: this also lifts the broken "JS event emits work" comment in the
helper-mode commit message into something true on Linux.

* feat(updater): wire Config.CheckInterval — the docs claimed it, code didn't

The Config field has shipped since the original commit with the
"Pop-up-on-found behaviour is the same as a manual Check" promise but

never consulted again. Init now starts a goroutine on a ticker when

session-setup machinery as a manual click.

downloading / verifying / installing) are dropped — concurrent state
machines aren't supported and CheckAndInstall's own lock would defer

* feat(updater): public BYOWindow constructor + WebviewWindow.AsUpdaterWindow

method that *application.WebviewWindow can't satisfy, and a
WebviewWindow's fluent Show()/Close() return types don't match
WindowHandle's bare Show()/Close() signatures either. The path was
dead code.

  (*WebviewWindow).AsUpdaterWindow() — returns the existing
                                     updaterWindowHandle adapter that

                                     signature difference.

  myWin := app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{...})
  app.Updater.Init(updater.Config{
      Window: updater.BYOWindow(myWin.AsUpdaterWindow()),
      ...,
  })

* fix: xbps InstallCommand type mismatch + two-pass symlink extraction

Two unrelated CI failures on the latest merge of master:

* internal/doctor/packagemanager/xbps.go and pkg/doctor-ng/packagemanager/xbps.go
  copied a v2-shaped expression into v3 — `pkg.InstallCommand[x.osid]`
  indexes a `string` by a `string`. The v3 Package struct made
  InstallCommand a flat string (matching the other v3 PMs); xbps just
  needs to return it directly like apt/dnf do.

* CodeQL's go/unsafe-unzip-symlink rule flagged the archive extractor
  for the classic zip-slip-via-symlink escalation: planting a symlink
  followed by a write through it (archive contains "link → /etc",
  then "link/passwd" — the write resolves the symlink and escapes
  root). The existing root-relative check on the symlink target is
  necessary but not sufficient.

  Standard mitigation: two-pass extraction. Pass 1 writes regular
  files and directories only, recording symlinks as pending. Pass 2
  creates the symlinks last. Because no symlink exists on disk
  during pass 1, no file write can be redirected through one.
  Pass-1 symlink entries are still validated up-front so a malicious
  archive is rejected before any disk work happens. Pass 2 re-runs
  the same validation as defence in depth.
